bits.comment: valdflag smooth module Count the number of successive detected speech frames,no longer count more than 6.After that , when detect no speech frames, smooth the overhead2 frames into speech frames. If less 6, smooth the overhead1 frames into speech frames

bits.name: overhead2
bits.comment: ditto

bits.name: wr_clr
bits.comment: SFIFO's write address is reset to all 0, high active

bits.name: rd_clr
bits.comment: SFIFO's read address is reset to all 0, high active

bits.name: test_ctrl_s
bits.comment: 0:test_port_s <= {1'b0,speech_stds_0 ,1'b0,speech_means_adj_0 } ;

bits.name: test_ctrl_n
bits.comment: 0: test_port_n <= {1'b0,noise_stds_0 ,1'b0,noise_means_adj_0 } ;

bits.name: test_port_s
bits.comment: {1'b0,speech_stds ,1'b0,speech_means_adj } ;

bits.name: test_port_n
bits.comment: {1'b0,noise_stds ,1'b0,noise_means_adj }

bits.name: enable
bits.comment: Enables the SIM Card IF module

bits.name: parity
bits.comment: Selects the parity generation/detection

bits.name: perf
bits.comment:
Parity Error Receive Feed-through
0 = Don't store bytes with detected parity errors
1 = Feed-through bytes with detected parity errors

bits.name: filter_disable
bits.comment:
Enable or disable NULL (0x60) character filtering when SIM card sends NULL to reset WWT timer.
0 = Enable NULL character filtering, NULL characters are not reported if not data.
1 = Disable NULL character filtering. NULL characters (0x60) are transferred to the SCI data buffer.

bits.name: clockstop
bits.comment:
Manual SCI Clock Stop control. Manually starts and stops the SCI clock. This bit must be set to '1' when Autostop mode is enabled.
0 = Enable the SCI clock
1 = Disable SCI clock

bits.name: autostop_en_h
bits.comment:
Enables automatic clock shutdown when command is complete. Enabling this will generate the necessary startup and shutdown delays required by the SIM protocol.
0 = Auto clock control not enabled. SCI clock controlled by SCI_Clockstop bit
1 = Auto clock control enabled.

bits.name: msbh_lsbl
bits.comment:
Sets the transmission and reception bit order:
0 = LSB is sent/recieved first (Direct convention)
1 = MSB is sent/received first (Inverse convention)

bits.name: lli
bits.comment:
Logic Level Invert:
0 = Logic level 0 data is sent/received as '0' or 'A' which is the same as the start bit. (Direct convention)
1 = Logic level 0 data is sent/received as '1' or 'Z' which is the opposite of the start bit. (Inverse convention)

bits.name: pegen_len
bits.comment:
Parity Error signal length. This configuration bit can be used to extend the duration of the parity error signal generation from 1 ETU to 1.5 ETU
0 = Parity Error signal duration is 1 ETU starting at 10.5 ETU
1 = Parity Error signal duration is 1.5 ETU starting at 10.5 ETU

bits.name: parity_en
bits.comment:
Enable or disable parity error checking on the receive data
0 = Disable parity error checking
1 = Enable parity error checking

bits.name: stop_level
bits.comment:
Logical value of the clock signal when SCI clock is stopped (either due to automatic shutdown or manual shutdown)
0 = Stop clock at low level
1 = Stop clock at high level

bits.name: arg_h
bits.comment: Automatic Reset Generator. Write a '1' to this bit to initiate an automatic reset procedure on the SIM. Write '0' to switch back to SCI_Reset control (bit 20). An ARG interrupt will be generated if the ARG process succeeded or failed. The ARG status bit (ARG_Det) must be read to determine if a reset response from the card was detected. This bit needs to be cleared between ARG attempts.

bits.name: afd_en_h
bits.comment:
Automatic format detection. This bit is generally set in conjunction with the ARG_H bit to enable automatic detection of the data convention.
1 = Enable TS detection and automatic convention settings programming
0 = disable automatic settings and use the register bits (MSBH_LSBL and LLI) to control the convention

bits.name: tx_resend_en_h
bits.comment:
1 = Enable automatic resend of characters when Tx parity error is detected
0 = Disable automatic resend

bits.name: reset
bits.comment:
Direct connection to the SIM card reset pin. This is overridden when ARG_H is enabled
0 = SCI_Reset low voltage
1 = SCI Reset high voltage

bits.name: dly_sel
bits.comment:
This selects between two delay times for the automatic clock stop startup and shutdown:
0 = short delay
Startup/Shutdown : 744 SCI clocks / 1860 SCI clocks
1 = long delay
Startup/Shutdown : (2 x 744) SCI clocks / (2 x 1860) SCI clocks

bits.name: in_avg_en
bits.comment:
Input data average enable.
0 = Disable
1 = Enable

bits.name: par_chk_offset
bits.comment: Allows fine control of the parity check position during the parity error time period.

bits.name: rxdata_rdy
bits.comment:
Returns the status of the Rx FIFO:
0 = Rx FIFO empty
1 = There is at least 1 character in the Rx FIFO

bits.name: tx_fifo_rdy
bits.comment:
Returns the status of the Tx FIFO:
0 = Tx FIFO is full
1 = There is at least 1 free spot in the Tx FIFO

bits.name: format_det
bits.comment:
Returns the status of the automatic format detection after reset:
0 = TS character has not been detected in the ATR
1 = TS character has been detected and SCI module is using the automatic convention settings
This bit is cleared when the AFD_En bit is cleared

bits.name: arg_det
bits.comment:
Returns the status of the automatic reset procedure:
0 = ARG detection has failed
1 = ARG detection has detected that the SIM has responded to the reset
This bit is used in conjunction with the ARG interrupt. The ARG interrupt will be generated at the successful or unsuccessful termination of the ARG process. This bit can be used to determine the success or failure.

bits.name: reset_det
bits.comment: This is the status of the Reset pin when automatic reset generation is enabled. This bit can be used to discover whether the SIM card that has successfully responded to an ARG procedure has an active high or active low reset. (Det means 'Detection')

bits.name: clk_rdy_h
bits.comment:
Status of the control signal to the clock control module. This bit respects the startup and shutdown phases, so during these times, the clock may actually be on, but it is not considered to be 'ready'
0 = SCI clock may be on or off but is not ready for use
1 = SCI clock is on and ready for use

bits.name: clk_off
bits.comment:
Status bit of the Sci clock.
0 = Sci clock is ON
1 = Sci clock is OFF

bits.name: rx_err
bits.comment: A receive parity error was detected. Reading this register clears the bit.

bits.name: tx_err
bits.comment: A transmit parity error was detected. Reading this register clears the bit.

bits.name: rxoverflow
bits.comment: The internal receive FIFO has reached an overflow condition. Reading this register clears the bit.

bits.name: txoverflow
bits.comment: The internal transmit FIFO has reached an overflow condition. Reading this register clears the bit.

bits.name: autostop_state
bits.comment: Returns the state of the clock management state machine when AutoStop mode is enabled. This value is '00' when manual mode is selected.

option.name: Startup_phase
option.comment: Clock is on, but not ready to be used.

option.name: Auto_on
option.comment: Clock is on and ready to be used

option.name: Shutdown_phase
option.comment: Clock is still on, but should not be used.

bits.name: data_in
bits.comment: Writing to this register will send the data to the SIM card. If automatic clock shutdown is enabled, the appropriate delay will be applied before the data is actually sent.

bits.name: data_out
bits.comment: Reading this register will read from the receive data FIFO.

bits.name: clkdiv
bits.comment: Clock divider for generating the baud clock from the SCI clock. This value must match the value used by the SIM card whose default value is 0x174.

bits.name: baud_x8_en
bits.comment:
Speed mode enable.
0 = Low speed mode
1 = High speed mode(372/32, 372/64, 512/64)

bits.name: rx_clk_cnt_limit
bits.comment: Rx_clk_cnt wrap value.

bits.name: clkdiv_16
bits.comment: Secondary clock divider for generating 16x baud clock.

bits.name: maindiv
bits.comment:
Main clock divider to generate the SCI clock. This value should be calculated as follows:
MainDiv = Clk_Sys/(2xSCI_Clk) - 1
where SCI_Clk is in the range of 3-5 MHz as specified in the SIM specification.

bits.name: clk_out_inv
bits.comment:
Inverts the polarity of the SCI clock to the SIM card only.
0 = No inversion
1 = Invert external SCI clock

bits.name: clk_inv
bits.comment:
Inverts the polarity of the SCI clock to the SIM card and internal.
0 = No inversion
1 = Invert external SCI clock

bits.name: rxcnt
bits.comment: This value should be programmed with the number of expected characters to receive. It will be decremented each time a character is actually received and should be 0 when the transfer is complete. If a character is sent after the RxCnt reaches zero, the extra character flag will be set but this value will stay at zero.

bits.name: clk_persist
bits.comment:
When in automatic clock shutdown mode, this bit can prevent the clock from entering shutdown mode when the transfer is complete. This should be used for multi-transfer commands where the clock must not be shut down until the command is complete. This bit must be programmed for each transfer.
1 = Keep clock on
0 = Allow clock shutdown when transfer is complete

bits.name: chguard
bits.comment: This is the extra guard time that can be added to the 2 ETU minimum (and default) guard time between successive transmitted characters. This should be programmed depending on the SIM's ATR. The total ETU guard time will be ChGuard + 1.

bits.name: turnaroundguard
bits.comment:
Turnaround guard time configuration. This value can be used to adjust the delay between the leading edge of a received character and the leading edge of the next transmitted character. The minimum time specified in the SIM recommendation is 16 ETU. The number of ETUs can be calculated using the following formula:
Total Turnaround Time (in ETUs) = 11 + TurnaroundGuard

bits.name: wi
bits.comment:
Work Waiting Time factor. A timeout will be generated when the WWT is exceeded. The WWT is calculated by:
WWT = 960 x WI x (F/Fi)
where Fi is the main SCI clock frequency (3-5 MHz) and F is 372 before an enhanced PPS and 512 after an enhanced PPS.
The SCI_WI value must be calculated as follows:
SCI_WI = WI * D
Thus, by default (WI = 10) this value needs to be set to 10 before an EPPS, but needs to be scaled to WI*D=80 after the EPPS procedure.

bits.name: tx_pert
bits.comment: Number of times to try resending character when the SIM indicates a parity error.

bits.name: ch_filt
bits.comment: Value of the character to be filtered. 0x60 is the NULL character in the SIM protocol. If character filtering is enabled, the first 0x60 character that is received by the SIM during a transfer will not be recorded. The purpose of this character is to enable the SIM to reset the WWT counter when the SIM is not ready to send the data. This filter has no effect on characters within the datastream.

reg.name: dbg

bits.name: fifo_rx_clr
bits.comment: Clear RX FIFO.

bits.name: fifo_tx_clr
bits.comment: Clear TX FIFO.

reg.comment: clear RX/TX FIFO

reg.name: int_cause

bits.name: rx_done
bits.comment: Number of expected Rx characters, as programmed in the RxCnt register, has been received.

bits.name: rx_half
bits.comment: Receiver FIFO is half full.

bits.name: wwt_timeout
bits.comment: No Tx character has been sent NOR any Rx character detected within the WWT timeout.

bits.name: extra_rx
bits.comment: An extra character has been received after the number of characters in RxCnt has been received.

bits.name: resend_ovfl
bits.comment: The automatic re-transmit of parity error characters has exceeded the threshold specified in the Tx_PERT field.

bits.name: arg_end
bits.comment: End of the ARG sequence. The status register must be read to determine whether the ARG sequence was successful or not.

bits.name: sci_dma_tx_done
bits.comment: DMA tx done.

bits.name: sci_dma_rx_done
bits.comment: DMA rx done.

reg.comment: This register is a READ ONLY register that returns the logical and of the SCI_INT_STATUS register and the SCI_INT_MASK. If any of these bits is '1', the SCI module will generate an interrupt. Bits 21:16 return the status of the interrupt which is the interrupt state before the mask is applied. These bits should only be used for debugging.

reg.name: int_clr

bits.name: rx_done
bits.comment: Number of expected Rx characters, as programmed in the SCI_RxCnt register, has been received.

bits.name: rx_half
bits.comment: Receiver FIFO is half full.

bits.name: wwt_timeout
bits.comment: No Tx character has been sent NOR any Rx character detected within the WWT timeout.

bits.name: extra_rx
bits.comment: An extra character has been received after the number of characters in SCI_RxCnt has been received.

bits.name: resend_ovfl
bits.comment: The automatic re-transmit of parity error characters has exceeded the threshold specified in the SCI_Tx_PERT field.

bits.name: arg_end
bits.comment: End of the ARG sequence. The status register must be read to determine whether the ARG sequence was successful or not.

bits.name: sci_dma_tx_done
bits.comment: DMA tx done.

bits.name: sci_dma_rx_done
bits.comment: DMA rx done.

reg.comment: This is a WRITE ONLY register that is used to clear an SCI interrupt. Write a '1' to the interrupt that is to be cleared. Writing '0' has no effect.

bits.comment: Number of expected Rx characters, as programmed in the SCI_RxCnt register, has been received.

bits.comment: Receiver FIFO is half full.

bits.name: wwt_timeout
bits.comment: No Tx character has been sent NOR any Rx character detected within the WWT timeout.

bits.comment: An extra character has been received after the number of characters in SCI_RxCnt has been received.

reg.comment: This register is READ/WRITE register that enables the desired interrupt. A '1' in a bit position indicates that the corresponding interrupt is enabled and if the interrupt occurs, the SCI will generate a hardware interrupt.

bits.name: lps_sf_enable
bits.comment:
Lps Skip Frame Enable.
When enabled the frame interrupt are masked until the programmed number of frames are elapsed.
This is done by masking the frame interrupt line from the regular TCU counter, and counting the frames. Also when activating the LowPower SkipFrame the frame counter is tranfered to the low power counter that will update it based on the 32kHz Clock.

bits.name: lps_sf_lowpower
bits.comment: Controls the Lps Low Power Counters (counters at 32kHz) usage.

option.name: SkipFrame
option.comment: The Low Power Counters are started in Skip Frame Mode. In this mode the Low Power Counter are used to maintain the Time base, The Skip Frame Must be enabled as this is the Low Power extention of the Skip Frame feature.

option.name: Calib
option.comment: Start the calibration. The Low Power Counters are used to Calibrate the 32kHz clock against the System Clock, The Calibration is required to compensate from temperature variation. Note that the Skip Frame can also be enabled during calibration (but not with low power).

bits.name: lps_sf_wakeup0
bits.comment: Enable fake Fint used with wakeupNumber=0.

bits.name: lps_sf_wakeup0_cfg
bits.comment:
Enable fake Fint when sys_sf_frame_count>=cfg_sf_frame.
Default sys_sf_frame_count>cfg_sf_frame.

bits.name: lps_sf_ready
bits.comment:
Lps Skip Frame Ready, status of the state machines to keep valid state between system clock and 32Khz clock.
Must read as '1' before entering Low Power Skip Frame or Calibration mode.

bits.name: lps_sf_slowrunning
bits.comment:
'1' when Lps Skip Frame Low Power Counters are Running.
When entering Low Power Skip Frame, the counters are not immediately started, they wait for the nextFrame interrupt. Reading this status allow to know if the counters are running, and the System Clock can be safely disabled.

bits.name: lps_sf_calibrationdone
bits.comment: '1' when the Lps Skip Frame Calibration is Done.

bits.name: lps_sf_pu_reached
bits.comment: '1' when the Lps Skip Frame Power-up sequence frame is reached.

bits.name: lps_sf_tcu_restart
bits.comment: '1' when tcu counter is restarted.

bits.name: lps_sf_frame
bits.comment:
Number of frames to Skip.
If the power up sequence is enabled, frames are skipped until both this number is reached and the powerup sequence has finished.
Note: The power up sequence must be Done before the the frame LPS_SF_Frame ends.

bits.name: lps_sf_pu_frame
bits.comment: Number of frames before activating the Power-up sequence.

bits.name: lps_sf_restart_time
bits.comment:
For LowPower SkipFrame mode: Value to restart TCU (and frame interrupt generation) on the system clock counter after a low power phase.
For Calibration mode: number of 32k cycles for the calibration.

bits.name: lps_sf_frame_period
bits.comment: Value of the frame period in system clock count.

reg.name: lps_sf_rate
reg.comment: The rate is the number of System Clocks per 32kHz Clocks.

bits.name: lps_sf_rate_int
bits.comment: Integer part of the rate.

bits.name: lps_sf_rate_frac
bits.comment: Fractional part of the rate.

bits.name: lps_sf_elapsed_frames
bits.comment:
Current number of elapsed frames.
Valid when Skip Frame is Enabled.

bits.name: lps_sf_sys_count
bits.comment:
Value of the system clock counter at the end of calibration (when CalibrationDone is '1' in LPS_SF_Status register).
The hardware behind it is reused during other operation, reading that register at any other time will return an undefined value.

bits.name: lps_irq_calibration_done_cause
bits.comment:
1 when the IRQ was triggered because the calibration is done.
Write 1 in cause or status bit to clear.

bits.name: lps_irq_slow_running_cause
bits.comment:
1 when the IRQ was triggered because the Slow Counter started.
Write 1 in cause or status bit to clear.

bits.name: lps_irq_pu_reached_cause
bits.comment:
1 when the IRQ was triggered because the Power-Up frame was reached.
Write 1 in cause or status bit to clear.

bits.name: lps_irq_tcu_restart_cause
bits.comment:
1 when the IRQ was triggered because the tcu counter was restarted.
Write 1 in cause or status bit to clear.

bits.name: lps_irq_calibration_done_status
bits.comment:
1 when the calibration is done.
Write 1 in cause or status bit to clear.

bits.name: lps_irq_slow_running_status
bits.comment:
1 when the Slow Counter started.
Write 1 in cause or status bit to clear.

bits.name: lps_irq_pu_reached_status
bits.comment:
1 when the Power-Up frame was reached.
Write 1 in cause or status bit to clear.

bits.name: lps_irq_tcu_restart_status
bits.comment:
1 when the tcu counter was restarted.
Write 1 in cause or status bit to clear.

bits.name: lps_irq_calibration_done_mask
bits.comment: when 1 the LPS_IRQ_Calibration_Done is enabled.

bits.name: lps_irq_slow_running_mask
bits.comment: when 1 the LPS_IRQ_Slow_Running is enabled.

bits.name: lps_irq_pu_reached_mask
bits.comment: when 1 the LPS_IRQ_PU_Reached is enabled.

bits.name: lps_irq_tcu_restart_mask
bits.comment: when 1 the LPS_IRQ_TCU_Restart is enabled.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment: Enable the module and activate the chip select selected by CS_sel field.

bits.name: cs_sel
bits.comment: Selects the active CS.

bits.name: input_mode
bits.comment:
When set to 1 the inputs are activated, else only the output is driven and no data are stored in the receive FIFO.
Notes: The Input_mode bit status is also readable onto the bit rxtx_buffer[31].

bits.name: clock_polarity
bits.comment:
The spi clock polarity
when '0' the clock disabled level is low, and the first edge is a rising edge.
When '1' the clock disabled level is high, and the first edge is a falling edge.

bits.name: clock_delay
bits.comment: Transfer start to first edge delay value from 0 to 2 is the number of spi clock half period between the CS activation and the first clock edge.

bits.name: do_delay
bits.comment: Transfer start to first data out delay value from 0 to 2 is the number of spi clock half period between the CS activation and the first data out

bits.name: di_delay
bits.comment:
Transfer start to first data in sample delay value from 0 to 3 is the number of spi clock half period between the CS activation and the first data in sampled.
NOTE: DI_Delay must be less or equal to DO_Delay + CS_Delay + 2.
In other words DI_Delay can be 3 only if DO_Delay and CS_Delay are not both equal to 0.

bits.name: cs_delay
bits.comment: Transfer end to chip select deactivation delay value from 0 to 3 is the number of spi clock half period between the end of transfer and CS deactivation

bits.name: cs_pulse
bits.comment: Chip select deactivation to reactivation minimum delay value from 0 to 3 is the number of spi clock half period between the CS deactivation and a new CS activation (CS will activate only if more data are available in the transmit FIFO)

bits.name: frame_size
bits.comment:
Frame Size
The frame size is the binary value of this register + 1 valid value are 3 to 31 (frame size 4 to 32bits)

bits.name: oe_delay
bits.comment:
OE delay
When 0: regular mode, SPI_DO pin as output only.
Value from 1 to 31 is the number of data out to transfert before the SPI_DO pin switch to input.

bits.name: ctrl_data_mux_sel
bits.comment:
Selects the active CS and Input_reg either from the ctrl or rxtx_buffer register.
If SPI FIFO 8b or 32b, when set to "0": CS from CS_sel and INPUT from Input_mode in the register ctrl.
Only if SPI FIFO 32b, when set to "1": CS and INPUT from SPI DATA.(Do not work for FIFO8b)

bits.name: input_sel
bits.comment:
Selects the input line to be used as SPI data in.(Not used for SPI3)
when "00" the SPI_DI_0 is used.
When "01" the SPI_DI_1 is used.
When "10" the SPI_DI_2 is used.
When "11" reserved.

bits.name: active_status
bits.comment: '1' when a transfer is in progress.

bits.name: cause_rx_ovf_irq
bits.comment:
The receive FIFO overflow irq cause.
Writing a '1' clear the receive overflow status and cause.

bits.name: cause_tx_th_irq
bits.comment: The transmit FIFO threshold irq cause.

bits.name: cause_tx_dma_irq
bits.comment:
The transmit Dma Done irq cause.
Writing a '1' clear the transmit Dma Done status and cause.

bits.name: cause_rx_th_irq
bits.comment: The receive FIFO threshold irq cause.

bits.name: cause_rx_dma_irq
bits.comment:
The receive Dma Done irq cause.
Writing a '1' clear the receive Dma Done status and cause.

bits.name: tx_ovf
bits.comment:
The transmit FIFO overflow status.
Writing a '1' clear the transmit overflow status and cause.

bits.name: rx_udf
bits.comment:
The receive FIFO underflow status.
Writing a '1' clear the receive underflow status and cause.

bits.name: rx_ovf
bits.comment:
The receive FIFO overflow status.
Writing a '1' clear the receive overflow status and cause.

bits.name: tx_th
bits.comment: The transmit FIFO threshold status.

bits.name: tx_dma_done
bits.comment:
The transmit Dma Done status.
Writing a '1' clear the transmit Dma Done status and cause.

bits.name: rx_th
bits.comment: The receive FIFO threshold status.

bits.name: rx_dma_done
bits.comment:
The receive Dma Done status.
Writing a '1' clear the receive Dma Done status and cause.

bits.name: tx_space
bits.comment:
Transmit FIFO Space
Number of empty spot in the FIFO

bits.name: rx_level
bits.comment:
Receive FIFO level
Number of DATA in the FIFO

bits.name: fifo_flush
bits.comment: Writing '1' flush both FIFO, don't do it when SPI is active (transfer in progress)

reg.name: rxtx_buffer
reg.comment:
Spi1 fifo size (rxtx_buffer): 8bits.
Spi2 fifo size (rxtx_buffer): 8bits.
Spi3 fifo size (rxtx_buffer): 32bits.

bits.name: data_in_out
bits.comment: Write to the transmit FIFO Read in the receive FIFO.

bits.name: cs
bits.comment: Chip Select on which write the data written in the Fifo. Data in bit [30:29] Data out bit [30:29]

bits.name: read_ena
bits.comment: Set this bit to one when the data received while sending this peculiar data are expected to be kept in the FIFO, otherwise no data is recorded in the FIFO. Data in bit [31] Data out bit [31]

bits.name: cs_polarity
bits.comment: Chip select polarity

bits.name: clock_divider
bits.comment:
Clock Divider
The state machine clock is generated by dividing the system clock by the value of this register + 1.
So the output clock is divided by (register + 1)*2

bits.name: clock_limiter
bits.comment:
When enabled the clock input to the divider is not the system clock, but a limited version of it: It cannot be above 52MHz, so the output clock will never be above 26MHz.
for system clock of 104Mhz the clock input to the divider is 52Mhz, for system clock of 78Mhz the clock input to the divider is 39Mhz, for lower system clock value, the input to the divider is the system clock.

bits.name: pattern
bits.comment: MMC Pattern value for RX pattern match mode.

bits.name: pattern_mode
bits.comment: Enable the pattern mode.

bits.name: pattern_selector
bits.comment: Select the RX pattern matching mode when the pattern_mode is enabled( set 1). Used for SD/MMC SPI mode.

option.name: UNTIL
option.comment: No datas are written into the RX FIFO UNTIL the received data is equal to the pattern.

option.name: WHILE
option.comment: No datas are written into the RX FIFO WHILE the received data is equal to the pattern.

bits.name: tx_stream_bit
bits.comment: When TX stream mode is enabled, once the TX fifo is empty, all new bits send have the value of this bit.

bits.name: tx_stream_mode
bits.comment:
Enable the TX stream mode. Used for SD/MMC SPI mode.
When enabled, this mode provide infinite bit stream for sending, after fifo is empty the extra bits generated all have the same value. The value is in tx_stream_bit.

bits.name: tx_stream_stop_with_rx_dma_done
bits.comment: Allow to automatically clear the tx_stream_mode when Rx_Dma_Done is set.

option.name: Spi Ctrl
option.comment: The Spi_Clk pin is set OUTPUT(Basic SPI Behaviour).

option.name: Input Ctrl
option.comment: The Spi_Clk pin is set INPUT (High Impedance).

option.name: Force 0 Ctrl
option.comment: The Spi_Clk pin is set OUTPUT and forced to 0.

option.name: Force 1 Ctrl
option.comment: The Spi_Clk pin is set OUTPUT and forced to 1.

option.name: Spi Ctrl
option.comment: The Spi_DO pin is set OUTPUT(Basic SPI Behaviour).

option.name: Input Ctrl
option.comment: The Spi_DO pin is set INPUT (High Impedance).

option.name: Force 0 Ctrl
option.comment: The Spi_DO pin is set OUTPUT and forced to 0.

option.name: Force 1 Ctrl
option.comment: The Spi_DO pin is set OUTPUT and forced to 1.

option.name: Spi Ctrl
option.comment: The Spi_CSO pin is set OUTPUT(Basic SPI Behaviour).

option.name: Input Ctrl
option.comment: The Spi_CSO pin is set INPUT (High Impedance).

option.name: Force 0 Ctrl

bits.name: scratch
bits.comment:
[7:0] Write 0x89 to the register to release automatically for related clock gate enable in sysctrl datapath
[15:8] Write 0x89 to the register to release automatically for related soft reset in sysctrl datapath

bits.name: write unlock status
bits.comment:
Is set to 1 when a write attempt has been done on a protected register
Can be reset by writing 0xa50000 or 0xa50001 to the debug register (With the LSB at 1 to unlock the protected registers, with the LSB at 0 to lock them)

bits.name: write unlock
bits.comment:
When this bit is set to 1, the protected registers are accessible
When this bit is set to 0, the protected registers can not be written
Write 0xa50000 to the debug register to set this bit to 0
Write 0xa50001 to the debug register to set this bit to 1

reg.name: pll_ctrl
reg.comment: Register protected by Write_Unlocked_H.

bits.name: pll_enable
bits.comment: Mode of the Pll. This register is set to enable by the LPS_start_ExtPll_pulse_H.

bits.name: pll_lock_reset
bits.comment: Used to reset the PLL Lock Detector.

option.name: Pass
option.comment: In this mode the output of the PLL is its input clock divided by the proper dividers

option.name: Bypass
option.comment: In this mode the output of the PLL is its input clock

bits.name: pll_clk_fast_enable
bits.comment: Enables the Fast Clock from the ExtPll (Clock Gate Reg Resync).

reg.name: sel_clock
reg.comment: This register is protected.

bits.name: slow_sel_rf
bits.comment: PreSelects between RF clock(26mhz) and Oscillator clock(32k) for Clock Slow

bits.name: sys_sel_fast
bits.comment: Selects between the Slow clock and the Fast Clock (APll clock) and Selects between the Slow clock and the APcpu Clock

bits.name: osc_32k_26m_div32k_sel
bits.comment:
When 0, select 26m div32k.
When 1, select osc 32k.

bits.name: pll_disable_lps
bits.comment: Disable PLL when LPS power up.

option.name: Ok
option.comment: When 1, the clock from the XCver is detected.

option.name: No
option.comment: When 0, the clock from the XCver is not detected.

bits.name: rf_detect_bypass
bits.comment:
If RF_Detect_Bypass = 0, RF clock is selected when she is detected.
If RF_Detect_Bypass = 1, RF clock is selected even she is not detected.

bits.name: rf_detect_reset
bits.comment:
When 1, The RF clock detection counter is force reseted.
When 0, The RF clock detection counter is enabled.

bits.name: rf_selected_l
bits.comment: 0 when RF clock is effectively selected for Slow Clock. RF clock selection is not done until the clock has been detected.

bits.name: fast_selected_l
bits.comment: 0 when Fast clock is effectively selected. Fast clock selection is not done until the PLL has locked.

bits.name: soft_sel_spiflash
bits.comment:
When 1, clk_spiflash is clk_slow.
When 0, switch from clk_slow to clk_spiflash

bits.name: soft_sel_mem_bridge
bits.comment:
When 1, clk_mem_bridge is clk_slow.
When 0, switch from clk_slow to clk_pll_mem_bridge

bits.name: bblte_clk_pll_sel
bits.comment:
When 1, clk_bblte is inverted.
When 0, clk_bblte is itself, pole select

bits.name: camera_clk_pll_sel
bits.comment:
When 1, clk_pix is clk_slow.
When 0, switch from clk_slow to clk_pll_pix_div_out

bits.name: usb_pll_locked_h
bits.comment:
When 1, usb clock pll locked.
When 0, usb clock pll not locked.

bits.name: bb26m_sel
bits.comment:
When 1, select i_osc_26m.
When 0, select i_bb_26m(default).

bits.name: soft_sel_spiflash1
bits.comment:
When 1, clk_spiflash is clk_slow.
When 0, switch from clk_slow to clk_spiflash

bits.name: apll_locked_h
bits.comment:
When 1, apll locked
When 0, apll not locked

bits.name: mempll_locked_h
bits.comment:
When 1, mempll locked
When 0, mempll not locked

bits.name: audiopll_locked_h
bits.comment:
When 1, audiopll locked
When 0, audiopll not locked

bits.name: bbpll2_locked_h
bits.comment:
When 1, bbpll2 locked
When 0, bbpll2 not locked

bits.name: bbpll1_locked_h
bits.comment:
When 1, bbpll1 locked
When 0, bbpll1 not locked

bits.name: usbpll_locked_h
bits.comment:
When 1, usbpll locked
When 0, usbpll not locked

bits.name: boot_mode
bits.comment:
This contains the state of boot mode pins latched during Reset.
bit 16: Force download.
bit 17: Mass production.
bit 18: Secure boot 1-> secure boot, 0-> nonsecure boot.
bit 19: Unused.
bit 20: Unused.
bit 21: Unused.
see BootSequence for details.
This register is not reseted by a software or host reset.

bits.name: sw_boot_mode
bits.comment:

This register is not reseted by a software or host reset.

bits.name: fonctional_test_mode
bits.comment: When 1 the chip has booted in fonctional test mode (for chip production tests).

bits.name: ch_to_use
bits.comment:
This field indicates which standard channel to use.
Before using a channel, the CPU read this register to know which channel must be used. After reading this registers, the channel is to be regarded as busy.
After reading this register, if the CPU doesn't want to use the specified channel, the CPU must write a disable in the control register of the channel to release the channel.
0000 = use Channel0
0001 = use Channel1
0010 = use Channel2
...
0111 = use Channel7
1111 = all channels are busy

bits.name: ch_enable
bits.comment:
This register indicates which channel is enabled. It is a copy of the enable bit of the control register of each channel. One bit per channel, for example:
0000_0000 = All channels disabled
0000_0001 = Ch0 enabled
0000_0010 = Ch1 enabled
0000_0100 = Ch2 enabled
0000_0101 = Ch0 and Ch2 enabled
0000_0111 = Ch0, Ch1 and Ch2 enabled
1111_1111 = all channels enabled

bits.name: ch_busy
bits.comment: This register indicates which standard channel is busy (this field doesn't include the RF_SPI channel). A standard channel is mark as busy, when a channel is enabled or a previous reading of the GET_CH register, the field CH_TO_USE indicates this channel. One bit per channel

bits.name: enable
bits.comment:
Channel Enable, write one in this bit enable the channel.
When the channel is enabled, for a peripheral to memory transfer the DMA wait request from peripheral to start transfer.

bits.name: disable
bits.comment:
Channel Disable, write one in this bit disable the channel.
When writing one in this bit, the current AHB transfer and current APB transfer (if one in progress) is completed and the channel is then disabled.

struct.name: ch
struct.comment:
The Channel 0 conveys data from the AIF to the memory.
The Channel 1 conveys data from the memory to the AIF.
These Channels only exist with Voice Option.

bits.name: enable

When the channel is enabled, for a peripheral to memory transfer the DMA wait request from peripheral to start transfer.

bits.name: disable

Channel Disable, write one in this bit disable the channel.
When writing one in this bit, the current AHB transfer and current APB transfer (if one in progress) is completed and the channel is then disabled.

Channel Disable, write one in this bit disable the channel.
When writing one in this bit, the current AHB transfer and current APB transfer (if one in progress) is completed and the channel is then disabled.

bits.name: rd_hw_exch
wr_hw_exch
autodisable
bits.comment:
Set Auto-disable mode
0 = when TC reach zero the channel is not automatically released.
1 = At the end of the transfer when TC reach zero the channel is automatically disabled. the current channel is released.

bits.name: size
bits.comment:
Peripheral Size
0= 8-bit peripheral
1= 32-bit peripheral

bits.name: req_src
bits.comment: Select DMA Request source

bits.name: flush
bits.comment:
When one, flush the internal FIFO channel.
This bit must be used only in case of Rx transfer. Until this bit is 1, the APB request is masked. The flush doesn't release the channel.
Before writting back this bit to zero the internal fifo must empty.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment: Enable bit, when '1' the channel is running

bits.name: fifo_empty
bits.comment: The internal channel fifo is empty

bits.name: start_addr
bits.comment:
AHB Address. This field represent the start address of the transfer.
For a 32-bit peripheral, this address must be aligned 32-bit.

bits.name: tc
bits.comment:
Transfer Count, this field indicated the transfer size in bytes to perform.
During a transfer a write in this register add the new value to the current TC.
A read of this register return the current current transfer count.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment:
Channel Enable, write one in this bit enable the channel.
This channel works only in fifo mode.

bits.name: disable
bits.comment: Channel Disable, write one in this bit to disable the channel.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment: Enable bit, when '1' the channel is running

bits.name: fifo_empty
bits.comment: The internal channel fifo is empty

bits.name: fifo_level
bits.comment: Internal fifo level

bits.name: start_ahb_addr
bits.comment:
AHB Start Address.
This field represent the start address of the fifo. The start address must 32-bit aligned.

bits.name: end_ahb_addr
bits.comment:
AHB End Address.
This field represent the last address of the fifo (it is the first address not used in the fifo).
The end address must 32-bit aligned.

bits.name: tc
bits.comment:
Transfer Count, transfer size in bytes.
This bit indicated the transfer size in bytes to perform. Up to 16kbytes per transfer.
During a transfer a write in this register add the new value to the current TC. A read of this register return the current current transfer count.

bits.name: loadval
bits.comment: Value loaded to OS timer.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment:
Write '1' to this bit will enable OS timer.
When read, the value is what we have written to this bit, it changes immediately after been written.

bits.name: enabled
bits.comment:
Read this bit will get the information if OS timer is really enabled or not. This bit will change only after the next front of 16 KHz system clock.
'1' indicates OS timer enabled.
'0' indicates OS timer not enabled.

bits.name: cleared
bits.comment:
Read this bit will get the information if OS timer interruption clear operation is finished or not.
'1' indicates OS timer interruption clear operation is on going.
'0' indicates no OS timer interruption clear operation is on going.

bits.name: repeat
bits.comment:
Write '1' to this bit will set OS timer to repeat mode.
When read, get the information if OS timer is in repeat mode.
'1' indicates OS timer in repeat mode.
'0' indicates OS timer not in repeat mode.

bits.name: wrap
bits.comment:
Write '1' to this bit will set OS timer to wrap mode.
When read, get the information if OS timer is in wrap mode.
'1' indicates OS timer in wrap mode.
'0' indicates OS timer not in wrap mode.

bits.name: load
bits.comment: Write '1' to this bit will load the initial value to OS timer.

bits.name: curval
bits.comment: Current value of OS timer. The value is 24 bits and the first 8 bits are sign extension of the most important bit. A negative value indicates that the timer has wraped.

bits.name: start
bits.comment: Write '1' to this bit will enable watchdog timer and Load it with WDTimer_LoadVal.

bits.name: stop
bits.comment: Write '1' to this bit will stop watchdog timer.

bits.name: reload
bits.comment:
Write '1' to this bit will load WDTimer_LoadVal value to watchdog timer.
Use this bit to implement the watchog keep alive.

bits.name: wdenabled
bits.comment:
Read this bit will get the information if watchdog timer is really enabled or not. This bit will change only after the next front of 32 KHz system clock.
'1' indicates watchdog timer is enabled, if current watchdog timer value reaches 0, the system will be reseted.
'0' indicates watchdog timer is not enabled.

bits.name: wdloadval
bits.comment: Load value of watchdog timer. Number of 32kHz Clock before Reset.

bits.name: interval_en
bits.comment:
This bit enables interval IRQ mode.
'0': hw delay timer does not generate interval IRQ.
'1': hw delay timer generate an IRQ each interval.

bits.name: interval
bits.comment:
interval of generating an HwTimer IRQ.
"00": interval of 1/8 second.
"01": interval of 1/4 second.
"10": interval of 1/2 second.
"11": interval of 1 second.

bits.name: curval
bits.comment: Current value of the hardware delay timer. The value is incremented every 61 us. This timer is running all the time and wrap at value 0xFFFFFFFF.

bits.comment: baud rate divider coeffcient,baud rate formula is: BAUD RATE = Fclk/(Nx(BAUD_DIV+1)) default baud rate is 921.6K, N=4, Ffun=26MHz.

bits.comment: 1: enable software flow XON interrupt 0: disable software flow XON interrupt

bits.name: at_div_mode

bits.name: at_parity_en

bits.name: rx_trig
bits.comment: RX FIFO trigger settings 00000000: don't trigger 00000001: 1 byte trigger 00000010: 2 bytes trigger 00000011: 3 bytes trigger 00000100: 4 bytes trigger ...... 01111111: 127bytes trigger 10000000: 128bytes trigger

bits.name: tx_trig
bits.comment: TX FIFO trigger setting 00000000: 0 byte trigger 00000001: 1 byte trigger 00000010: 2 bytes trigger 00000011: 3 bytes trigger 00000100: 4 bytes trigger ...... 01111110: 126bytes trigger 01111111: 127bytes trigger 10000000: don't trigger

bits.name: toutcnt

bits.name: cts

bits.name: st_error

bits.name: p_error

bits.name: tx_int
bits.comment: bit type is changed from rw1c to rc. TX data interrupt status bit 1: TX_FIFO_CNT TX_TRIG 0: TX_FIFO_CNT >TX_TRIG

bits.name: rx_fifo_cnt
bits.comment: RX FIFO data number 00000000: RX FIFO has 0 data 00000001: RX FIFO has 1 data ...... 01111111: RX FIFO has 127 data 10000000: RX FIFO has 128 data

bits.name: tx_fifo_cnt
bits.comment: TX FIFO data number 00000000: TX FIFO has 0 data 00000001: TX FIFO has 1 data ...... 01111111: TX FIFO has 127 data 10000000: TX FIFO has 128 data

bits.name: hdlc_rxfifo_cnt
bits.comment: enable HDLC, the number of RX FIFO data when received at the end of frames(include the end of frames) 00000000: RX FIFO has 0 data 00000001: RX FIFO has 1 data ...... 01111111: RX FIFO has 127 data 10000000: RX FIFO has 128 data Note: UART_RXFIFO_HDLC only read.Uart automatically updates the register value, after receiving the end of frames "7e".

bits.name: character_status

bits.name: auto_baud_locked
bits.comment: 1: Automatic detection complete,lock baud rate 0: automatic detection is not completed

bits.name: character_miscompare
bits.comment: 1: automatic detection failed, no matching bytes detected 0: automatic detection of matching bytes
