bits.name: enable_timestamping
bits.comment: Set to 1 to enable timestamping. On an ETM reset this bit is 0.

bits.name: core_select
bits.comment: If an ETM is shared between multiple cores, selects which core to trace. For the maximum value permitted, see bits [14:12] of the System Configuration Register. See the Embedded Trace Macrocell Architecture Specification for more information. To guarantee that the ETM is correctly synchronized to the new core, you must update these bits as follows: 1:Set bit [10], ETM programming, and bit [0], ETM power down, to 1. 2:Change the core select bits. 3:Clear bit [0], ETM power down, to 0. 4:Perform other programming required as normal. On an ETM reset this field is zero.

bits.name: instr_res_access_ctrl
bits.comment: Instrumentation resources access control, ETM-A5 does not implement any instrumentation resources and therefore this bit is RAZ.

bits.name: dis_sw_wr
bits.comment: Disable software writes. ETM-A5 does not support this feature and therefore this bit is RAZ.

bits.name: dis_reg_wr_from_debugger
bits.comment: Disable register writes from the debugger. ETM-A5 does not support this feature and therefore this bit is RAZ.

bits.name: port_size_3
bits.comment: Port size[3].Use this bit in conjunction with bits [6:4].On an ETM reset this bit is 0, corresponding to the 32-bit port size.

bits.name: data_only_mode
bits.comment: 0:Instruction trace enabled. 1:Instruction trace disabled. Data-only tracing is possible in this mode. On an ETM reset this bit is 0.

bits.name: filter_cprt
bits.comment: Use this bit in conjunction with bit [1], the MonitorCPRT bit. For details see Filter Coprocessor Register Transfers (CPRT) in ETMv3.0 and later in the Embedded Trace Macrocell Architecture Specification.

bits.name: suppressdata
bits.comment: Use this bit with bit [7] to suppress data. For details see Data suppression in the Embedded Trace Macrocell Architecture Specification.On an ETM reset this bit is 0.

bits.name: port_mode_1_0
bits.comment: These bits are used, in conjunction with bit [13], to set the trace port clocking mode. ETM-A5 supports only dynamic mode, corresponding to the value b000, but you can write other values to these bits, and a read of the register returns the value written. Writing another value to these bits has no effect on the ETM. Bit [11] of the System Configuration Register indicates if these bits are set to select a supported clocking mode.On an ETM reset these bits are zero.

bits.name: contextidsize
bits.comment: b00 No Context ID tracing. b01 Context ID bits [7:0] traced. b10 Context ID bits [15:0] b11 Context ID bits [31:0] traced. Note Only the number of bytes specified is traced even if the new value is larger than this.On an ETM reset this field is zero.

bits.name: port_mode_2
bits.comment: See the description of bits [17:16].On an ETM reset this bit is 0.

bits.name: cycle-accuratetracing
bits.comment: Set this bit to 1 if you want the trace to include a precise cycle count of executed instructions. This is achieved by adding extra information into the trace, giving cycle counts even when TraceEnable is inactive.On an ETM reset this bit is 0.

bits.name: etm_port_sel
bits.comment: This bit controls an external output, ETMEN. The possible values are: 0 ETMEN is LOW. 1 ETMEN is HIGH. You can use the ETMEN signal to control the routing of trace port signals to shared GPIO pins on your SoC, under the control of logic external to the ETM.Trace software tools must set this bit to 1 to ensure that trace output is enabled from this ETM.

bits.name: etm_programming
bits.comment: When set to 1, the ETM is being programmed. For more information, see ETM Programming bit and associated state in the Embedded Trace Macrocell Architecture Specification.

bits.name: debugrequestcontrol
bits.comment: If you set this bit to 1, when the trigger event occurs, the DBGRQ output is asserted until DBGACK is observed. This enables the Cortex-A5 processor to be forced into Debug state. On an ETM reset this bit is 0.

bits.name: branchoutput
bits.comment: Set this bit to 1 if you want the ETM to output all branch addresses, even if the branch isbecause of a direct branch instruction. Setting this bit to 1 enables reconstruction of the program flow without having access to the memory image of the code being executed.On an ETM reset this bit is 0.

bits.name: stallprocessor
bits.comment: ETM-A5 does not implement FIFOFULL stalling of the processor, and therefore this bit is RAZ.

bits.name: portsize[2:0]
bits.comment: Use this field with bit [21] to specify the port size.The port size determines how many external pins are available to output the trace information on ATDATA[31:0]. ETM-A5 supports only the 32-bit port size, corresponding to a Port size[3:0] value of b0100, but you can write other values to these bits, and a read of the register returns the value written. Writing other values to these bits has no effect on the ETM.Bit [10] of the System Configuration Register indicates if these bits are set to select an unsupported port size.For more information see the Embedded Trace Macrocell Architecture Specification. On an ETM reset this field is b100, corresponding to the 32-bit port size.

bits.name: dataaccess
bits.comment: This field configures the data tracing mode. The possible values are: b00 No data tracing. b01 Trace only the data portion of the access. b10 Trace only the address portion of the access. b11 Trace both the address and the data of the access. On an ETM reset this field is zero.

bits.name: monitorcprt
bits.comment: This field controls whether CPRTs are traced. The possible values are: 0 CPRTs not traced. 1 CPRTs traced. This bit is used with bit [19]. For details see Filter Coprocessor Register Transfers (CPRT) in ETMv3.0 and later in the Embedded Trace Macrocell Architecture Specification.

bits.name: etmpowerdown
bits.comment: A pin controlled by this bit enables the ETM power to be controlled externally, see Control of ETM power down. The sense of this bit is inverted, and drives the ETMPWRUP signal. This bit must be cleared by the trace software tools at the beginning of a debug session. When this bit is set to 1, ETM tracing is disabled and accesses to any registers other than this register and the Lock Access Register are ignored.On an ETM reset this bit is set to 1.

bits.name: etmidrpresent.
bits.comment: ETMIDR present.

bits.name: softwareaccessissupported.
bits.comment: Software access is supported.

bits.name: tracestart/stopblockispresent.
bits.comment: Trace start/stop block is present.

bits.name: numberofcontextidcomparators
bits.comment: Number of Context ID comparators.

bits.name: fifofulllogicabsent.
bits.comment: FIFOFULL logic absent.

bits.name: number_ext_out
bits.comment: Number of external outputs. Determined by the MAXEXTOUT[1:0] inputs.The value of these bits is the minimum of MAXEXTOUT[1:0] and 2, because ETM-A5 supports a maximum of 2 external outputs.

bits.name: number_ext_in
bits.comment: Number of external inputs. Determined by the MAXEXTIN[2:0] inputs. The value of these bits is the minimum of MAXEXTIN[2:0] and 4, because ETM-A5 supports a maximum of 4 external inputs.

bits.name: sequncer_is_present
bits.comment: The sequencer is present.

bits.name: number_counters
bits.comment: Number of counters.

bits.name: number_mm_decoder
bits.comment: Number of memory map decoders.

bits.name: number_data_comparator
bits.comment: Number of data comparators.

bits.name: number_pair_addr_comparator
bits.comment: Number of pairs of address comparators.

bits.name: func
bits.comment: function: 0: A 1: NOT(A) 2: A AND B 3: NOT(A) AND B 4: NOT(A) AND NOT(B) 5: A OR B 6: NOT(A) OR B 7: NOT(A) OR NOT(B)

bits.name: resource_b
bits.comment: Resource B [13:11]: resource type [10:7]: resource index

bits.name: resource_a
bits.comment: Resource A

bits.name: asic_ctl
bits.comment: ASICCTL[7:0]: when a bit in this field is set to 0 the corresponding bit of ASICCTL[7:0] is LOW when a bit in this field is set to 1 the corresponding bit of ASICCTL[7:0] is HIGH.

bits.name: trig_bit
bits.comment: v3.1 Trigger bit. Set when the trigger occurs, and prevents the trigger from being output until the ETM is programmed again. This bit exists in all architecture versions, but can only be accessed in ETMv3.1 and later as described in ETM Programming bit and associated state on page 3-97.

bits.name: curr_status_trace
bits.comment: Holds the current status of the trace start/stop resource. If set to 1, it indicates that a trace on address has been matched, without a corresponding trace off address match

bits.name: curr_effect_val_etm_prog_bit
bits.comment: The current effective value of the ETM Programming bit, bit [10] of the ETMCR. You must wait for this bit to go to 1 before you start to program the ETM as described in ETM Programming bit and associated state on page 3-97. If you read other bits in the ETMSR while this bit is 0, some instructions might not have taken effect. ARM recommends that you set the ETM Programming bit and wait for this bit to go to 1 before reading the overflow bit. In ETMv3.2 and later this bit remains 0 if there is any data in the FIFO. This ensures that the FIFO is empty before the ETM programming is changed. In ETMv3.5 this bit is set when the OS Lock is set. See OS Lock Status Register, ETMOSLSR, ETMv3.3 and later on page 3-166. In ETMv3.5 this bit must be polled before saving or restoring state. See Access permissions for ETMv3.5, multiple power domains on page 3-224

bits.name: trace_overflow
bits.comment: If set to 1, there is an overflow that has not yet been traced. This bit is cleared to 0 when either: ? trace is restarted. ? the ETM Power Down bit, bit [0] of ETMCR, is set to 1. Setting or clearing the ETM Programming bit does not cause this bit to be cleared to 0.

bits.name: no_fetch_comp
bits.comment: No Fetch comparisons. If this bit is set to 1, address comparators cannot perform fetch-stage comparisons. Setting bits [2:0] of an ETMACTR to b000, instruction fetch causes the comparator to have UNPREDICTABLE behavior.

bits.name: number_support_processor
bits.comment: Number of supported processors minus 1. The value given here is the maximum value that can be written to bits [27:25] of the ETMCR, register 0x000. This field must be b000 if the ETM supports Direct JTAG access

bits.name: port_mode_support
bits.comment: Port mode supported. Set to 1 if the currently selected port mode is supported internally or externally.

bits.name: port_size_support
bits.comment: Port size supported. Set to 1 if the currently selected port size is supported internally or externally for the currently selected port mode. Enables more complex port sizes to be supported

bits.name: max_port_size_3
bits.comment: Maximum port size[3]. This bit is used in conjunction with bits [2:0].

bits.name: fifofull_support
bits.comment: If set to 1, FIFOFULL is supported. This bit is used in conjunction with bit [23] of the ETMCCR, register 0x001.

bits.name: max_port_size_2_0
bits.comment: Maximum port size[2:0]. This bit is used in conjunction with bit [9]. The value given here is the maximum size supported by both the ETM and the ASIC. Smaller sizes might or might not be supported. Check bit [10] for precise information on supported modes. See bits [6:4] in ETMCR bit assignments on page 3-101.

bits.name: stop_addr
bits.comment: When a bit is set to 1, it selects a single address comparator 16-1 as stop addresses. For example, bit [16] set to 1 selects single address comparator 1 as a stop address.

bits.name: start_addr
bits.comment: When a bit is set to 1, it selects a single address comparator 16-1 as start addresses. For example, bit [0] set to 1 selects single address comparator 1 as a start address.

bits.name: slect_address_comparator
bits.comment: When a bit is set to 1, it selects a single address comparator 16-1 for include/exclude control. For example, bit [0] set to 1 selects single address comparator 1.

bits.name: func
bits.comment: function: 0: A 1: NOT(A) 2: A AND B 3: NOT(A) AND B 4: NOT(A) AND NOT(B) 5: A OR B 6: NOT(A) OR B 7: NOT(A) OR NOT(B)

bits.name: resource_b
bits.comment: Resource B [13:11]: resource type [10:7]: resource index

bits.name: resource_a
bits.comment: Resource A

bits.name: trace_start_stop_en
bits.comment: Trace start/stop enable. The possible values of this bit are: 0 Tracing is unaffected by the trace start/stop logic. 1 Tracing is controlled by the trace on and off addresses configured for the trace start/stop logic. See The trace start/stop block on page 2-40. The trace start/stop resource (resource 0x5F) is unaffected by the value of this bit.

bits.name: include_exclude_ctrl
bits.comment: Include/exclude control. The possible values of this bit are: 0 Include. The specified resources indicate the regions where tracing can occur. When outside this region tracing is prevented. 1 Exclude. The resources, specified in bits [23:0] and in the ETMTECR2, indicate regions to be excluded from the trace. When outside an exclude region, tracing can occur.

bits.name: select_mm_decoder
bits.comment: When a bit is set to 1, it selects memory map decode 16-1 for include/exclude control. For example, bit [8] set to 1 selects MMD 1.

bits.name: select_addr_range_comparator
bits.comment: When a bit is set to 1, it selects address range comparator 8-1 for include/exclude control. For example, bit [0] set to 1 selects address range comparator 1.

bits.name: number_bytes_left_fifo
bits.comment: The number of bytes left in the FIFO, below which the FIFOFULL or SuppressData signal is asserted. For example, setting this value to 15 causes data trace suppression or processor stalling, if enabled, when there are less than 15 free bytes in the FIFO.

bits.name: func
bits.comment: function: 0: A 1: NOT(A) 2: A AND B 3: NOT(A) AND B 4: NOT(A) AND NOT(B) 5: A OR B 6: NOT(A) OR B 7: NOT(A) OR NOT(B)

bits.name: resource_b
bits.comment: Resource B [13:11]: resource type [10:7]: resource index

bits.name: resource_a
bits.comment: Resource A

bits.name: select_addr_comparator_exclude
bits.comment: When a bit is set to 1, it selects single address comparator 16 to 1 for exclude control. For example, bit [16] set to 1 selects single address comparator 1.

bits.name: select_addr_comparator_include
bits.comment: When a bit is set to 1, it selects single address comparator 16 to 1 for include control. For example, bit [0] set to 1 selects single address comparator 1.

bits.name: exclude_ctrl
bits.comment: Exclude-only control. The possible values of this bit are: 0 Mixed mode. ViewData operates in a mixed mode, and both include and exclude resources can be programmed. 1 Exclude-only mode. ViewData is programmed only in an excluding mode. If none of the excluding resources match, tracing can occur.

bits.name: select_addr_comparator_exclude
bits.comment: When a bit is set to 1, it selects address range comparator 8-1 for exclude control. For example, bit [8] set to 1 selects address range comparator 1.

bits.name: select_addr_comparator_include
bits.comment: When a bit is set to 1, it selects address range comparator 8-1 for include control. For example, bit [0] set to 1 selects address range comparator 1.

bits.name: addr_value
bits.comment: Address value

bits.name: addr_value
bits.comment: Address value

bits.name: addr_value
bits.comment: Address value

bits.name: addr_value
bits.comment: Address value

bits.name: addr_value
bits.comment: Address value

bits.name: addr_value
bits.comment: Address value

bits.name: addr_value
bits.comment: Address value

bits.name: addr_value
bits.comment: Address value

bits.name: vmid_comp_enable
bits.comment: Virtual Machine ID (VMID) comparison enable, if the processor implements the Virtualization Extensions.b A value of 1 means that the address comparator matches only if the current VMID matches the value stored in the ETMVMIDCVR. See VMID Comparator Value Register, ETMVMIDCVR, ETMv3.5 on page 3-164. This bit is reserved, RAZ if the processor does not implement the Virtualization extensions

bits.name: hyp_mode_comp_enable
bits.comment: Hyp mode comparison enable, if the processor implements the Virtualization Extensions.b A value of 1 means that the address comparator also matches if the processor is operating in Hyp mode. See Virtualization Extensions, ETMv3.5 on page 7-345. This bit is reserved, RAZ if the processor does not implement the Virtualization extensions.

bits.name: state_mode_comp_enable
bits.comment: State and mode comparison control. The assignment of these bits is: Bit [13, 11] Non-secure state comparison control. Bit [12, 10] Secure state comparison control. For each pair of bits, the encoding is: b00 Match in all modes in this state. b01 Do not match in any modes in this state. b10 Match in all modes except User mode in this state. b11 Match only in User mode in this state. If the processor does not implement the Security Extensions, bits [13, 11] are reserved, RAZ/WI. See Filtering by state and mode, in ETMv3.5 on page 3-131

bits.name: context_id_comp_ctrl
bits.comment: Context ID comparator control. The permitted values of this field are: b00 Ignore Context ID comparator. b01 Address comparator matches only if Context ID comparator value 1 matches. b10 Address comparator matches only if Context ID comparator value 2 matches. b11 Address comparator matches only if Context ID comparator value 3 matches.

bits.name: exact_match
bits.comment: Exact match bit. Specifies comparator behavior when exceptions, aborts, and load misses occur. See Exact matching, in ETMv2.0 and later on page 2-54.

bits.name: data_value_comp_ctrl
bits.comment: Data value comparison control. The permitted values of this field are: b00 No data value comparison is made. b01 Comparator can match only if data value matches. b11 Comparator can match only if data value does not match. The value of b10 is reserved and must not be used. Note: The b11 encoding was introduced in ETM architecture version 1.2. Previously this value was reserved. For details of the effect of this field on data value comparison, see Exact matching for data address comparisons on page 2-56.

bits.name: comp_access_size
bits.comment: Comparison access size. The permitted values of this field are: b00 Java instruction (from ETM architecture version 1.3 only) or byte data. b01 Thumb instruction or halfword data. b11 ARM instruction or word data. The value of b10 is reserved and must not be used. For more information, see Comparator access size on page 2-49.

bits.name: access_type
bits.comment: Access type. The permitted values of this field are: b000c Instruction fetch. b001 Instruction execute. b010 Instruction executed and passed condition code test. b011 Instruction executed and failed condition code test. b100 Data load or store. b101 Data load. b110 Data store. The value of b111 is reserved and must not be used. Note: ? The b010 and b011 encodings were introduced in ETM architecture version 1.2. Previously these values were reserved. ? From ETMv3.3, if data address comparisons are not supported, writing b100, b101 or b110 to this field causes UNPREDICTABLE behavior. See No data address comparator option, ETMv3.3 and later on page 2-25 for more information.

See VMID Comparator Value Register, ETMVMIDCVR, ETMv3.5 on page 3-164. This bit is reserved, RAZ if the processor does not implement the Virtualization extensions

bits.name: hyp_mode_comp_enable
bits.comment: Hyp mode comparison enable, if the processor implements the Virtualization Extensions.b A value of 1 means that the address comparator also matches if the processor is operating in Hyp mode. See Virtualization Extensions, ETMv3.5 on page 7-345. This bit is reserved, RAZ if the processor does not implement the Virtualization extensions.

bits.name: state_mode_comp_enable
bits.comment: State and mode comparison control. The assignment of these bits is: Bit [13, 11] Non-secure state comparison control. Bit [12, 10] Secure state comparison control. For each pair of bits, the encoding is: b00 Match in all modes in this state. b01 Do not match in any modes in this state. b10 Match in all modes except User mode in this state. b11 Match only in User mode in this state. If the processor does not implement the Security Extensions, bits [13, 11] are reserved, RAZ/WI. See Filtering by state and mode, in ETMv3.5 on page 3-131

bits.name: context_id_comp_ctrl
bits.comment: Context ID comparator control. The permitted values of this field are: b00 Ignore Context ID comparator. b01 Address comparator matches only if Context ID comparator value 1 matches. b10 Address comparator matches only if Context ID comparator value 2 matches. b11 Address comparator matches only if Context ID comparator value 3 matches.

bits.name: exact_match
bits.comment: Exact match bit. Specifies comparator behavior when exceptions, aborts, and load misses occur. See Exact matching, in ETMv2.0 and later on page 2-54.

bits.name: data_value_comp_ctrl
bits.comment: Data value comparison control. The permitted values of this field are: b00 No data value comparison is made. b01 Comparator can match only if data value matches. b11 Comparator can match only if data value does not match. The value of b10 is reserved and must not be used. Note: The b11 encoding was introduced in ETM architecture version 1.2. Previously this value was reserved. For details of the effect of this field on data value comparison, see Exact matching for data address comparisons on page 2-56.

bits.name: comp_access_size
bits.comment: Comparison access size. The permitted values of this field are: b00 Java instruction (from ETM architecture version 1.3 only) or byte data. b01 Thumb instruction or halfword data. b11 ARM instruction or word data. The value of b10 is reserved and must not be used. For more information, see Comparator access size on page 2-49.

bits.name: access_type
bits.comment: Access type. The permitted values of this field are: b000c Instruction fetch. b001 Instruction execute. b010 Instruction executed and passed condition code test. b011 Instruction executed and failed condition code test. b100 Data load or store. b101 Data load. b110 Data store. The value of b111 is reserved and must not be used. Note: ? The b010 and b011 encodings were introduced in ETM architecture version 1.2. Previously these values were reserved. ? From ETMv3.3, if data address comparisons are not supported, writing b100, b101 or b110 to this field causes UNPREDICTABLE behavior. See No data address comparator option, ETMv3.3 and later on page 2-25 for more information.

See VMID Comparator Value Register, ETMVMIDCVR, ETMv3.5 on page 3-164. This bit is reserved, RAZ if the processor does not implement the Virtualization extensions

See Virtualization Extensions, ETMv3.5 on page 7-345. This bit is reserved, RAZ if the processor does not implement the Virtualization extensions.

bits.name: count_enable_source
bits.comment: Count enable source in ETMv1.x. When set to 0, the counter is continuously enabled and decrements every cycle regardless of the count enable event. When set to 1, the count enable event is used to enable the counter. ARM recommends that bit [17] is always set to 1 and that the count enable event is used to control counter operation, using 0x6F (TRUE) if a free running counter is required. Note This bit is not supported in ETMv2.0 and later, and is always set to 1 in these ETM architecture versions.

bits.name: curr_sequencer_state
bits.comment: Current sequencer state.The permitted values of this field are: b00 Sequencer currently in state 1. b01 Sequencer currently in state 2. b10 Sequencer currently in state 3. The value of b11 is reserved. From ETMv3.1, when the Programming bit is set to 1, software can write to this field to force the sequencer to a particular state. The effect of writing b11 to this field is UNPREDICTABLE, and software must not write this value.

bits.name: context_id
bits.comment: Context ID value

bits.name: context_id_mask
bits.comment: Context ID mask value

bits.name: sync_freq
bits.comment: Synchronization frequency. Default value is 1024.

bits.name: branch_packet_encode_impl
bits.comment: Branch packet encoding implemented. The possible values of this bit are: 0 The ETM implements the original branch packet encoding. See Branch packet formats with the original address encoding scheme on page 7-310. 1 The ETM implements the alternative branch packet encoding. See Branch packet formats with the alternative address encoding scheme on page 7-313.

bits.name: sec_ext_support
bits.comment: Support for Security Extensions. The possible values of this bit are: 0 The ETM behaves as if the processor is in Secure state at all times. 1 The ARM architecture Security Extensions are implemented by the processor

bits.name: thumb_32bit_instr_support
bits.comment: Support for 32-bit Thumb instructions. The possible values of this bit are: 0: A 32-bit Thumb instruction is traced as two instructions, and exceptions might occur between these two instructions. 1: A 32-bit Thumb instruction is traced as a single instruction. See 32-bit Thumb instructions on page 4-240 for more information.

bits.name: load_pc_first
bits.comment: Load PC first. If this bit is set to 1, LSMs with the PC in the list load the PC first, followed by the other registers in the normal order. This can be decompressed by using the following procedure: 1. Calculate the number of items transferred by the LSM by looking at the code image. 2. As each item is read, assign an address equal to 4 greater than the previous one as normal. 3. When the number of items read equals the total number of items transferred, subtract (4 * number of items) from each address other than the first. Note This means that a branch address can be traced before the remaining data values of an instruction. While this has never been prohibited in the protocol, care must be taken to ensure that this case is correctly handled.

bits.name: processor_family
bits.comment: Processor family. The meaning of this field depends on the value of the Implementer code.The following apply if Implementer code = 0x41, for ARM Limited: b0000 ARM7 processor. b0001 ARM9 processor. b0010 ARM10 processor. b0011 ARM11 processor b1111 Processor family is defined elsewhere. See The Processor family field on page 3-157 for more information. When the Implementer code = 0x41, all other values are reserved by ARM Limited. For any other Implementer code the permitted values of this field are defined by the implementer.

bits.name: major_etm_arch_ver
bits.comment: Major ETM architecture version number. See The ETM architecture version. Possible values of this field are: b0000 ETMv1. b0001 ETMv2. b0010 ETMv3. All other values are reserved.

bits.name: minor_etm_arch_ver
bits.comment: Minor ETM architecture version number. See The ETM architecture version.

bits.name: impl_rev
bits.comment: Implementation revision. See Implementation revision on page 3-157

bits.name: timestamp_packet_size
bits.comment: Timestamp packet size. This bit is 0 if the size of the packet is 48 bits. This bit is 1 if the size of the packet is 64 bits.

bits.name: timestamp_packet_encoding
bits.comment: Timestamp packet encoding. This bit is 1 if the timestamp packet is encoded as a natural binary number. This bit is 0 if the packet is gray coded. For more information see Encoding of the timestamp value on page 7-343.

bits.name: reduced_func_counter
bits.comment: Reduced function counter. This bit is 1 if counter 1 is implemented as a reduced function counter. This bit is 0 if all counters are implemented as full-function counters.

bits.name: virt_extension_impl
bits.comment: The Virtualization Extensions are implemented. This bit is 1 if the Virtualization Extensions are implemented, and 0 if not implemented.

bits.name: timestamp_impl
bits.comment: Timestamping implemented. This bit is 1 if timestamping is implemented, and 0 if it is not implemented

bits.name: etmeibcr_impl
bits.comment: ETMEIBCR implemented. This bit is 1 if the register is implemented, and 0 if it is not implemented.

bits.name: trace_embedice_start_stop
bits.comment: Trace Start/Stop block can use EmbeddedICE watchpoint inputs. This bit is 1 if the Trace Start/Stop block can use these inputs, and is 0 otherwise.

bits.name: number_embedice_watch_point
bits.comment: Number of EmbeddedICE watchpoint inputs implemented. This field can take any value from b0000 (0 inputs) to b1000 (8 inputs).

bits.name: number_instr_resource
bits.comment: Number of Instrumentation resources supported. The maximum value of this field is b100, for four Instrumentation resources. For more information see Instrumentation resources, from ETMv3.3 on page 2-69.

bits.name: addr_comparison_not_support
bits.comment: Set to 1 if data address comparisons are not supported. For more information see No data address comparator option, ETMv3.3 and later on page 2-25.

bits.name: all_reg_readable
bits.comment: Set to 1 if all registers are readable

bits.name: size_extended_ext_input
bits.comment: Size of extended external input bus. This field must be 0 if bits [2:0] are 0.

bits.name: numer_extended_input_sel
bits.comment: Number of extended external input selectors.

bits.name: exteneded_external_input_sel4
bits.comment: Extended external input selector 4

bits.name: exteneded_external_input_sel3
bits.comment: Extended external input selector 3

bits.name: exteneded_external_input_sel2
bits.comment: Extended external input selector 2

bits.name: exteneded_external_input_sel1
bits.comment: Extended external input selector 1

bits.name: stop_resource_sel
bits.comment: Stop resource selection. Setting a bit in this field to 1 selects the corresponding EmbeddedICE watchpoint input as a TraceEnable stop resource. Bit [16] corresponds to input 1, bit [17] to input 2, and this pattern continues up to bit [23] corresponding to input 8.

bits.name: start_resource_sel
bits.comment: Start resource selection. Setting a bit in this field to 1 selects the corresponding EmbeddedICE watchpoint input as a TraceEnable start resource. Bit [0] corresponds to input 1, bit [1] to input 2, and this pattern continues up to bit [7] corresponding to input 8.

bits.name: trace_id_ouput
bits.comment: Trace ID to output onto the trace bus. On an ETM reset this field is cleared to 0x00.

bits.name: order_trans_swp
bits.comment: Identifies the order of transfers for a SWP or SWPB instruction: 0 = the Load transfer is traced before the Store transfer 1 = the Store transfer is traced before the Load transfer

bits.name: order_trans_rfe
bits.comment: Identifies the order of transfers for the RFE instruction: 0 = the PC transfer is traced before the CPSR transfer 1 = the CPSR transfer is traced before the PC transfer

bits.name: os_lock_status
bits.comment: OS lock status. The value of this bit is the same as the value of bit [1] of the ETMOSLSR, which indicates whether the ETM trace registers are locked. See OS Lock Status Register, ETMOSLSR, ETMv3.3 and later on page 3-166. This bit is UNKNOWN when the ETM is powered down

bits.name: sticky_reg_state
bits.comment: Sticky Register state bit. The possible values of this bit are: 0 ETM Trace Registers have not been powered down since this register was last read. 1 ETM Trace Registers have been powered down since this register was last read, and have lost their state. When the core power domain of the ETM is powered down or reset, this bit is set to 1. Reads of this register when the core power domain is powered down or held in reset return 1 for this bit, and do not change the value of this bit. Reads of this register when the core power domain is powered up and not held in reset return the current value of this bit, and then clear this bit to 0. If the Software Lock mechanism is locked and the ETMPDSR read is made through the memory mapped interface, this bit is not cleared. In ETMv3.3 and ETMv3.4,when this bit is set, accesses to any ETM Trace Registers return an error response. In ETMv3.5, the value of this bit has no effect on accesses to the ETM Trace Registers.

bits.name: etm_powerup
bits.comment: ETM powered up bit. The value of this bit indicates whether you can access the ETM Trace Registers. The possible values are: 0 ETM Trace Registers cannot be accessed. 1 ETM Trace Registers can be accessed. When this bit is set to 0, accesses to any ETM Trace Registers return an error response.

bits.name: extout
bits.comment: Drives the EXTOUT[1:0] output pins

bits.name: etmwfxready
bits.comment: Drives the nETMWFXREADY output pin

bits.name: etmdbgrq
bits.comment: Drives the ETMDBGRQ output pina

bits.name: etmwfxpending
bits.comment: Returns the value of the ETMWFXPENDING input pin

bits.name: dbgack
bits.comment: Returns the value of the DBGACK input pin

bits.name: extin
bits.comment: Returns the value of the EXTIN[3:0] input pins

bits.name: trigger
bits.comment: Drives the TRIGGER output pin

bits.name: drive_atdata1
bits.comment: Drives the ATDATA[31, 23, 15, 7, 0] output pins

bits.name: syncreq
bits.comment: Returns the value of the SYNCREQ input pin

bits.name: afvalid
bits.comment: Returns the value of the AFVALID input pin

bits.name: atready
bits.comment: Returns the value of the ATREADY input pin

bits.name: atid
bits.comment: Drives the ATID[6:0] output pins

bits.name: atbytes
bits.comment: Drives the ATBYTES[1:0] output pins

bits.name: afready
bits.comment: Drives the AFREADY output pin

bits.name: atvalid
bits.comment: Drives the ATVALID output pin

bits.name: int_mode
bits.comment: When this bit is set to 1, the device enters an integration mode to enable Topology Detection or Integration Testing to be checked. On an ETM reset this bit is cleared to 0.

bits.name: tag_bits_set
bits.comment: On reads, returns 0xFF. On writes, a 1 in a bit position causes the corresponding bit in the claim tag value to be set.

bits.name: tag_bits_clr
bits.comment: On reads, returns the current claim tag value. On writes, a 1 in a bit position causes the corresponding bit in the claim tag value to be cleared to 0. On an ETM reset this field is cleared to 0x00.

bits.name: etmlar
bits.comment: Write 0xC5ACCE55 to this field to unlock the ETM. Write any other value to this field to lock the ETM

bits.name: etmlar_32_bits
bits.comment: Reads as b0. Indicates that the ETMLAR is 32 bits

bits.name: etm_locked
bits.comment: Indicates whether the ETM is locked. The possible values of this bit are: 0 Writes are permitted. 1 ETM locked. Writes are ignored. If this register is accessed from an interface where the lock registers are ignored, this field reads as 0 regardless of whether the ETM is locked.

bits.name: lock_reg_impl
bits.comment: Indicates whether the lock registers are implemented for this interface. The possible values of this bit are: 0 This access is from an interface that ignores the lock registers. 1 This access is from an interface that requires the ETM to be unlocked.

bits.name: snid
bits.comment: Permission for Secure non-invasive debug.

bits.name: sid
bits.comment: Reads as b00, Secure invasive debug not supported by the ETM

bits.name: nsnid
bits.comment: Permission for Non-secure non-invasive debug. This field is only implemented if the processor implemented with the ETM implements the Security Extensions. When this field is implemented the possible values of the field are: b10 Non-secure non-invasive debug disabled. b11 Non-secure non-invasive debug enabled. This field is a logical OR of the NIDEN and DBGEN signals. It takes the value b11 when the OR is TRUE, and b10 when the OR is FALSE. If the processor does not support the Security Extensions, bits [3:2] are reserved, RAZ.

bits.name: nsid
bits.comment: Reads as b00, Non-secure invasive debug not supported by the ETM.

bits.name: sub_type
bits.comment: 0x1 Sub type, processor trace

bits.name: main_type
bits.comment: 0x3 Main type, trace source

bits.name: n
bits.comment: n, where 2n is number of 4KB blocks used.

bits.name: jep106_con_code
bits.comment: JEP 106 continuation code

bits.name: part_number
bits.comment: Part Number[7:0]. Middle and Lower BCD value of Device Number.

bits.name: jep106_id_3_0
bits.comment: JEP 106 identity code[3:0]

bits.name: part_number_11_8
bits.comment: Part Number[11:8]. Upper Binary Coded Decimal (BCD) value of Device Number.

bits.name: rev_number
bits.comment: Revision Number of Peripheral. This value is the same as the Implementation revision field of the ETMIDR, see ETM ID Register on page 3-19.

bits.name: jedec_val_in_use
bits.comment: Always 1. Indicates that a JEDEC assigned value is used.

bits.name: jep106_id_6_4
bits.comment: JEP 106 identity code[6:4].

bits.name: revand
bits.comment: RevAnd (at top level). Manufacturer revision number.

bits.name: customized_val
bits.comment: Customer Modified. 0x0 indicates from ARM

bits.name: cid_7_0
bits.comment: Component identifier, bits [7:0].

bits.name: component_class
bits.comment: Component class (component identifier, bits [15:12]).

bits.name: cid_11_8
bits.comment: Component identifier, bits [11:8].

bits.name: cid_23_16
bits.comment: Component identifier, bits [23:16].

bits.name: cid_31_24
bits.comment: Component identifier, bits [31:24].

bits.name: glben
bits.comment: Enables or disables the CTI. 0 When this bit is 0, all cross-triggering mapping logic functionality is disabled. 1 When this bit is 1, cross-triggering mapping logic functionality is enabled.

bits.name: intack
bits.comment: Acknowledges the corresponding ctitrigout output. There is one bit of the register for each ctitrigout output. When a 1 is written to a bit in this register, the corresponding ctitrigout is acknowledged, causing it to be cleared.

bits.name: appset
bits.comment: Setting a bit HIGH generates a channel event for the selected channel. There is one bit of the register for each channel. Reads as follows: 0 Application trigger is inactive. 1 Application trigger is active. Writes as follows: 0 No effect. 1 Generate channel event.

bits.name: appclear
bits.comment: Sets the corresponding bits in the CTIAPPSET to 0. There is one bit of the register for each channel. On writes, for each bit: 0 Has no effect. 1 Clears the corresponding channel event.

bits.name: appulse
bits.comment: Setting a bit HIGH generates a channel event pulse for the selected channel. There is one bit of the register for each channel. On writes, for each bit: 0 Has no effect. 1 Generate an event pulse on the corresponding channel.

bits.name: triginen
bits.comment: Enables a cross trigger event to the corresponding channel when a ctitrigin input is activated. There is one bit of the field for each of the four channels. On writes, for each bit: 0 Input trigger 0 events are ignored by the corresponding channel. 1 When an event is received on input trigger 0, ctitrigin[0], generate an event on the channel corresponding to this bit.

bits.name: triginen
bits.comment: Enables a cross trigger event to the corresponding channel when a ctitrigin input is activated. There is one bit of the field for each of the four channels. On writes, for each bit: 0 Input trigger 0 events are ignored by the corresponding channel. 1 When an event is received on input trigger 0, ctitrigin[1], generate an event on the channel corresponding to this bit.

bits.name: triginen
bits.comment: Enables a cross trigger event to the corresponding channel when a ctitrigin input is activated. There is one bit of the field for each of the four channels. On writes, for each bit: 0 Input trigger 0 events are ignored by the corresponding channel. 1 When an event is received on input trigger 0, ctitrigin[2], generate an event on the channel corresponding to this bit.

bits.name: triginen
bits.comment: Enables a cross trigger event to the corresponding channel when a ctitrigin input is activated. There is one bit of the field for each of the four channels. On writes, for each bit: 0 Input trigger 0 events are ignored by the corresponding channel. 1 When an event is received on input trigger 0, ctitrigin[3], generate an event on the channel corresponding to this bit.

bits.name: triginen
bits.comment: Enables a cross trigger event to the corresponding channel when a ctitrigin input is activated. There is one bit of the field for each of the four channels. On writes, for each bit: 0 Input trigger 0 events are ignored by the corresponding channel. 1 When an event is received on input trigger 0, ctitrigin[4], generate an event on the channel corresponding to this bit.

bits.name: triginen
bits.comment: Enables a cross trigger event to the corresponding channel when a ctitrigin input is activated. There is one bit of the field for each of the four channels. On writes, for each bit: 0 Input trigger 0 events are ignored by the corresponding channel. 1 When an event is received on input trigger 0, ctitrigin[5], generate an event on the channel corresponding to this bit.

bits.name: triginen
bits.comment: Enables a cross trigger event to the corresponding channel when a ctitrigin input is activated. There is one bit of the field for each of the four channels. bits.name: ram_write_pointer

bits.name: trigger_counter
bits.comment: The counter is used as follows: Trace after The counter is set to a large value, slightly less than the number of entries in the RAM. Trace before The counter is set to a small value. Trace about The counter is set to half the depth of the trace RAM. You must not write to this register when trace capture is enabled, FFSR.FtStopped is 0, and CTL.TraceCaptEn is 1. When a write is attempted, then the register is not updated. A read operation is permitted when trace capture is enabled.

bits.name: tracecapten
bits.comment: ETB Trace Capture Enable. This is the master enable bit that sets FtStopped to HIGH when TraceCaptEn is LOW. When capture is disabled, any remaining data in the ATB formatter is stored to RAM. When all of the data is stored, the formatter outputs FtStopped. Capture is fully disabled, or complete, when FtStopped goes HIGH. See ETB Formatter and Flush Status Register. 0 Disable trace capture. 1 Enable trace capture.

bits.name: ram_write_data
bits.comment: When CTL.TraceCaptEn is 0: ? Writes to this register write the data to the ETB trace RAM. The RAM Write Pointer Register value is incremented. ? The data is not written to the ETB trace RAM and the RAM Write Pointer is not affected. ? Reads of this register return an UNKNOWN value.

bits.name: ime
bits.comment: Integration Mode Enable. 0 Disable integration mode. 1 Enable integration mode.

bits.name: set
bits.comment: On reads, for each bit: 1 Claim tag bit is implemented On writes, for each bit: 0 Has no effect. 1 Sets the relevant bit of the claim tag.

bits.name: clr
bits.comment: On reads, for each bit: 0 Claim tag bit is not set. 1 Claim tag bit is set. On writes, for each bit: 0 Has no effect. 1 Clears the relevant bit of the claim tag.

bits.name: key
bits.comment: Software lock key value. 0xC5ACCE55 Clear the software lock. All other write values set the software lock.

bits.name: ntt
bits.comment: Register size indicator. Always 0. Indicates that the LAR is implemented as 32-bit.

bits.name: slk
bits.comment: 0 Indicates that write operations are permitted from this interface. 1 Indicates that write operations are not permitted from this interface. Read operations are permitted.

bits.name: sli
bits.comment: Software Lock Implemented. Indicates that a lock control mechanism is present from this interface. 0 Indicates that a lock control mechanism is not present from this interface. Write operations to the LAR are ignored. 1 Indicates that a lock control mechanism is present from this interface

bits.name: snid
bits.comment: Always 0b00. The security level for Secure non-invasive debug is not implemented or is controlled elsewhere.

bits.name: sid
bits.comment: Always 0b00 Secure invasive debug is not implemented or is controlled elsewhere.

bits.name: nsnid
bits.comment: Indicates the security level for Non-secure non-invasive debug: 0b10 Disabled. 0b11 Enabled.

bits.name: nsid
bits.comment: Indicates the security level for Non-secure invasive debug: 0b10 Disabled. 0b11 Enabled.

bits.name: scheme
bits.comment: Indicates the priority scheme implemented in this component. 0b0011 Program the slave ports to have higher or lower priority with respect to each other.

bits.name: portcount
bits.comment: Indicates the number of input ports connected. 0x0 and 0x1 are illegal values. 0b0010 Two ATB slave ports. 0b0011 Three ATB slave ports. 0b0100 Four ATB slave ports. 0b0101 Five ATB slave ports. 0b0110 Six ATB slave ports. 0b0111 Seven ATB slave ports. 0b1000 Eight ATB slave ports.

bits.name: sub
bits.comment: Sub-classification of the type of the debug component as specified in the ARM? CoreSight? Architecture Specification within the major classification as specified in the MAJOR field: 0b0001 This component arbitrates ATB inputs mapping to ATB outputs.

bits.name: major
bits.comment: Major classification of the type of the debug component as specified in the ARM? CoreSight? Architecture Specification for this debug and trace component: 0b0010 This component has both ATB inputs and ATB outputs.

bits.name: size
bits.comment: Always 0b0000. Indicates that the device only occupies 4KB of memory.

bits.name: des_2
bits.comment: Together, PIDR1.DES_0, PIDR2.DES_1, and PIDR4.DES_2 identify the designer of the component. 0b0100 JEDEC continuation code.

bits.name: part_0
bits.comment: Bits[7:0] of the 12-bit part number of the component. The designer of the component assigns this part number. 0x08 Indicates bits[7:0] of the part number of the component.

bits.name: des_0
bits.comment: Together, PIDR1.DES_0, PIDR2.DES_1, and PIDR4.DES_2 identify the designer of the component. 0b1011 ARM. Bits[3:0] of the JEDEC JEP106 Identity Code.

bits.name: part_0
bits.comment: Bits[11:8] of the 12-bit part number of the component. The designer of the component assigns this part number. 0b1001 Indicates bits[11:8] of the part number of the component.

bits.name: revision
bits.comment: 0b0011, This device is at r1p1.

bits.name: jedec
bits.comment: Always 1. Indicates that a JEDEC assigned value is used.

bits.name: des_1
bits.comment: Together, PIDR1.DES_0, PIDR2.DES_1, and PIDR4.DES_2 identify the designer of the component. 0b011 ARM. Bits[6:4] of the JEDEC JEP106 Identity Code.

bits.name: revand
bits.comment: Indicates minor errata fixes specific to the revision of the component being used, for example metal fixes after implementation. In most cases, this field is 0b0000. ARM recommends that the component designers ensure that a metal fix can change this field if required, for example, by driving it from registers that reset to 0b0000. 0b0000 Indicates that there are no errata fixes to this component.

bits.name: cmod
bits.comment: Customer Modified. Indicates whether the customer has modified the behavior of the component. In most cases, this field is 0b0000. bits.name: prmbl_0
bits.comment: Preamble[0]. Contains bits[7:0] of the component identification code. 0x0D Bits[7:0] of the identification code.

bits.name: prmbl_1
bits.comment: Preamble[1]. Contains bits[11:8] of the component identification code. 0b0000 Bits[11:8] of the identification code.

bits.name: prmbl_2
bits.comment: Preamble[2]. Contains bits[23:16] of the component identification code. 0x05 Bits[23:16] of the identification code.

bits.name: prmbl_3
bits.comment: Preamble[3]. Contains bits[31:24] of the component identification code. 0xB1 Bits[31:24] of the identification code.

bits.name: hdbg
bits.comment: Halt on Debug. 0 Do not halt on debug, HLTDBG signal into the counter has no effect. 1 Halt on debug, when HLTDBG is driven HIGH, the count value is held static.

bits.name: en
bits.comment: Enable. 0 The counter is disabled and not incrementing. 1 The counter is enabled and is incrementing.

bits.name: dbgh
bits.comment: Debug Halted.

bits.name: cntcvl_l_32
bits.comment: Current value of the timestamp counter, lower 32 bits. To change the current timestamp value, write the lower 32 bits of the new value to this register before writing the upper 32 bits to CNTCVU. The timestamp value is not changed until the CNTCVU register is written to.

bits.name: cntcvl_u_32
bits.comment: Current value of the timestamp counter, upper 32 bits. To change the current timestamp value, write the lower 32 bits of the new value to CNTCVL before writing the upper 32 bits to this register. The 64-bit timestamp value is updated with the value from both writes when this register is written to.

bits.name: tx_data
bits.comment: transmit data register

bits.name: rx_data
bits.comment: receive data register

bits.name: baud_const
bits.comment: baud rate divider constant N: (N>=4) 0011: N=4 ... 0111: N=8 ... 1111: N=16

bits.name: baud_div
bits.comment: baud rate divider coeffcientbaud rate formula is: BAUD RATE = Fclk/(Nx(BAUD_DIV+1)) default baud rate is 115.2K, N=16, Ffun=26MHz.

bits.name: tx_endian
bits.comment: choose big or little endian 0: little endian 1: big endian

bits.name: rxrst
bits.comment: RX FIFO reset control 1: RX FIFO reset 0: RX FIFO not reset; or set 1'b1, auto clear to 1'b0

bits.name: txrst
bits.comment: TX FIFO reset control 1: TX FIFO reset 0: TX FIFO not reset;or set to 1'b1,auto clear to 1'b0

bits.name: tout_hwfc
bits.comment: after RX timeout, enable hardware flow control (on condition that HWFC is enable) 1: after RX timeout,enable hardware flow control. Do not accept data until the timeout bit has been cleared, so that disable the hardware flow control 0: after RX timeout, disable hardware flow control

bits.name: rx_trig_hwfc
bits.comment: RX trigger RTS enable control (on condition that HWFC is enable) 1: enable RX TRIG trigger RTS flow signal 0: disable RX TRIG trigger RTS flow signal

bits.name: hwfc
bits.comment: hardware flow control bit 1: enable 0: disable

bits.name: tout_ie
bits.comment: RX timeout interrupt control bit 1: enable 0: disable

bits.name: tx_ie
bits.comment: TX data interrupt control bit 1: enable TX interrupt 0: disable TX interrupt

bits.name: rx_ie
bits.comment: RX data interrupt control bit 1: enable RX interrupt 0: disable RX interrupt

bits.name: st_check
bits.comment: stop bit detection control bit 1: enable stop bit detection 0: disable stop bit detection

bits.name: stop_bit
bits.comment: stop bit control bit 1: 2bit stop bit 0: 1bit stop bit

bits.name: parity
bits.comment: check bit 1: odd check 0: even check

bits.name: check
bits.comment: check bit enable or not 1: enable 0: disable

bits.name: tx_trig
bits.comment: TX FIFO trigger setting 00000000: 0 byte trigger 00000001: 1 byte trigger 00000010: 2 bytes trigger 00000011: 3 bytes trigger 00000100: 4 bytes trigger 01111110: 126bytes trigger 01111111: 127bytes trigger 10000000: don't trigger

bits.name: rx_trig
bits.comment: RX FIFO trigger settings 00000000: don't trigger 00000001: 1 byte trigger 00000010: 2 bytes trigger 00000011: 3 bytes trigger 00000100: 4 bytes trigger 01111111: 127bytes trigger 10000000: 128bytes trigger

bits.name: two_tx_delay
bits.comment: configure the time interval between sending data twice 0000: interval 0 baud rate clock 0001: interval 1 baud rate clock 1111: interval 15 baud rate clock

bits.name: toutcnt
bits.comment: configure the threshold value of the UART timeout interrupt counter 00000000: configure the initial value of 0 baud rate clock 00000001: configure the initial value of 1 baud rate clock 00000010: configure the initial value of 2 baud rate clock 11111111: configure the initial value of 255 baud rate clock

bits.name: rts
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1c to rc. request to send status bit 1: prohibit far-end to send 0: request far-end to send

bits.name: cts
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1c to rc. clear the sending status bit 1: prohibit home terminal to send 0: allow home terminal to send

bits.name: st_error
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1c to rc. the received data stop bit state 1: stop bit error 0: stop bit right

bits.name: p_error
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1c to rc. RX data parity status 1: parity error 0: parity right

bits.name: timeout_int
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1c to rc. RX data timeout interrupt status bit 1: timeout 0: not timeout

bits.name: rx_int
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1c to rc. RX data interrupt status bit 1: RX_FIFO_CNTRX_TRIG 0: RX_FIFO_CNT<RX_TRIG

bits.name: tx_int
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1c to rc. TX data interrupt status bit 1: TX_FIFO_CNT TX_TRIG 0: TX_FIFO_CNT >TX_TRIG

bits.name: tx_fifo_cnt
bits.comment: TX FIFO data number 00000000: TX FIFO has 0 data 00000001: TX FIFO has 1 data 01111111: TX FIFO has 127 data 10000000: TX FIFO has 128 data

bits.name: rx_fifo_cnt
bits.comment: RX FIFO data number 00000000: RX FIFO has 0 data 00000001: RX FIFO has 1 data 01111111: RX FIFO has 127 data 10000000: RX FIFO has 128 data

bits.name: auxadc_version
bits.comment: IP version r6p0

bits.name: adc_offset_cal_en
bits.comment: Auxadc offset function enable 0: disable offset calibration function 1: enable offset calibration function When set 1, the adc inner offset is calibrated and not include in output data

bits.name: rg_auxad_average
bits.comment: auxadc convert data out average control: 000: disable adc average, output 12bit data and valid after once conversion; 001: adc convert twice and output the average data; 010: adc convert 4 times and output the average data; 011: adc convert 8 times and output the average data; 100: adc convert 16 times and output the average data; 101: adc convert 32 times and output the average data; 110: adc convert 64 times and output the average data; 111: adc convert 128 times and output the average data;

bits.name: sw_ch_run_num
bits.comment: the number of SW channel accessing, N+1.

bits.name: adc_12b
bits.comment: No use, reserved

bits.name: sw_ch_run
bits.comment: SW channel run, Write 1 to run a SW channel accessing, it is cleared by HW.

bits.comment: ADC global enable, 0: ADC module disable; 1: ADC module enable.

bits.comment: ADC scale setting for current ADC channel, more detail see 7.6.6.3 Application note

bits.name: cal_start_busy
bits.comment: Write this bit 1 will start calibration process, write 0 has no effect Read this this will get the current calibration status. If 1, means the calibration is on progress. If 0, means calibration is finished, current is idle.

bits.name: cal_cycle_p0
bits.comment: Calibration cycle control, this is the low part of calibration cycle. Coupled with CAL_CYCLE_P1[7:0], the whole calibration cycles is : Calibration cycle = {CAL_CYCLE_P1[7:0],CAL_CYCLE_P0[15:0]}; The calibration cycle means using how many self-oscillator clocks to do calibration, the more cycles used, the more accuracy will be achieved. To make calculation simple, calibration cycle should be multiple of 2, that means, Calibration cycle = 2^n

bits.name: cal_cycle_p1
bits.comment: Calibration cycle control, this is the high part of calibration cycle.

bits.name: cal_result_p0
bits.comment: Calibration result, part 0. Coupled with CAL_RESULT_P1, the total calibration result is : Cal result = {CAL_RESULT_P1[15:0],CAL_RESULT_P0[15:0]}

bits.name: cal_result_p1
bits.comment: Calibration result, part 1.

bits.name: osc_div_fac_upd
bits.comment: Write this bit 1 will start 32k sigma-delta divider factor update process. write 0 has no effect Read this this will get the current update process status. If 1, means the update process is not finished. If 0, means this process is finished,current is idle.

bits.name: osc_div_fac_frac
bits.comment: 32k sigma-delta divider factor fraction part. This field is part of the fraction bits.

bits.name: osc_div_fac_int
bits.comment: 32k sigma-delta divider integer.

bits.name: margin_mode
bits.comment: Reserved

bits.name: efuse_type
bits.comment: Reserved

bits.name: efuse_pgm_enable
bits.comment: 0: Normal read mode, 1:Margin read1 mode

bits.name: efuse_data_rd
bits.comment: Efuse read data, If SW use efuse controller to send a read command to efuse memory, the return value will store here.

bits.name: efuse_data_wr
bits.comment: Efuse data to be write. If SW want to program the efuse memory, the data to be programmed will write to this register before SW issue a PGM command.

bits.name: efuse_addr_index
bits.comment: The efuse memory block index to be read or write.

bits.name: efuse_normal_rd_flag_clr
bits.comment: Write 1 to this bit will clear normal read flag. This bit is self-clear, read this bit will always get 0

bits.name: efuse_rd_start
bits.comment: Write 1 to this bit start READ mode(read mode). This bit is self-clear, read this bit will always get 0

bits.name: efuse_pg_start
bits.comment: Write 1 to this bit start PGM mode(PGM mode). This bit is self-clear, read this bit will always get 0

bits.name: efuse_normal_rd_done
bits.comment: 1 indicate EFUSE normal read has been done

bits.name: efuse_global_prot
bits.comment: If SW send a PGM command to memory and memory controller find the memory need to be protected (LSB of 64 bit is 1), this flag will be set to 1.

bits.name: standby_busy
bits.comment: 1 indicate efuse memory in standby mode

bits.name: read_busy
bits.comment: 1 indicate efuse memory in read mode

bits.name: pgm_busy
bits.comment: 1 indicate efuse memory in programming mode

bits.name: efuse_magin_magic_number
bits.comment: Magic number, only when this field is 0x2720, the Efuse programming command can be handle. So if SW want to program efuse memory, except open clocks and power, 2 other conditions must be met : a) PGM_EN =1; b) EFUSE_MAGIC_NUMBER = 0x2720

bits.name: efuse_magin_magic_number
bits.comment: Magic number, only when this field is 0x6868, the margin read is usable.

bits.name: efuse_wr_timing_ctrl
bits.comment: Config this register to control the timing of writing operation related signals. 300us voltage rise,20usx16 program,300us voltage fall

bits.name: efuse_rd_timing_ctrl
bits.comment: Config this register to control the timing of writing operation related signals 2.348us Read Time

bits.name: qmax_update_en
bits.comment: Qmax Update enables. Write 1 to this bit will do a Qmax update processing. It is auto cleared to 0, after write 1. To check the updating status, please read QMAX_UPD_STS.

bits.name: fgu_reset
bits.comment: FGU Reset signal. Write this bit to reset the module, it is auto cleared to 0 after reset.

bits.name: write_setclb_en
bits.comment: When write CLBCNT_SETH & CLBCNT_SETL, software should write this bit after write all of the two register to sync. It to CLK32KHz domain.

bits.name: sw_force_lock_high
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Software force qmax low voltage area to be locked, (Need to check WRITE_ACTIVE_STS)

bits.name: sw_force_lock_low
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Software force qmax high voltage area to be locked

bits.name: sw_force_qmax_cnt
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. When set to 1, qmax counter will be forced to intergrate current, regardless of qmax lock conditions.

bits.name: volt_h_valid
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Voltage high bit valid 0: voltage is 12 bits valid (high bit is omitted) 1: voltage is 13 bits valid

bits.name: fgu_disable_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. FGU Disable signal. It indicates if the FGU is worked or not. 0: FGU is not disable and worked 1: FGU is disable and not worked

bits.name: clbcnt_delta_mode
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Coulomb Counter Delta Threshold Mode. This bit indicates if the coulomb counter is working when the battery is in low power condition. 0: work when in low power condition 1: no work when in low power condition It is working in default.

bits.name: volt_duty
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Voltage duty ratio. 2h0: 1-7 2h1: 1-3 2h2: 1-1 2h3: 1-0 When ADC_SEL = 0, these bits are invalid. Refer to Timing Diagram for detail

bits.name: sw_dis_curt
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. When just use voltage of this module, this bit can disable all the current calculation logic, which will save power. 0: not disable current 1: disable current logic

bits.name: force_lock_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. When update the Qmax, if the battery is not in relax mode, then the voltage wont lock, write this bit will force the voltage lock to OCV either the battery is in relax mode or in active mode. 0: not force lock 1: force lock

bits.name: low_power_mode
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. There are 2 methods to judge whether the battery is in low power mode. 0: use relax counter to judge 1: use deep_sleep signal to judge

bits.name: auto_low_power
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. When the battery is in relax mode, the current can be set to sample at each 1 second instead of each 500ms, which will save power. If this bit is set 1, then the module will auto switch to low power mode. 0: not auto low, SW should control manually 1: auto low when the battery is in relax mode. Note: when AD1_ENABLE = 0, the voltage and current is measured in ADC0 Note: when AD1_ENABLE = 1, the current is measured in ADC0, and voltage is measured in ADC1.

bits.name: rg_sd_rsv
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. RG_SD_RSV[14]

bits.name: rg_sd_vcminavss_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Enable Common voltage tied to ground

bits.name: rg_sd_iboot_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Enable high current mode

bits.name: rg_sd_bgref_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Enable reference band gap

bits.name: adc_en_sel
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. When ADC_EN_SEL is 0, ADC enable is always high When ADC_EN_SEL is 1, FGU takes the control of ADC enable

bits.name: ad0_in_data
bits.comment: Ad0_in_data

bits.name: ad1_in_data
bits.comment: Ad1_in_data

bits.name: force_ad1_vin_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Force ADC1_VIN_EN interface to set value.

bits.name: force_ad0_vin_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Force ADC0_VIN_EN interface to set value.

bits.name: force_ad0_iin_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Force ADC0_IIN_EN interface to set value.

bits.name: force_ad_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Force ADC0/ADC1 interface enable.

bits.name: ad1_volt_ref
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. ADC1 Voltage Reference. 0: 0.1V 1: 0.2V

bits.name: ad0_volt_ref
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. ADC0 Voltage Reference. 0: 0.1V 1: 0.2V

bits.name: ad01_reset
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. ADC0 / ADC1 Reset

bits.name: ad01_pd
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. ADC0 / ADC1 Power Down

bits.name: battery_flag
bits.comment: This flag indicates whether the battery is plugged in during power on sequence.

bits.name: invalid_pocv
bits.comment: This flag indicates the power on open circuit voltage measurement is invalid.

bits.name: fgu_ana_sel
bits.comment: Select current and voltage enable signal between fgu_top and fgu_ana 0: select fgu_ana current and voltage enable signal 1: select fgu_top current and voltage enable signal

bits.name: power_low
bits.comment: Indicate the power is lower 0: not lower 1: lower Note: Case LOW_POWER_MODE = 0 when CURT_LOW is 1 and the relax counter is bigger than threshold, then the power is low. Case LOW_POWER_MODE = 1; The power mode select the deepsleep, then it is equal to deepsleep signal.

bits.name: curt_low
bits.comment: Indicate the current is lower then threshold 0: not lower 1: lower Note: when CURT_LOW is occur, the POWER_LOW may not occur other than the relax count is bigger than threshold.

bits.name: ocv_lock_sts
bits.comment: To update the Qmax, there should be two OCV lock. 2b00: OCV0 not locked OCV1 not locked. 2b01: OCV0 locked first OCV1 locked second. 2b10: OCV0 locked first OCV1 locked second 2b11: Invalid When both of them are locked, the Qmax is locked.

bits.name: qmax_update_sts
bits.comment: Qmax updating status 0: not in updating process. 1: in updating process.

bits.name: write_active_sts
bits.comment: When write following register, software should check this register to know whether it has been sync. to clk32KHz domain. FGU_CONFIG, ADC_CONFIG, FGU_INT_EN, FGU_HIGH_OVER, FGU_LOW_OVER, FGU_CLBCNT_SETH, FGU_CLBCNT_SETL

bits.name: clbcnt_low_int_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. When the CLBCNT is lower than wet clbcnt low threshold , then interrupt

bits.name: ocv_low_int_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. When the OCV is lower than set ocv low threshold, then interrupt

bits.name: curt_rden_int_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. When Current data is ready, an interrupt is generated. It is used when calibration.

bits.name: volt_rden_int_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. When Voltage data is ready, an interrupt is generated.

bits.name: qmax_upd_tout_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Qmax update timeout interrupt Enable

bits.name: qmax_upd_done_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Qmax update done interrupt Enable

bits.name: relx_cnt_int_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Relax Counter interrupt Enable. When the relax counter reached its set threshold, an interrupt is generated.

bits.name: clbcnt_delta_int_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Coulomb counter threshold interrupt Enable When the Coulomb counter reached the multiply of the threshold, then an interrupt is generated. E.g. If set CLBCNT_DELTA = 5mAh, then when the Coulomb counter is 5mAh, 10mAh, 15mAh will generate interrupt.

bits.name: volt_high_int_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Voltage High overload interrupts Enable. When the voltage is higher than the threshold, then an interrupt is generated.

bits.name: volt_low_int_en
bits.comment: bit type is changed from r/w to rw. Voltage Low overload interrupt Enable. When the voltage is lower than the threshold, then an interrupt is generated.

bits.comment: CLBCNT lower interrupt clear

bits.name: ocv_low_int_clr
bits.comment: OCV lower interrupt clear

bits.name: curt_rden_int_clr
bits.comment: Current ready interrupt clear

bits.name: volt_rden_int_clr
bits.comment: Voltage ready interrupt clear

bits.name: clbcnt_delta_int_clr
bits.comment: Coulomb counter delta interrupt clear

bits.name: volt_high_int_clr
bits.comment: Voltage High overload interrupts clear.

bits.name: volt_low_int_clr
bits.comment: Voltage Low overload interrupts clear.
