bits.name: enable
bits.comment:
Enable the rf spi
1 = Enable
0 = Disable (will finish current command anyway)

bits.name: cs_polarity
bits.comment:
Chip select polarity
1 = the chip select is active low
0 = the chip select is active high

bits.name: digrf_read
bits.comment:
DigRF Read style mode
1 = DigRF Read style mode (read after CS disabled)
0 = SPI Read mode (read during write)

bits.name: clocked_back2back
bits.comment:
DigRF style clocked back to back mode
1 = clocked back to back transfers using turnarround timing only when more data are present in the FIFO.
0 = stop the clock between each access according to CS_End_Hold and CS_Pulse_Min timings

bits.name: input_mode
bits.comment:
Input mode
1 = Record input data to input FIFO
0 = No input data

bits.name: clock_polarity
bits.comment:
SPI Clock polarity
1 = the clock disabled level is high, and the first edge is a falling edge.
0 = the clock disabled level is low, and the first edge is a rising edge.

bits.name: clock_delay
bits.comment:
Transfer start to first edge delay
value from 0 to 2 is the number of spi clock half period between the Transfer start and the first clock edge.

bits.name: do_delay
bits.comment:
Transfer start to first data out delay
value from 0 to 2 is the number of spi clock half period between the Transfer start and the first data out.

bits.name: di_delay
bits.comment:
Transfer start to first data in sampled delay
value from 0 to 3 is the number of spi clock half period between the Transfer start and the first data sampled in.
The DI_Delay only specify the sampling time, for frame size, the counter is based on the DO_Delay even in DigRF read mode.

bits.name: cs_delay
bits.comment:
Transfer start to CS activation delay
value from 0 to 3 is the number of spi clock half period between the Transfer start and the CS activation edge.

bits.name: cs_end_hold
bits.comment:
Transfer end to chip select deactivation delay
value from 0 to 3 is the number of spi clock half period between the end of transfer (DO) and the CS deactivation edge.
Not used for Clocked_Back2Back mode

bits.name: frame_size
bits.comment:
Number of data in the frame, or number of out data in DigRF read mode.
The actual frame size is the value of this register + 1; valid value are 3 to 31 (frame size 4 to 32bits)
The frame size is given for the number of data, the actual number of clock pulses might be greater. First if Clock_Delay < DO_Delay an extra clock pulse is generated, second in case of DigRF read or back2back, some more clock pulses will be generated.

bits.name: cs_end_pulse
bits.comment:
Chip select deactivation to new start of transfer minimum delay
value from 0 to 3 is the number of spi clock half period between the CS deactivation and a new transfer start (transfer will start only if more data are available in the transmit FIFO)
Not used for Clocked_Back2Back mode

bits.name: input_frame_size
bits.comment:
Frame Size For Input in DigRF input mode
The actual frame size is the value of this register + 1; valid value are 3 to 31 (frame size 4 to 32bits)

bits.name: turnaround_time
bits.comment:
TurnAround time: end of write frame to start of read frame delay (in cycles)
value from 0 to 3 is the number of spi clock period between the end of the output frame (without the DO_Delay) and the Input Frame start.
Also used for Clocked_Back2Back mode, when Clocked_Back2Back=1 and there is more data available in the transmit FIFO:
value from 0 to 3 is the number of spi clock period between the end of the frame (without the DO_Delay) and the start of the new frame. (It can also be seen as the number of spi clock period between the end of the last data bit and the start of the new data bit.)

bits.name: active_status
bits.comment:
The SPI activity status
1 = A transfer is in progress
0 = The transfer is done

bits.name: error_cmd
bits.comment:
Error status
1 = a new command (or gain) has been requested while a command was in progress.
0 = No error
Write 1 to clear.

bits.name: table_ovf
bits.comment:
The Gain Table overflow status.
1 = Too many data has been written in the table
Writing a 1 clear the overflow status.

bits.name: table_udf
bits.comment:
The Gain Table underflow status.
1 = a next gain request has been received while the read pointer was already at the top of the table.
Writing a '1' clear the underflow status.

bits.name: cmd_level
bits.comment: Command FIFO level, number of command in the FIFO

bits.name: cmd_ovf
bits.comment:
The command FIFO overflow status.
1 = Too many data has been written in the FIFO
Writing a 1 clear the overflow status.

bits.name: cmd_udf
bits.comment:
The command FIFO underflow status.
1 = Data has been requested to read while the FIFO was empty
Writing a 1 clear the underflow status.

bits.name: cmd_data_level
bits.comment: Command FIFO level, number of bytes in the FIFO

bits.name: cmd_data_ovf
bits.comment:
The command data FIFO overflow status.
1 = Too many data has been written in the FIFO
Writing a 1 clear the overflow status.

bits.name: cmd_data_udf
bits.comment:
The command data FIFO underflow status.
1 = Data has been requested to read while the FIFO was empty
Writing a 1 clear the underflow status.

bits.name: rx_level
bits.comment: Receive FIFO level, number of bytes in the FIFO

bits.name: rx_ovf
bits.comment:
The receive FIFO overflow status.
1 = Too many data has been written in the FIFO
Writing a 1 clear the overflow status.

bits.name: rx_udf
bits.comment:
The receive FIFO underflow status.
1 = Data has been requested to read while the FIFO was empty
Writing a 1 clear the underflow status.

bits.name: rx_data
bits.comment:
Read in the receive FIFO
Writing this register will write to Cmd_Data fifo (same as Cmd_Data register). This is because this address is used by the IFC channels to access the fifos.

bits.name: send_cmd
bits.comment: Writing 1 send the next command in the Cmd FIFO (This replace the TCU next cmd signal)

bits.name: flush_cmd_fifo
bits.comment: Writing 1 flush both Cmd, and cmd_data FIFO, don't do it when SPI is active (transfer in progress)

bits.name: flush_rx_fifo
bits.comment: Writing 1 flush the receive data FIFO, don't do it when SPI is active (transfer in progress)

bits.name: restart_gain
bits.comment: Writing 1 place the read pointer at the beginning of the gain table. don't do it when SPI is active (transfer in progress)

bits.name: reload_gain
bits.comment: Writing 1 place the write pointer at the beginning of the gain table allowing to fill the table.

bits.name: drive_zero
bits.comment: Writing 1 change all the ouputs of the SPI interface to drive a logical '0'. This mode stops when a new command is requested to be send (by TCU) or when writting 0 to this register. This mode is useful when powering off the tranciever chip connected to the RF_SPI.

bits.name: cmd_size
bits.comment: Write the size in bytes of the next command in the FIFO

bits.name: cmd_mark
bits.comment:
Write 1 to mark the command.
Marked commands are discarded if Enable_Rf_Spi_Marked_Cmd is low in the tcu register.

bits.name: cmd_data
bits.comment: Write in the Command data FIFO

bits.name: gain_size
bits.comment: Size of a Gain command in bytes.

bits.name: gain_data
bits.comment: Write in the Gain Table (the pointer auto increments)

bits.name: cmd_data_dma_done_cause
bits.comment:
Cmd_Data_DMA_Done IRQ Cause bit
1 = the IRQ was triggered by the end of the DMA transfer to the cmd FIFO.
To clear it write 1 in this bit or Cmd_Data_DMA_Done_Status bit.

bits.name: cmd_fifo_empty_cause
bits.comment:
Cmd_FIFO_empty IRQ Cause bit
1 = the IRQ was triggered because the Cmd_FIFO is empty.
To clear it, fill the FIFO.

bits.name: cmd_threshold_cause
bits.comment:
Cmd_Threshold IRQ Cause bit
1 = the IRQ was triggered because the Cmd_FIFO level is below the Cmd_Threshold.
To clear it, fill the FIFO.

bits.name: rx_fifo_full_cause
bits.comment:
Rx_FIFO_full IRQ Cause bit
1 = the IRQ was triggered because the Rx_Data_FIFO is full.
To clear it, read from the FIFO.

bits.name: rx_threshold_cause
bits.comment:
Rx_Threshold IRQ Cause bit
1 = the IRQ was triggered because the Rx_Data_FIFO level is over the Rx_Threshold.
To clear it, read from the FIFO.

bits.name: error_cause
bits.comment:
Error IRQ Cause bit
1 = the IRQ was triggered because an error occured. Read the Status register to check the kind of error.
To clear it, clear it in the Status register.

bits.name: cmd_data_dma_done_status
bits.comment:
Cmd_Data_DMA_Done IRQ Status bit
1 = the end of the DMA transfer to the cmd FIFO occured.
To clear it write 1 in this bit or Cmd_Data_DMA_Done_Cause bit.

bits.name: cmd_fifo_empty_status
bits.comment:
Cmd_FIFO_empty IRQ Status bit
1 = the Cmd_FIFO is empty.

bits.name: cmd_threshold_status
bits.comment:
Cmd_Threshold IRQ Status bit
1 = the Cmd_FIFO level is bellow the Cmd_Threshold.

bits.name: rx_fifo_full_status
bits.comment:
Rx_FIFO_full IRQ Status bit
1 = the Rx_Data_FIFO is full.

bits.name: rx_threshold_status
bits.comment:
Rx_Threshold IRQ Status bit
1 = the Rx_Data_FIFO level is over the Rx_Threshold.

bits.name: error_status
bits.comment:
Error IRQ Status bit
1 = an error occured. Read the Status register to check the kind of error.

bits.name: cmd_data_dma_done_mask
bits.comment:
Cmd_Data_DMA_Done IRQ Mask bit
1 = the Cmd_Data_DMA_Done IRQ is enabled
0 = the Cmd_Data_DMA_Done IRQ is disabled

bits.name: cmd_fifo_empty_mask
bits.comment:
Cmd_FIFO_empty IRQ Mask bit
1 = the Cmd_FIFO_empty IRQ is enabled
0 = the Cmd_FIFO_empty IRQ is disabled

bits.name: cmd_threshold_mask
bits.comment:
Cmd_Threshold IRQ Mask bit
1 = the Cmd_Threshold IRQ is enabled
0 = the Cmd_Threshold IRQ is disabled

bits.name: rx_fifo_full_mask
bits.comment:
Rx_FIFO_full IRQ Mask bit
1 = the Rx_FIFO_full IRQ is enabled
0 = the Rx_FIFO_full IRQ is disabled

bits.name: rx_threshold_mask
bits.comment:
Rx_Threshold IRQ Mask bit
1 = the Rx_Threshold IRQ is enabled
0 = the Rx_Threshold IRQ is disabled

bits.name: error_mask
bits.comment:
Error IRQ Mask bit
1 = the Error IRQ is enabled
0 = the Error IRQ is disabled

bits.name: cmd_threshold
bits.comment: Command FIFO Threshold, number of command in the FIFO bellow which the Cmd_Threshold_IRQ is triggered.

bits.name: rx_threshold
bits.comment: Receive FIFO Threshold, number of bytes in the FIFO above which the Rx_Threshold_IRQ is triggered.

bits.name: divider
bits.comment:
Clock Divider
The state machine clock is generated by dividing the system clock by the value of this register + 1. So the output clock is divided by (register + 1)*2

bits.name: clock_limiter
bits.comment:
When enabled the clock input to the divider is not the system clock, but a limited version of it: It cannot be above 52MHz, so the output clock will never be above 26MHz.
for system clock of 104Mhz the clock input to the divider is 52Mhz, for system clock of 78Mhz the clock input to the divider is 39Mhz, for lower system clock value, the input to the divider is the system clock.

bits.name: ch_to_use
bits.comment:
This field indicates which standard channel to use.
Before using a channel, the CPU read this register to know which channel must be used. After reading this registers, the channel is to be regarded as busy.
After reading this register, if the CPU doesn't want to use the specified channel, the CPU must write a disable in the control register of the channel to release the channel.
0000 = use Channel0
0001 = use Channel1
0010 = use Channel2
...
0111 = use Channel7
1111 = all channels are busy

bits.name: ch_enable
bits.comment:
This register indicates which channel is enabled. It is a copy of the enable bit of the control register of each channel. One bit per channel, for example:
0000_0000 = All channels disabled
0000_0001 = Ch0 enabled
0000_0010 = Ch1 enabled
0000_0100 = Ch2 enabled
0000_0101 = Ch0 and Ch2 enabled
0000_0111 = Ch0, Ch1 and Ch2 enabled
1111_1111 = all channels enabled

bits.name: ch_busy
bits.comment: This register indicates which standard channel is busy (this field doesn't include the RF_SPI channel). A standard channel is mark as busy, when a channel is enabled or a previous reading of the GET_CH register, the field CH_TO_USE indicates this channel. One bit per channel

bits.name: dbg_status
bits.comment:
Debug Channel Status .
0= The debug channel is running (not idle)
1= The debug channel is in idle mode

bits.name: enable
bits.comment:
Channel Enable, write one in this bit enable the channel.
When the channel is enabled, for a peripheral to memory transfer the DMA wait request from peripheral to start transfer.

bits.name: disable
bits.comment:
Channel Disable, write one in this bit disable the channel.
When writing one in this bit, the current AHB transfer and current APB transfer (if one in progress) is completed and the channel is then disabled.

bits.name: ch_rd_hw_exch
bits.comment: Exchange the read data from fifo halfword MSB or LSB

bits.name: ch_wr_hw_exch
bits.comment: Exchange the write data to fifo halfword MSB or LSB

bits.name: autodisable
bits.comment:
Set Auto-disable mode
0 = when TC reach zero the channel is not automatically released.
1 = At the end of the transfer when TC reach zero the channel is automatically disabled. the current channel is released.

bits.name: size
bits.comment:
Peripheral Size
0= 8-bit peripheral
1= 32-bit peripheral

bits.name: req_src
bits.comment: Select DMA Request source

bits.name: flush
bits.comment:
When one, flush the internal FIFO channel.
This bit must be used only in case of Rx transfer. Until this bit is 1, the APB request is masked. The flush doesn't release the channel.
Before writting back this bit to zero the internal fifo must empty.

bits.name: max_burst_length
bits.comment:
Set the MAX burst length for channel 0,1. This bit field is only used in channel 0~1, for channel 2~6, it is reserved.
The 2'b10 mean burst max 16 2'b01 mean burst max 8, 00 mean burst max 4.
.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment: Enable bit, when '1' the channel is running

bits.name: fifo_empty
bits.comment: The internal channel fifo is empty

bits.name: start_addr
bits.comment:
AHB Address. This field represent the start address of the transfer.
For a 32-bit peripheral, this address must be aligned 32-bit.

bits.name: tc
bits.comment:
Transfer Count, this field indicated the transfer size in bytes to perform.
During a transfer a write in this register add the new value to the current TC.
A read of this register return the current current transfer count.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment:
Channel Enable, write one in this bit enable the channel.
This channel works only in fifo mode.

bits.name: disable
bits.comment: Channel Disable, write one in this bit to disable the channel.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment: Enable bit, when '1' the channel is running

bits.name: fifo_empty
bits.comment: The internal channel fifo is empty

bits.name: fifo_level
bits.comment: Internal fifo level

bits.name: start_ahb_addr
bits.comment:
AHB Start Address.
This field represent the start address of the fifo. The start address must 32-bit aligned.

bits.name: end_ahb_addr
bits.comment:
AHB End Address.
This field represent the last address of the fifo (it is the first address not used in the fifo).
The end address must 32-bit aligned.

bits.name: tc
bits.comment:
Transfer Count, transfer size in bytes.
This bit indicated the transfer size in bytes to perform. Up to 16kbytes per transfer.
During a transfer a write in this register add the new value to the current TC. A read of this register return the current current transfer count.

bits.name: sel_clk_tcu_gsm
bits.comment:
0: sel 26MHz clock.
1: sel 32KHz clock.

bits.name: sel_clk_tcu_nb
bits.comment:
0: sel 61.44MHz clock.
1: sel 32KHz clock.

bits.name: snap_config_gsm
bits.comment: Number of snapshot.

bits.name: snap_config_nb
bits.comment: Number of snapshot.

bits.name: snapshot_gsm
bits.comment: Value of snapshots, snapshot value is automatically incremented at frame interrupt. This snapshot counter wrap at the value given by Snapshot_Cfg.

bits.name: snapshot_nb
bits.comment: Value of snapshots, snapshot value is automatically incremented at frame interrupt. This snapshot counter wrap at the value given by Snapshot_Cfg.

reg.name: soft_rst_gge
reg.comment:
0: low active, assert reset.
1: high inactive, deassert reset.

reg.name: ip_clk_disable_gge
reg.comment:
0: not disable ip_* clock.
1: disable ip_* clock.

reg.name: dbg_disable_acg_hclk
reg.comment:
0: enable hclk_* auto clock gating.
1: disable hclk_* auto clock gating.

reg.name: dbg_disable_acg_pclk
reg.comment:
0: enable pclk_* auto clock gating.
1: disable pclk_* auto clock gating.

reg.name: dbg_disable_acg_clk
reg.comment:
0: enable pclk_* and clk_* auto clock gating.
1: disable pclk_* and clk_* auto clock gating.

bits.name: cfg_ram
bits.comment: cfg ram.

bits.name: dbgmux_sel
dump_ctrl
bits.comment:
select rfif dump signal.
0: dfe_dump_data
1: dfe_rx_data
2: dfe_tx_data
deault: dfe_dump_data

bits.name: bcpu_cache_disable_reg
bits.comment: when bcpu is sleep, can disable bcpu cache mem.

bits.name: autodisable_cache_h
bits.comment: when bcpu not use cache, can disable bcpu cache mem.

entry.name: Clr_TCO_0
entry.comment:
Clear TCO 0 : set the TCO 0 to the inactive state
To clear TCO n, use event 2*n

entry.name: Set_TCO_0
entry.comment:
Set TCO 0 : set the TCO 0 to the active state
To set TCO n, use event 2*n+1

entry.name: Start_GMSK
entry.comment: starts modulation and output on IQ DAC

bits.name: load_val
bits.comment: Value loaded into the TCU counter when the Load bit is set to 1

bits.name: load
bits.comment:
Writing a 1 to this bit will load the TCU with the TCU loadval value
Writing a 0 has no effect

option.name: Normal
option.comment: Normal Behavior, The programmation area is copied to the active area when the tcu wraps

option.name: Force_Only
option.comment: The programmation area is copied into the active area only when force latch is used

bits.name: wakeup_en
bits.comment:
Writing a 1 to enable run tcu wakeup function in lowpower skip frame
Writing a 0 to disable

bits.name: wrap_val
bits.comment:
TCU counter wrap value.
The TCU counter returns to 0 when this value is reached

bits.name: cur_val
bits.comment: TCU counter current value

bits.name: forcelatch
bits.comment: Writing 1 transfer the programmed events to the active area.

bits.name: force_noevent
bits.comment: Writing 1 to this bit with one of the ForceLatch bit will force the corresponding Active Area to receive no events (i.e. clear it) instead of transfering the programmed area.

bits.name: clearprogarea
bits.comment: Writing 1 clears the Program Area

bits.name: tco_polarity
bits.comment: Configure the TCO polarity

bits.name: write_error
bits.comment:
Error Status: become 1 when writing to Program Area while the TCU is coping the Program Area to the Active Area. In this case the write is ignored.
Write 1 to clear it.

bits.name: debug_active
bits.comment: This bit allows to access directly the active area for debug purposes

option.name: Debug
option.comment: the active area is directly mapped instead of the program area.

bits.name: disable_tco
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the events that affect corresponding TCO.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_internal_tco
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the events that affect corresponding TCO.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_send_spi_cmd
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the events SEND_SPI_CMD.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_next_gain
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the events NEXT_GAIN.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_first_gain
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the events FIRST_GAIN.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_next_fc
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the events NEXT_FC.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_ramp
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the corresponding Ramp event.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_rx_soc
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the events RX_SOC.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_digrf_strobe
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the events DIGRF_STB.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_bcpu_irq
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the corresponding BCPU TCU irq event.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_xcpu_irq
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the corresponding XCPU TCU irq event.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_rfspi_start
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the events RFSPI_START.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_rfspi_end
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the events RFSPI_END.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: disable_rf_spi_marked_cmd
bits.comment:
Writing 1 disable the marked rf spi commands (cf RF SPI).
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_tco
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the events that affect corresponding TCO.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_internal_tco
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the events that affect corresponding TCO.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_send_spi_cmd
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the events SEND_SPI_CMD.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_next_gain
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the events NEXT_GAIN.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_first_gain
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the events FIRST_GAIN.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_next_fc
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the events NEXT_FC.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_ramp
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the corresponding Ramp event.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_rx_soc
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the events RX_SOC.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_digrf_strobe
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the events DIGRF_STB.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_bcpu_irq
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the corresponding BCPU TCU irq event.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_xcpu_irq
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the corresponding XCPU TCU irq event.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_rfspi_start
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the events RFSPI_START.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_rfspi_end
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the events RFSPI_END.
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: enable_rf_spi_marked_cmd
bits.comment:
Writing 1 enable the marked rf spi commands (cf RF SPI).
Reading return the actual enable state.

bits.name: set_tco
bits.comment:
Writing 1 set corresponding TCO to the active state (The actual line state also depends on TCO_Polarity).
Reading returns the actual state of all TCOs.

bits.name: clr_tco
bits.comment:
Writing 1 set corresponding TCO to the inactive state (The actual line state also depends on TCO_Polarity).
Reading returns the actual state of all TCOs.

bits.name: tcu_clk_same_sys
bits.comment: Enable Clk_TCU same with Clk_Sys.

bits.name: enable_dai_simple_208k
bits.comment: Enable the 208kHz pulse generation for DAI Simple. (!) When enabling the clock field Enable_Qbit should also be enabled.

bits.name: enable_qbit
bits.comment: Enable the Quarter bit generation (required for normal TCU operation)

bits.name: tcu_sync_done_cause
bits.comment:
1 when the IRQ was triggered because the tcu counter synchronization is done.
Write 1 in cause or status bit to clear.

bits.name: tcu_sync_done_status
bits.comment:
1 when the tcu counter synchronization is done.
Write 1 in cause or status bit to clear.

bits.name: tcu_sync_done_mask
bits.comment: when 1 the LPS_IRQ_TCU_Sync_Done is enabled.

bits.name: tcu_sync_enable
bits.comment: enable sync tcu counter to global counter function.

bits.name: tcu_sync_value
bits.comment: tcu counter load value when synchronized.

bits.name: rfspi_conflict_val
bits.comment: TCU counter value when rfspi conflict happen

bits.name: event_time
bits.comment: The event Id will be executed when the TCU counter reaches the value programmed in Event time field of this register.

bits.name: event_id
bits.comment: Event to be executed when the TCU counter reaches the programmed event time.

bits.name: start_equ
bits.comment: Writing a '1' in this register triggers a Viterbi Equalization process. Ignored if any Viterbi process is already ongoing. Auto-reset.

bits.name: start_dec
bits.comment: Writing a '1' in this register triggers a Viterbi Decoding process. Ignored if any Viterbi process is already ongoing. Auto-reset.

bits.name: start_tb
bits.comment: Writing a '1' in this register triggers the TraceBack process. Ignored if any Viterbi process is already ongoing. Auto-reset.

bits.name: int_mask
bits.comment: When this bit is set, it enables the generation of the VITAC_DONE_H interrupt.

bits.name: punctured
bits.comment: Indicates whether a puncturing scheme has to be used during decoding. If this bit is set to '0', the code is assumed unpunctured and no puncturing matrix is needed.

bits.name: nb_states
bits.comment:
This field sets the number of states of the Trellis:
"00": 16 states
"01": 32 states
"10": 64 states
"11": reserved

bits.name: bkwd_trellis
bits.comment: When this bit is set, the channel symbols are treated in the reverse order, i.e. CH_SYMB_ADDR represents the end of the buffer and the symbols are read out backward.

bits.name: code_rate
bits.comment:
This field sets the convolutional code rate for decoding:
"010": 1/2 rate
"011": 1/3 rate
"100": 1/4 rate
"101": 1/5 rate
"110": 1/6 rate
others: reserved

bits.name: bm_shift_lev
bits.comment:
This field sets the amount of shift right applied at the output of the equalizer BM calculation:
"0000": BM = OUT[30:19]
"0001": BM = OUT[29:18]
...
"1111": BM = OUT[15:4]

bits.name: sv_shift_lev
bits.comment:
This field sets the amount of shift right applied to the difference of the two metrics arriving at a node to create a Softvalue:
"0000": SoftVal = DELTA[15:9]
"0001": SoftVal = DELTA[14:8]
...
"1101": SoftVal = DELTA[2:0]&"0000"
others: reserved

bits.name: nb_symbols
bits.comment: Number of symbols to be Equalized / Decoded. Auto decrement.

bits.name: equ_pending
bits.comment: This bit is high when an equalization process is ongoing. It stays high when the module is stalled during operation.

bits.name: dec pending
bits.comment: This bit is high when an decoding process is ongoing. It stays high when the module is stalled during operation.

bits.name: tb_pending
bits.comment: This bit is high when an traceback process is ongoing. It stays high when the module is stalled during operation.

bits.name: nb_rescales
bits.comment:
After a Viterbi process, this field reports the number of rescaling operations that have been performed along the trellis.
This field is reset at every new Viterbi process.

bits.name: addr
bits.comment:
This is the start address of the channel symbols buffer in SRAM. For Equalization channel symbols are the sampled RF samples (2x12-bits packed complex values), and for Decoding channel symbols are a frame of softvalues (4x8-bits packed).
This address must be 4-bytes aligned, bits[1:0] will be ignored.

bits.name: addr
bits.comment:
For Equalization, this is the base address of the partial sum terms buffer in SRAM. (2x12-bits packed complex values)
For Decoding, this is the base address of the puncturing matrix.
This address must be 4-bytes aligned, bits[1:0] will be ignored.

bits.name: addr
bits.comment:
This is the base address in SRAM of the Path Metrics buffer. The VITAC will read and update PMs according to the scheme given in 1.2.1.2. (2x16-bits packed values).
This address must be 4-bytes aligned, bits[1:0] will be ignored.

bits.name: addr
bits.comment:
This is the start address of the output buffer in SRAM. When in Equalizer mode, the VITAC will output the calculated Softvalues according to the scheme given in 1.2.1.7. When in Decoder mode, the VITAC will output the trace words according to the scheme given in 1.2.2.4.
This address must be 4-bytes aligned, bits[1:0] will be ignored.

bits.name: h0_i_part
bits.comment: Real part of the h0 parameter of the estimated channel response.

bits.name: h0_q_part
bits.comment: Imaginary part of the h0 parameter of the estimated channel response.

bits.name: hl_i_part
bits.comment: Real part of the hL parameter of the estimated channel response.

bits.name: hl_q_part
bits.comment: Imaginary part of the hL parameter of the estimated channel response.

bits.name: threshold
bits.comment: This field indicates the threshold value to be reach by every PMs for triggering a rescale operation. The rescale operation consist in subtracting the threshold value to every PMs to avoid overflow during PM update.

reg.name: res_poly
reg.comment: This register bank stores the less significant bit of the output from the coder for a particular code (see 1.2.2.1). The kth butterfly uses the bit k of this register.

bits.name: res_poly
bits.comment: This register stores the less significant bit of the output from the coder for a particular code (see 1.2.2.1). The kth butterfly uses the bit k of this register.

bits.name: it_cause
bits.comment:
This bit is set when the VITAC module finishes an ongoing operation. It can be masked by setting VITAC_CMD(IT_MASK) to '1'.
Resetting this bit is done by writing in IT_CLEAR register.
IT_CAUSE is the image of the VITAC_DONE_H interrupt line to the CPU.

bits.name: it_status
bits.comment: This bit is the unmasked version of the IT_CAUSE bit.

bits.name: it_clear
bits.comment: Setting this bit to '1' resets the VITAC interrupt.

bits.name: count_value_0
bits.comment: Count Value for 1st TimeOut

bits.name: count_value_1
bits.comment: Count Value for 2nd TimeOut

bits.name: mode
bits.comment:
Watchdog response mode.
0 = Generate a system reset.
1 = First generate an interrupt and if it is not cleared by the time a second timeout occurs then generate a system reset.

bits.name: reset_length
bits.comment:
Reset pulse length in number of wdt clock cycles. The range of values available is 1 to 8 clk cycles.
3'b000 - 1 clk cycle
3'b001 - 2 clk cycles
3'b010 - 3 clk cycles
...
3'b111 - 8 clk cycles

bits.name: cmd
bits.comment:
This register is used to restart/stop the WDT counter. As a safety feature to prevent accidental restarts/stops, write 8'h76 to restart and 8'h34 to stop.
When written is done, this register is self-cleared on the next clock cycle. Reading this register always returns zero.

bits.name: int_clr
bits.comment:
A pulse to clear interrupt.
When written is done, this register is self-cleared on the next clock cycle. Reading this register always returns zero.

bits.name: wdt_active
bits.comment:
This register shows the word status of the WDT.
0 = The watchdog counter is idle/stopped.
1 = The watchdog counter runs.

bits.name: int_assert
bits.comment:
This register shows the interrupt status of the WDT.
0 = Interrupt is inactive.
1 = Interrupt asserts.

bits.name: biterr_en
bits.comment: Enables the Biterror calculation mode. Auto-reset.

bits.name: dco1p_en
bits.comment: Enables the DC Offset Correction (1st pass) mode. Auto-reset.

bits.name: dco2p_en
bits.comment: Enables the DC Offset Correction (2nd pass) mode. Auto-reset.

bits.name: dco3p_en
bits.comment: Enables the DC Offset Correction (3rd pass) mode. Auto-reset.

bits.name: tscxc_en
bits.comment: Enables the Training Sequence Cross-Correlation mode. Auto-reset.

bits.name: srec_en
bits.comment: Enables the Symbol Re-Construction mode. Auto-reset.

bits.name: bext_en
bits.comment: Enables the Bit Extraction mode. Auto-reset.

bits.name: sproc_en
bits.comment: Enables the Sum Of PROduCt mode. Auto-reset.

bits.name: chest_en
bits.comment: Enables the Channel Estimation mode. Auto-reset.

bits.name: fchxc_en
bits.comment: Enables the FCH Xcorrelation mode. Auto-reset.

bits.name: sldwin_en
bits.comment: Enables the Sliding window mode. Auto-reset.

bits.name: it_mask
bits.comment: Mask of the end of processing interrupt.

bits.name: pack_iq
bits.comment: Data path setting. Pack I and Q on a single 32-bits word.

bits.name: derotation_en
bits.comment: Data path setting. Enables derotation for DCOC 3pass.

bits.name: nb_iloop
bits.comment: Control setting. Number of internal loop iteration.

bits.name: nb_symb
bits.comment: Control setting. Number of symbols to process.

bits.name: op_pending
bits.comment: This bit is high when an operation is ongoing.

bits.name: it_cause
bits.comment: Masked version of it_status that goes to Interrupt controller.

bits.name: it_status
bits.comment: This bit is set high when an operation is finished. It must be reset before lauching a new operation if Xcor interrupt is enabled.

reg.name: hv0
reg.comment:
Multipurpose Data Register.
Store Training Sequence in TSXC mode.
Store SUM in DCOC 3rd pass mode.
Store bit sequence in SREC mode.
Store SUM in SPROC mode.
Store I SUM in CHEST mode.
Store R(k-1) in FCHXC mode.

bits.name: hv0
bits.comment: Multipurpose.

reg.name: hv1
reg.comment:
Multipurpose Data Register.
Store Training Sequence in TSXC mode.
Store bit sequence in SREC mode.
Store Q SUM in CHEST mode.

bits.name: hv1
bits.comment: Multipurpose.

reg.name: data
reg.comment:
Multipurpose Data Registers.
D0 stores symbols/softvalues/channel taps depending on mode. Not readable.
D1 stores decoded bits/IQ threshols/IQ Offsets/A terms depending on mode. Not readable.
D2 (aka A1) serves as Rd address (decoded bits, A or B terms) / Wr address register (I or packed IQ results, Symbols) / event counter depending on mode.
D3 (aka A2) serves as Wr address (Q results) / event counter depending on mode.
D4 stores results from VITAC / extracted HardValues depending on mode. Not readable.
D5 (aka A3) serves as Wr address (CQ results) Not readable.

bits.name: data
bits.comment: Multipurpose.

bits.name: accui
bits.comment: I part accumulator register.

bits.name: accuq
bits.comment: I part accumulator register.

reg.name: addr0
reg.comment:
Address 0 Register.
Stores Rd address for symbols / SoftValues / A terms depending on mode.
Auto increment/decrement/reset.

bits.name: addr0
bits.comment: 32-bit word address (bits 0 and 1 disregarded).

reg.name: data_e
reg.comment: Multipurpose Data Edge Registers.

bits.name: data
bits.comment: Multipurpose.

bits.name: rf0_addr
bits.comment: program counter for the RF stage.

option.name: AdEL
option.comment: Address error exception (load or instruction fetch)

option.name: DBE
option.comment: Bus error exception (data reference: load or store)

bits.name: cp0_cause_ip_soft
bits.comment: Theses interrupt lines are software interrupts (the cpu can write in the CP0 bits to trigger and clear them).

bits.name: cp0_cause_ip_ext
bits.comment: Theses interrupt lines maps to the hardware interrupt lines from the corresponding irq module.

bits.name: cp0_cause_ce
bits.comment: The Coprocessor Error (CE) field indicate the coprocessor unit number referenced when a Coprocessor Unusable exception is taken.

bits.name: cp0_cause_bd
bits.comment: The Branch Delay (BD) bit indicate whether the last exception was taken while executing in a branch delay slot.

bits.name: cp0_status_iec
bits.comment: Current Interrupt Enable

bits.name: cp0_status_kuc
bits.comment: Current Kernel/User mode

bits.name: cp0_status_iep
bits.comment: Previous Interrupt Enable

bits.name: cp0_status_kup
bits.comment: Previous Kernel/User mode

bits.name: cp0_status_ieo
bits.comment: Old Interrupt Enable

bits.name: cp0_status_kuo
bits.comment: Old Kernel/User mode

bits.name: cp0_status_intmask
bits.comment: Interrupt Mask control the enabling of each of the external and software interrupts. (See Cause for more information on interruptions).

bits.name: cp0_streaming_disable
bits.comment: This bit control handling of non-cached instruction fetch requests. By default, the system block reads multiple words of data from the AMBA bus in burst transactions and saves them in the Streaming Buffer. Non cached instruction fetch requests get their data directly from the Streaming Buffer. When "1" the cpu does not use the streaming buffer and does not ask for burst requests on the AMBA bus for non-cache instruction fetch requests.

bits.name: cp0_status_cm
bits.comment:
Cache Miss
Signals that the most recent access to the cachable space resulted in cache miss.

bits.name: cp0_status_ts
bits.comment: Signals that 2 entries in the TLB matched the virtual address. This is an error condition but the processor takes no action other than signalling it via this bit in the Status Register.

bits.name: cp0_status_bev
bits.comment: Select the location of the exception vectors in ROM or in DRAM.

bits.name: cp0_status_re
bits.comment: Reverse Endian in User mode. (probably unused in xcpu)

bits.name: cp0_status_cu_0
bits.comment: Control the Usability of the corresponding Coprocessor Unit. (CP0 is always usable when in Kernel mode, regardless of the setting of the CU_0 bit.

bits.name: cp0_status_cu_123
bits.comment: Control the Usability of the corresponding Coprocessor Unit.

bits.name: cp0_epc
bits.comment: Exception Program Counter. Saves the value of the program counter for the instruction that caused the exception.

bits.name: cp0_badvaddr
bits.comment: Bad virtual address. Saves the address that caused the address exception.

bits.name: cp0_depc
bits.comment: Exception Program Counter. Saves the value of the program counter for the instruction that caused the exception by break point instruction.

bits.name: at
bits.comment: assembler temporary register; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: v0
bits.comment:
Used for expression evaluations and for hold integer function results.
Also used to pass the statuc link when calling nested procedure.

bits.name: v1
bits.comment:
Used for expression evaluations and for hold integer function results.
Also used to pass the statuc link when calling nested procedure.

bits.name: a0
bits.comment: register A0 to A3 is used to pass the first 4 words of integer type actual arguments; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: a1
bits.comment: register A0 to A3 is used to pass the first 4 words of integer type actual arguments; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: a2
bits.comment: register A0 to A3 is used to pass the first 4 words of integer type actual arguments; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: a3
bits.comment: register A0 to A3 is used to pass the first 4 words of integer type actual arguments; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: t0
bits.comment: temporary register, used for expression evaluations; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: t1
bits.comment: temporary register, used for expression evaluations; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: t2
bits.comment: temporary register, used for expression evaluations; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: t3
bits.comment: temporary register, used for expression evaluations; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: t4
bits.comment: temporary register, used for expression evaluations; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: t5
bits.comment: temporary register, used for expression evaluations; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: t6
bits.comment: temporary register, used for expression evaluations; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: t7
bits.comment: temporary register, used for expression evaluations; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: s0
bits.comment: saved register; their values must preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: s1
bits.comment: saved register; their values must preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: s2
bits.comment: saved register; their values must preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: s3
bits.comment: saved register; their values must preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: s4
bits.comment: saved register; their values must preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: s5
bits.comment: saved register; their values must preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: s6
bits.comment: saved register; their values must preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: s7
bits.comment: saved register; their values must preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: t8
bits.comment: temporary register, used for expression evaluations; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: t9
bits.comment: temporary register, used for expression evaluations; their values are not preserved across procedure calls.

bits.name: k0
bits.comment: reserved for the operating system kernal.

bits.name: k1
bits.comment: reserved for the operating system kernal.

bits.name: gp
bits.comment: contains the global pointer.

bits.name: sp
bits.comment: contains the stack pointer.

bits.name: s8
bits.comment: a saved register (like s0-s7).

bits.name: ra
bits.comment: contains the return address; used for expression evaluation.

bits.name: debug_page_address
bits.comment:
Debug Page Address Register Is a 4 bit register used for extending the address of the debug to enable full access to the cache RAMs.
bit 3 is used when accessing the TAGs to select between Instruction TAG (0) or Data TAG (1).

bits.name: dcache_inhibit
bits.comment: when "ON" all accesses for data are treated as non cache. Data is fetched directly from main memory. The content of the Data Cache is not altered.

bits.name: icache_inhibit
bits.comment: when "ON" all accesses for instructions are treated as non cache. Data is fetched directly from main memory. The content of the cache is not altered.

bits.name: cache hit disable
bits.comment: when "ON" all accesses to either Instruction or data caches result in a cache miss and a cache refill. This is a quick way to initialize the caches.

reg.name: ctrl
reg.comment: logic analyzer control register

bits.name: run
bits.comment:
run control.
0 ela-500 disabled. register programming permitted.
1 ela-500 enabled.

reg.name: timectrl
reg.comment: timestamp control register

bits.name: tsen
bits.comment: timestamp enable.

bits.name: tsint
bits.comment:
timestamp interval.
when timestamps are enabled, tsint specifies the bit number of the 16-bit trace counter that causes a timestamp packet to be requested. the trace counter runs from elaclk. when the specified bit changes, a timestamp packet is requested to be inserted into the trace sram when there is an elaclk cycle during which trace data is not being captured. the ela-500 does not insert back-to-back timestamps in the sram, even when tsint causes multiple requests to be made.
when tsint = 0, a timestamp is written when action.trace disables trace. looping trigger states enable and then disable trace, causing timestamp writes. a timestamp is always written when ctrl.run is cleared and the previous trace write contained a data payload.

bits.name: tcsel1
bits.comment:
trace counter 1 select.
selects the bit number of the 16-bit trace counter that is presented as trace counter[1] in the sram header byte.

bits.name: tcsel0
bits.comment:
trace counter 0 select.
selects the bit number of the 16-bit trace counter that is presented as trace counter[0] in the sram header byte.

bits.comment:

altts[4]=1 trigger state 4 independent trace enabled.
all other bits read zero.

reg.comment: read captured transaction id register

bits.name: rdcaptid
bits.comment: returns the captured transaction id.

reg.name: rrar
reg.comment: ram read address register

bits.name: rra
bits.comment:
ram read address.
writes to the rra cause the trace sram data at that address to be transferred into the holding register.
after the sram read data is transferred to the holding register, rra increments by one. this prepares the rra address for sequential rrdr reads.
the rra automatically increments after apb reads from the rrdr have read the contents of the holding register. an rrdr read of the last data in the holding register initiates a read to sram at the address pointed to by the rra. the holding register is filled with the data at this address, then the rra increments.

reg.name: rrdr
reg.comment: ram read data register

bits.name: rrd
bits.comment:
reads sram data from the holding register.
reads from the rrd return the sram data from the holding register. the first read of the rrd after an rrar update returns the trace data header byte value, zero-extended to 32 bits. subsequent reads of the rrd return 32-bit chunks of the trace data payload, starting with the least significant word, until all the payload data has been read, that is, two words if grp_width = 64, four words if grp_width = 128, and eight words if grp_width = 256.
when the final 32 bits of the payload have been read, the rra is incremented automatically, and the next word of sram data is copied into the holding register. this enables the sram data content to be read out efficiently.
the rra wraps to address zero if it is incremented beyond the maximum depth of the sram.

reg.name: rwar
reg.comment: ram write address register

bits.name: wrap
bits.comment:
the wrap bit is set when the ram write address is incremented beyond 2ram_addr_size while
the ela-500 is capturing trace data. the wrap bit is not set by writes to the rwdr that cause the
ram write address to roll over. software must clear the wrap bit when writing to the rwar.

bits.name: rwa
bits.comment:
ram write address.
writes to the rwa set the sram address for data that is then written through the rwdr.
reads from the rwa return the address of the sram location that is to be written next, either by writes to the rwdr, or by the trace unit.
when trace is stopped, the rwa contains the address of the last sram location that was written plus one. if the ram write address was incremented beyond the depth of the ram while the ela-500 was capturing trace data, the wrap bit is set.
the rwar is automatically incremented by apb writes to the sram through the rwdr.

reg.name: rwdr
reg.comment: ram write data register

bits.name: rwdr
bits.comment:
writes data to the write holding register and initiates an sram write when the write holding register is full. writes to the rwd update the internal write holding register.
the first write to the rwd sets the header byte value from the least significant byte written. subsequent writes to the rwd set 32-bit chunks of the payload, starting with the least significant chunk. when the final 32 bits of the payload have been written, the content of the holding register is copied into the sram and the rwa is incremented automatically.

bits.comment:
selects signal group.

reg.comment: trigger control registers

bits.name: altcompsel
bits.comment:
selects the alternative comparison mode:
0b0 trigger signal alternative comparisons selected.
0b1 trigger counter alternative comparisons selected.

bits.name: altcomp
bits.comment:
trigger signal alternative comparison type select:
0b000 trigger signal alternative comparisons disabled.
0b001 alternative compare type is equal (==).
0b010 alternative compare type is greater than (>).
0b011 alternative compare type is greater than or equal (>=).
0b101 alternative compare type is not equal (!=).
0b110 alternative compare type is less than (<).
0b111 alternative compare type is less than or equal (<=).

bits.name: captid
bits.comment:
0b00 disable use of the captured id for signal comparisons.
0b01 capture id when trigger signal condition matches. the id is captured, from signalgrp[id_capture_size-1:0].
0b10 use the captured id instead of the target value in sigcomp[id_capture_size-1:0] for comparison of signalgrp[id_capture_size-1:0].
0b11 use the captured id instead of the signalgrp[id_capture_size-1:0] for a comparison against sigcomp[id_capture_size-1:0].

bits.name: countbrk
bits.comment:
loop counter break.
the loop counter break uses the trigger state counter to break loops between trigger states after a trigger counter comparison. when the counter comparison matches, the trigger state goes to a final state, which stops trace writes and leaves the output actions at the previous trigger state action value.
0b0 normal operation.
0b1 break trigger state loop: a counter comparison match causes a transition to the final state, otherwise go to the nextstate trigger state as the counter increments.

bits.name: countclr
bits.comment:
counter clear.
0b0 do not clear the counter value when moving to a different nextstate.
0b1 clear the counter value when moving to a different nextstate.
note: trigctrl.watchrst must be 0b0 when using this feature.

bits.name: trace
bits.comment:
trace capture control.
0b00 trace is captured when trigger signal comparison succeeds.
0b01 trace is captured when trigger counter comparison succeeds.
0b10 trace is captured every elaclk cycle.
0b11 reserved.

bits.name: countsrc
bits.comment:
counter source select.
0b0 counter is incremented every elaclk cycle.
0b1 counter is incremented when trigger signal comparison matches.

bits.name: watchrst
bits.comment:
counter reset.
0b0 do not reset the counter after a trigger signal comparison match.
0b1 reset the counter after a trigger signal comparison match.
the counter acts like an activity watchdog timer, only allowing advancement to the next trigger state when the trigger counter comparison is reached. the counter is reset by a signal comparison.

bits.name: compsel
bits.comment:
comparison mode. acts as both a counter enable and a select for the comparison mode.
0b0 disable counters and select trigger signal comparison mode.
0b1 enable counters and select trigger counter comparison mode.

bits.name: comp
bits.comment:
trigger signal comparison type select.
0b000 trigger signal comparisons disabled. the enabled counters count clocks immediately after the trigger state has been entered and generate a programmable output action and transition to the next trigger state when the counter compare register count is reached, that is when a trigger counter comparison match occurs.
0b001 compare type is equal (==).
0b010 compare type is greater than (>).
0b011 compare type is greater than or equal (>=).
0b101 compare type is not equal (!=).
0b110 compare type is less than (<).
0b111 compare type is less than or equal (<=).

0x1 selects trigger state 0.
0x2 selects trigger state 1.
0x4 selects trigger state 2.
0x8 selects trigger state 3.
0x10 selects trigger state 4, when num_trig_states=5.

Returns 1 and locks the DMA channel for a transaction if it is available. Else returns 0.
Clear the transfer done interrupt status.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment: Status of the DMA: 1 if enabled, 0 if disabled.

bits.name: int done cause
bits.comment:
Cause of the interrupt. This bit is set when the transfer is done and the interrupt mask bit is set.
Write one in the Int Clear or write 0 in Enable control bits to clear Int Done Cause bit.

bits.name: int done status
bits.comment:
Status of the interrupt. Status of the transfer: 1 if the transfer is finished, 0 if it is not finished.
Write one in the Int Clear or write 0 in Enable control bits to clear Int Done Status bit.

bits.name: channel lock
bits.comment: Actual status of channel lock. Channel is unlocked at the end of transaction or when the DMA is disabled.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment: Controls the DMA. Write 1 to enable the DMA, write 0 to disable it. When 0 is written in this register, the Int Done Status and Cause bits are reset.

bits.name: int done mask
bits.comment: End of transfer interrupt generation. When 1, the DMA will send an interrupt at transaction completion.

bits.name: int done clear
bits.comment:
Clear the transfer done interruption (this will clear Int Done Status and Int Done Cause).
This bit is auto-clear. You will always read 0 here.

bits.name: use pattern
bits.comment: If this bit is set, the source address will be ignored and the memory will be fill with the value of the pattern register.

bits.name: max_burst_length
bits.comment:
Set the MAX burst length.
The 2'b10 mean burst max 16, 2'b01 mean burst max 8, 00 mean burst max 4.

bits.name: stop transfer
bits.comment: The DMA stop the current transfer and flush his FIFO (write only bit). When the FIFO is empty and last write performed, the DMA is disabled and available for a next transfer. The number of bytes copied is readable on DMA_XFER_SIZE register.

bits.name: gea enable
bits.comment: Enable Gea process when 1.

bits.name: gea algorithm
bits.comment: This field sets the type of GEA algorithm to process.

bits.name: gea direction
bits.comment: This field selects the Direction in the GEA algorithm.

bits.name: fcs enable
bits.comment: Enable FCS process when 1.

bits.name: dst addr mgt
bits.comment:
Destination address management.
00 : Normal DMA operation, DMA_DST_ADDR register define the destination address.
01 : DMA write address is constant (no incremented) and defined by the DMA_DST_ADDR register. All data write are in 16-bit.
10 : DMA write address is alternatively defined by DMA_DST_ADDR and DMA_SD_DST_ADDR registers. All data write are in 16-bit.
In this configuration, DMA write operation is alternatively:
DMA_DST_ADDR <= DMA_PATTERN register
DMA_SD_DST_ADDR <= Data[DMA_SRC_ADDR]
11 : reserved

bits.name: src address
bits.comment: Source start read byte address. When a transfer is stalled by the Stop_Transfer bit, this register give the next current source address, which is directly the value to re-program to complete the transfer stopped.

bits.name: dst address

bits.name: sd dst address
bits.comment: Second destination address. This register is only used when Dst_Address_Mgt=10.

bits.name: transfer size
bits.comment: Transfer size in bytes. Maximum: 262144 bytes. When a transfer is stopped by the Stop_Transfer bit, this register give the number of remainder bytes to transfer.

bits.name: pattern
bits.comment: Value taken to fill the memory when the configuration bit Use Pattern is set. When the pattern mode is used the destination address must be 32-bit aligned and the transfer size multiple of 4. when Dst_Address_Mgt=10 Pattern is the data written at the address given by the Dst_Address register.

bits.name: rasp_on
bits.comment: Symbol power accumulation enable/disable signal and effective at subframe boundary. 1 : enable 0 : disable

bits.name: rasp_gain
bits.comment: Gain used in shift and saturation of accumulation power value. Bit[3:0] Gain 0000 2^-24 (default) 0001 2^-23 0010 2^-22 0011 2^-21

bits.name: rasp_length
bits.comment: Accumulation length of samples in every symbol. 0: 128 1: 64 2: 32 3: 16

bits.name: rasp_offset
bits.comment: Offset of samples from symbols boundaries which is the start boundary of agc symbol power calculation.

bits.name: rasp_rd_addr
bits.comment: Reading address for DSP to read asp response ram, and this register would auto-increment whenever access the rASP_RD_DATA register PING buffer address: 0~20 PONG buffer address: 21~41

bits.name: rdc_ofs_cfg_data
bits.comment: Bit[27:16]: Q DC offset configuration Bit[11:0]: I DC offset configuration

bits.name: rasp_done_status
bits.comment: Report agc symbol power and DCC done status, write 1 to clear this status

bits.name: rasp_buf_ping_pong_idx
bits.comment: Index bit to indicate which buffer is updated of PING-PONG 1: PONG buffer data is updated 0: PING buffer data is updated

bits.name: rasp_rd_data
bits.comment: Data = mem[rASP_RD_ADDR] which is the ASP response memory data content. The ASP_RD_ADDR would auto increase whenever access this register. ASP response Memory address range is 0-41 Address(0~6,21~27): symbol power, bit[15:0] for symbol 0,2,4,6,8,10,12 and bit[31:16] for symbol 1,3,5,7,9,11,13 Address(7~20,28~41):dc_offset value, bit[15:0] for I and bit[31:16] for Q

bits.name: rfft_fwd_inv
bits.comment: Forward/Inverse FFT transform computing selection

bits.name: rfft_buf_idx
rfft_scaling_factor
bits.comment: FFT scaling, it can be implemented by bit shift, 3d0: 2^-3 3d1: 2^-2 3d2: 2^-1 3d3: 2^0 (default) 3d4: 2^1 3d5: 2^2 3d6: 2^3 3d7: 2^4

bits.name: rfft_amp_scaling_factor
bits.comment: FFT_amp_out scaling for amplitude square output, it can be implemented by bit shift, 3d0: 2^-3 3d1: 2^-2 3d2: 2^-1 3d3: 2^0 (default) 3d4: 2^1 3d5: 2^2 3d6: 2^3 3d7: 2^4

bits.name: rfft_amp_cal_en

bits.name: rvd_crcresult_o
bits.comment: CRC checking result of the corresponding code block for output buffer odd, and CRC results from CB0 to CB3 have to be written sequentially to bit[0]~bit[15] of this register. 1: good 0: fail If rVD_CRCMASK_EN =1, 4 bits mask checking result is reported for every candidate CB [31:28] for CB3(28:MASK0, 29:MASK1, 30:MASK2, 31:MASK3) [27:24] for CB2(24:MASK0, 25: MASK1, 26: MASK2, 27: MASK3) [23:20] for CB1(20: MASK0, 21: MASK1, 22: MASK2, 23: MASK3) [19:16] for CB0(16: MASK0, 17: MASK1, 18: MASK2, 19: MASK3) And if rVD_CRCMASK_EN =0, 1 bit crc checking result is reported for every candidate CB [28] for CB3 [24] for CB2 [20] for CB1 [16] for CB0

bits.name: rvd_crcresult_e
bits.comment: CRC check result of the corresponding code block for output buffer even, and CRC results from CB0 to CB3 have to be written sequentially to bit[0]~bit[15] of this register. 1: good 0: fail If rVD_CRCMASK_EN =1, 4 bits mask checking result is reported for every candidate CB [15:12] for CB3(12: MASK0, 13: MASK1, 14: MASK2, 15: MASK3) [11:8] for CB2(8: MASK0, 9: MASK1, 10: MASK2, 11: MASK3) [7:4] for CB1(4: MASK0, 5: MASK1, 6: MASK2, 7: MASK3) [3:0] for CB0(0: MASK0, 1: MASK1, 2: MASK2, 3: MASK3) And if rVD_CRCMASK_EN =0, 1 bit crc checking result is reported for every candidate CB [12] for CB3 [8] for CB2 [4] for CB1 [0] for CB0

bits.name: auto_disable
bits.comment: Automatic channel Disable. When this bit is set, the channel is automatically disabled at the next interrupt.

bits.name: disable
bits.comment: Channel Disable, write one in this bit disable the channel. When writing one in this bit, the current AHB transfer and current APB transfer (if one in progress) is completed and the channel is then disabled.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment: Channel Enable, write one in this bit enable the channel. When the channel is enabled, for a peripheral to memory transfer the DMA wait request from peripheral to start transfer.

bits.name: master_soft_rst
bits.comment: Reset the complete BLE Core except registers and timing generator, when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0. In case of Dual Mode implementation, reset also common blocks.

bits.name: master_tgsoft_rst
bits.comment: Reset the timing generator, when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: reg_soft_rst
bits.comment: Reset the complete register block, when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: swint_req
bits.comment: Forces the generation of ble_sw_irq when written with a 1, and proper masking is set. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: rftest_abort
bits.comment: Abort the current RF Testing defined as per CS-FORMAT when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0. Note that when RFTEST_ABORT is requested 1/ In case of infinite Tx, the Packet Controller FSM stops at the end of the current byte in process, and processes accordingly the packet CRC. 2/ In case of Infinite Rx, the Packet Controller FSM either stops as the end of the current Packet reception (if Access address has been detected), or simply stop the processing switching off the RF.

bits.name: advert_abort
bits.comment: Abort the current Advertising event when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: scan_abort
bits.comment: Abort the current scan window when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: md_dsb
bits.comment: 0: Normal operation of MD bits management 1: Allow a single Tx/Rx exchange whatever the MD bits are. - value forced by SW from Tx Descriptor - value just saved in Rx Descriptor during reception

bits.name: sn_dsb
bits.comment: 0: Normal operation of Sequence number 1: Sequence Number Management disabled: - value forced by SW from Tx Descriptor - value ignored in Rx -> No SN error reported.

bits.name: nesn_dsb
bits.comment: 0: Normal operation of Acknowledge 1: Acknowledge scheme disabled: - value forced by SW from Tx Descriptor - value ignored in Rx -> No NESN error reported.

bits.name: crypt_dsb
bits.comment: 0: Normal operation. Encryption / Decryption enabled. 1: Encryption / Decryption disabled. Note that if CS-CRYPT_EN is set, then MIC is generated, and only data encryption is disabled, meaning data sent are plain data.

bits.name: whit_dsb
bits.comment: 0: Normal operation. Whitening enabled. 1: Whitening disabled.

bits.name: crc_dsb
bits.comment: 0: Normal operation. CRC removed from data stream. 1: CRC stripping disabled on Rx packets, CRC replaced by 0x000 in Tx.

bits.name: hop_remap_dsb
bits.comment: 0: Normal operation. Frequency Hopping Remapping algorithm enabled. 1: Frequency Hopping Remapping algorithm disabled

bits.name: advertfilt_en
bits.comment: Advertising Channels Error Filtering Enable control 0: RW-BLE Core reports all errors to RW-BLE Software 1: RW-BLE Core reports only correctly received packet, without error to RW-BLE Software

bits.name: rwble_en
bits.comment: 0: Disable RW-BLE Core Exchange Table pre-fetch mechanism. 1: Enable RW-BLE Core Exchange table pre-fetch mechanism.

bits.name: rxwinszdef
bits.comment: Default Rx Window size in 2s. Used when device - is master connected - performs its second receipt. 0 is not a valid value. Recommended value is 10 (in decimal).

bits.name: syncerr
bits.comment: Indicates the maximum number of errors allowed to recognize the synchronization word.

bits.name: typ
bits.comment: RW-BLE Core Type C 0x8 means BLE v4.2 (i.e. correspond LL version assigned number). Correspond to FS v8.0.10)

bits.name: rel
bits.comment: RW-BLE Core version C Major release number. Correspond to FS v8.0.10

bits.name: upg
bits.comment: RW-BLE Core upgrade C Upgrade number. Correspond to FS v8.0.10

bits.name: build_num
bits.comment: RW-BLE Core Build C Build number

bits.name: dmmode
bits.comment: 0: RW-BLE Core is used as a standalone BLE device 1: RW-BLE Core is used in a Dual Mode device

bits.name: isoportnb
bits.comment: Number of supported Isochronous Channel (0 to 3) 00: No ISO/Audio Channel available 01: One ISO/Audio Channel available 10: Two ISO/Audio Channels available 11: Three ISO/Audio Channels available

bits.name: decipher
bits.comment: 0: AES deciphering not present 1: AES deciphering present

bits.name: wlancoex
bits.comment: 0: WLAN Coexistence mechanism not present 1: WLAN Coexistence mechanism present (Default Value)

bits.name: rfif
bits.comment: RFIF[k]= 0: Control logic supporting radio k not present RFIF[k]= 1: Control logic supporting radio k present Index k values are: 00001: Ripple RF. 00010: External Radio Controller Support 00100: IcyTRx Radio xxx000: Reserved Default value is 0000001

bits.name: usedbg
bits.comment: 0: Diagnostic port not instantiated 1: Diagnostic port instantiated (Default Value)

bits.name: usecrypt
bits.comment: 0: AES-CCM Encryption block not present 1: AES-CCM Encryption block present (Default Value)

bits.name: clk_sel
bits.comment: Operating Frequency (in MHz) Default value is 13MHz

bits.name: intmode
bits.comment: 0: Interrupts are edge level generated, i.e. pulse. 1: Interrupts are trigger level generated, i.e. stays active at 1 till acknowledgement (Default Value)

bits.name: bus_type
bits.comment: Processor Bus Type 0: AHB Bus 1: X-Bar Bus

bits.name: data_width

bits.name: addr_width
bits.comment: Value of the RW_BLE_ADDRESS_WIDTH parameter concerted into binary. Default value is 13 (in decimal)
