This bit resets EVENTAPFAINTSTAT and EVENTAPFAINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: finetgtimintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Fine Target Timer interrupt acknowledgement bit Software writing 1 acknowledges the Fine Timer interrupt. This bit resets FINETGTIMINTSTAT and FINETGTIMINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: grosstgtimintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Gross Target Timer interrupt acknowledgement bit Software writing 1 acknowledges the Gross Timer interrupt. This bit resets GROSSTGTIMINTSTAT and GROSSTGTIMINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: errorintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Error interrupt acknowledgement bit Software writing 1 acknowledges the Error interrupt. This bit resets ERRORINTSTAT and ERRORINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: cryptintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Encryption engine interrupt acknowledgement bit Software writing 1 acknowledges the Encryption engine interrupt. This bit resets CRYPTINTSTAT and CRYPTINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: eventintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. End of Event interrupt acknowledgment bit Software writing 1 acknowledges the End of Advertising / Scanning / Connection interrupt. This bit resets SLPINTSTAT and SLPINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: slpintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. End of Deep Sleep interrupt acknowledgment bit Software writing 1 acknowledges the End of Sleep Mode interrupt. This bit resets SLPINTSTAT and SLPINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: rxintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Packet Reception interrupt acknowledgment bit Software writing 1 acknowledges the Rx interrupt. This bit resets RXINTSTAT and RXINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: cscntintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. 625s base time reference interrupt acknowledgment bit Software writing 1 acknowledges the CLKN interrupt. This bit resets CLKINTSTAT and CLKINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: samp
bits.comment: Writing a 1 samples the Base Time Counter value in BASETIMECNT register field. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: basetimecnt
bits.comment: Value of the 625s base time reference counter. Updated each time SAMP field is written. Used by the SW in order to synchronize with the HW

bits.name: finecnt
bits.comment: Value of the current s fine time reference counter. Updated each time SAMP field is written. Used by the SW in order to synchronize with the HW, and obtain a more precise sleep duration

bits.name: bdaddrl
bits.comment: Bluetooth Low Energy Device Address. LSB part.

bits.name: priv_npub
bits.comment: Bluetooth Low Energy Device Address privacy indicator 0: Public Bluetooth Device Address 1: Private Bluetooth Device Address

bits.name: bdaddru
bits.comment: Bluetooth Low Energy Device Address. MSB part.

bits.name: etptr
bits.comment: Exchange Table Pointer that determines the starting point of the Exchange Table

bits.name: currentrxdescptr
bits.comment: Rx Descriptor Pointer that determines the starting point of the Receive Buffer Chained List

bits.name: diag3_en
bits.comment: 0: Disable diagnostic port 3 output. All outputs are set to 0x0. 1: Enable diagnostic port 3 output.

bits.name: diag3
bits.comment: Only relevant when DIAGEN3 = 1. Selection of the outputs that must be driven to the diagnostic port 3. See section 2.16 for a detailed description.

bits.name: diag2_en
bits.comment: 0: Disable diagnostic port 2 output. All outputs are set to 0x0. 1: Enable diagnostic port 2 output.

bits.name: diag2
bits.comment: Only relevant when DIAGEN2 = 1. Selection of the outputs that must be driven to the diagnostic port 2. See section 2.16 for a detailed description.

bits.name: diag1_en
bits.comment: 0: Disable diagnostic port 1 output. All outputs are set to 0x0. 1: Enable diagnostic port 1 output.

bits.name: diag1
bits.comment: Only relevant when DIAGEN1 = 1. Selection of the outputs that must be driven to the diagnostic port 1. See section 2.16 for a detailed description.

bits.name: diag0_en
bits.comment: 0: Disable diagnostic port 0 output. All outputs are set to 0x0. 1: Enable diagnostic port 0 output.

bits.name: diag0
bits.comment: Only relevant when DIAGEN0 = 1. Selection of the outputs that must be driven to the diagnostic port 0. See section 2.16 for a detailed description.

bits.name: diag3stat
bits.comment: Directly connected to ble_dbg3[7:0] output. Debug use only.

bits.name: diag2stat
bits.comment: Directly connected to ble_dbg2[7:0] output. Debug use only.

bits.name: diag1stat
bits.comment: Directly connected to ble_dbg1[7:0] output. Debug use only.

bits.name: diag0stat
bits.comment: Directly connected to ble_dbg0[7:0] output. Debug use only.

bits.name: reg_addmax
bits.comment: Upper limit for the Register zone indicated by the reg_inzone flag (see section 2.16)

bits.name: em_addmax
bits.comment: Upper limit for the Exchange Memory zone indicated by the em_inzone flag (see section 2.16)

bits.name: reg_addmin
bits.comment: Lower limit for the Register zone indicated by the reg_inzone flag (see section 2.16)

bits.name: em_addmin
bits.comment: Lower limit for the Exchange Memory zone indicated by the em_inzone flag (see section 2.16)

bits.name: ral_underrun
bits.comment: Indicates Resolving Address List engine Under run issue, happens when RAL List parsing not finished on time 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: ral_error
bits.comment: Indicates Resolving Address List engine faced a bad setting (e.g CS-RAL_EN = 1 and null RALPTR, or RALPTR > CS-PEER_RALPTR). 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: concevtirq_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether two consecutive and concurrent ble_event_irq have been generated, and not acknowledged in time by the RW-BLE Software. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: rxdata_ptr_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether Rx data buffer pointer value programmed is null: this is a major programming failure. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: txdata_ptr_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether Tx data buffer pointer value programmed is null during Advertising / Scanning / Initiating events, or during Master / Slave connections with non-null packet length: this is a major programming failure. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: rxdesc_empty_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether Rx Descriptor pointer value programmed in register is null: this is a major programming failure. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: txdesc_empty_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether Tx Descriptor pointer value programmed in Control Structure is null during Advertising / Scanning / Initiating events: this is a major programming failure. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: csformat_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether CS-FORMAT has been programmed with an invalid value: this is a major software programming failure. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: llchmap_error
bits.comment: Indicates Link Layer Channel Map error, happens when actual number of CS-LLCHMAP bit set to one is different from CS-NBCHGOOD at the beginning of Frequency Hopping process 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: adv_underrun
bits.comment: Indicates Advertising Interval Under run, occurs if time between two consecutive Advertising packet (in Advertising mode) is lower than described in Table 3-11. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: ifs_underrun
bits.comment: Indicates Inter Frame Space Under run, occurs if IFS time is not enough to update and read Control Structure/Descriptors, and/or White List parsing is not finished and/or Decryption time is too long to be finished on time 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: whitelist_error
bits.comment: Indicates White List Timeout error, occurs if White List parsing is not finished on time 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: evt_cntl_apfm_error
bits.comment: Indicates Anticipated Pre-Fetch Mechanism error: happens when 2 consecutive events are programmed, and when the first event is not completely finished while second pre-fetch instant is reached. 0: No error 1: Error occured

bits.name: evt_schdl_apfm_error
bits.comment: Indicates Anticipated Pre-Fetch Mechanism error: happens when 2 consecutive events are programmed, and when the first event is not completely finished while second pre-fetch instant is reached. 0: No error 1: Error occured

bits.name: evt_schdl_entry_error
bits.comment: Indicates Event Scheduler faced Invalid timing programing on two consecutive ET entries (e.g first one with 624s offset and second one with no offset) 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: evt_schdl_emacc_error
bits.comment: Indicates Event Scheduler Exchange Memory access error, happens when Exchange Memory accesses are not served in time, and blocks the Exchange Table entry read 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: radio_emacc_error
bits.comment: Indicates Radio Controller Exchange Memory access error, happens when Exchange Memory accesses are not served in time and data are corrupted. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: pktcntl_emacc_error
bits.comment: Indicates Packet Controller Exchange Memory access error, happens when Exchange Memory accesses are not served in time and Tx/Rx data are corrupted 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: rxcrypt_error
bits.comment: Indicates real time decryption error, happens when AES-CCM decryption is too slow compared to Packet Controller requests. A 16-bytes block has to be decrypted prior the next block is received by the Packet Controller 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: txcrypt_error
bits.comment: Indicates Real Time encryption error, happens when AES-CCM encryption is too slow compared to Packet Controller requests. A 16-bytes block has to be encrypted and prepared on Packet Controller request, and needs to be ready before the Packet Controller has to send ti 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: swprof
bits.comment: Software Profiling register: used by RW-BLE Software for profiling purpose: this value is copied on Diagnostic port (Please refer to section 2.16 for details)

bits.name: sync_pulse_mode
bits.comment: Determines whether SYNC_P output will be dragged as pulse or level maintained till end of the Packet. 0: Access Code detection indicator provided as pulse 1: Access Code detection indicator provided as level

bits.name: dpcorr_en
bits.comment: Enables the use of the delayed DC offset compensated data path in Radio Correlator block. 1: Enable 0: Disable

bits.name: forceagc_en
bits.comment: Control Ripple AGC force mode based on RADIOCNTL2-FORCEAGC_LENGTH value 1: Enable 0: Disable

bits.name: forcebleiq
bits.comment: Control Ripple modulation mode in between FM and I&Q 1: I&Q modulation mode 0: FM modulation mode

bits.name: jef_select
bits.comment: Selects Jitter Elimination FIFO

bits.name: spifreq
bits.comment: Frequency of the SPI clock 00: SPI clock frequency is baseband master clock frequency divided by 2 (i.e 6.5MHz @ 13MHz) 01: SPI clock frequency is baseband master clock frequency divided by 4 (i.e 3.25MHz @ 13MHz) 10: SPI clock frequency is baseband master clock frequency divided by 8 (i.e 1.67MHz @ 13MHz) 11: Do not use

bits.name: spicomp
bits.comment: This bit is READ ONLY. 0: Indicates that the SPI transfer is in progress. 1: Indicates that the SPI transfer is complete. The RW-BT Dual Mode is ready to start another transfer.

bits.name: spigo
bits.comment: Software writing 1 triggers the SPI access. This bit is always read as 0.

bits.name: subversion
bits.comment: Has no effect on Radio Controller

bits.name: xrfsel
bits.comment: Extended radio selection field 5'b00000: No radio selected 5'b00001: RivieraWaves Ripple RF (BT4.0) 5'b00010: External Radio controller support 5'b00011-5'b11111: reserved

bits.name: spiptr
bits.comment: Pointer to the buffer containing data to be transferred to or received from the SPI port.

bits.name: rfrxtmda
bits.comment: RF Rx Test Mode Delay Adjustment

bits.name: tx_delay
bits.comment: Used to compensate Modem&RF Tx delay. When used, rtrip_delay should be set as Rx delay

bits.name: sync_position
bits.comment: Expected bit offset when rx symbol flag found. Used to compensate Modem&RF Rx delay.

bits.name: forceagc_length
bits.comment: Defines Rx window time threshold that forces Ripple AGC to max gain

bits.name: freqtable_ptr
bits.comment: BR/EDR Frequency Table pointer

bits.name: rtrip_delay
bits.comment: Defines round trip delay value. This value correspond to the addition of data latency in Tx and data latency in Rx. Value is in s

bits.name: rxpwrup
bits.comment: This register holds the length in us of the RX power up phase for the current radio device. Default value is 210us (reset value). Operating range depends on the selected radio.

bits.name: txpwrdn
bits.comment: This register extends the length in us of the TX power down phase for the current radio device. Default value is 3us (reset value). Operating range depends on the selected radio.

bits.name: txpwrup
bits.comment: This register holds the length in us of the TX power up phase for the current radio device. Default value is 210us (reset value). Operating range depends on the selected radio.

bits.name: rtrip_delay_2m
bits.comment: Defines round trip delay value for 2M mode. This value correspond to the addition of data latency in Tx and data latency in Rx. Value is in s

bits.name: sync_position_2m
bits.comment: Expected bit offset when rx symbol flag found for 2M mode. Used to compensate Modem&RF Rx delay.

bits.name: advchmap
bits.comment: Advertising Channel Map, defined as per the advertising connection settings. Contains advertising channels index 37 to 39. If ADVCHMAP[i] equals: 0: Do not use data channel i+37. 1: Use data channel i+37.

bits.name: advint
bits.comment: Advertising Packet Interval defines the time interval in between two ADV_xxx packet sent. Value is in s. Value to program depends on the used Advertising Packet type and the device filtering policy. Please refer to Table 3-11 for details about ADVINT programming range.

bits.name: backoff
bits.comment: Active scan mode back-off counter initialization value.

bits.name: upperlimit
bits.comment: Active scan mode upper limit counter value.

bits.name: wlpubaddptr
bits.comment: Start address pointer of the public devices white list.

bits.name: wlprivaddptr
bits.comment: Start address pointer of the private devices white list.

bits.name: nbprivdev
bits.comment: Number of private devices in the white list.

bits.name: nbpubdev
bits.comment: Number of public devices in the white list.

bits.name: aes_mode
bits.comment: 0: Cipher mode 1: Decipher mode

bits.name: aes_start
bits.comment: Writing a 1 starts AES-128 ciphering/deciphering process. This bit is reset once the process is finished (i.e. ble_crypt_irq interrupt occurs, even masked)

bits.name: aeskey31_0
bits.comment: AES encryption 128-bit key. Bit 31 down to 0

bits.name: aeskey63_32
bits.comment: AES encryption 128-bit key. Bit 63 down to 32

bits.name: aeskey95_64
bits.comment: AES encryption 128-bit key. Bit 95 down to 64

bits.name: aeskey127_96
bits.comment: AES encryption 128-bit key. Bit 127 down to 96

bits.name: aesptr
bits.comment: Pointer to the memory zone where the block to cipher/decipher using AES-128 is stored.

bits.name: txmicval
bits.comment: AES-CCM plain MIC value. Valid on when MIC has been calculated (in Tx)

bits.name: rxmicval
bits.comment: AES-CCM plain MIC value. Valid on once MIC has been extracted from Rx packet.

bits.name: infiniterx
bits.comment: Applicable to all event type 0: Normal mode of operation 1: Infinite Rx window

bits.name: rxpktcnten
bits.comment: Applicable in RF Direct Rx Test mode only 0: Rx packet count disabled 1: Rx packet count enabled, and reported in CS-RXCCMPKTCNT and RFTESTRXSTAT-RXPKTCNT on RF abort command

bits.name: infinitetx
bits.comment: Applicable to all event type 0: Normal mode of operation. 1: Infinite Tx packet / Normal start of a packet but endless payload

bits.name: txlengthsrc
bits.comment: Applicable to all event type 0: Normal mode of operation: TxDESC-<TXADVLEN/TXLEN> controls the Tx packet payload size 1: Uses RFTESTCNTL-TXLENGTH packet length (can support up to 512 bytes transmit)

bits.name: prbstype
bits.comment: Defines the PRBS in use 0: Tx Packet Payload are PRBS9 type 1: Tx Packet Payload are PRBS15 type

bits.name: txpldsrc
bits.comment: Applicable to all event type 0: Tx Packet Payload source is the Control Structure 1: Tx Packet Payload are PRBS generator

bits.name: txpktcnten
bits.comment: Applicable in RF Direct Tx Test mode only 0: Tx packet count disabled 1: Tx packet count enabled, and reported in CS-TXCCMPKTCNT and RFTESTTXSTAT-TXPKTCNT on RF abort command

bits.name: txlength
bits.comment: Applicable to all event type, valid when RFTESTCNTL-TXLENGTHSRC = 1 Tx packet length in number of byte

bits.name: txpktcnt
bits.comment: Reports number of transmitted packet during Test Modes. Value is valid if RFTESTCNTL-TXPKTCNTEN is set

bits.name: rxpktcnt
bits.comment: Reports number of correctly received packet during Test Modes (no sync error, no CRC error). Value is valid if RFTESTCNTL-RXPKTCNTEN is set

bits.name: apfm_en
bits.comment: Controls the Anticipated pre-Fetch Abort mechanism 0: Disabled 1: Enabled

bits.name: prefetchabort_time
bits.comment: Defines the instant in s at which immediate abort is required after anticipated pre-fetch abort

bits.name: prefetch_time
bits.comment: Defines Exchange Table pre-fetch instant in s

bits.name: grosstarget
bits.comment: Gross Timer Target value on which a ble_grosstgtim_irq must be generated. This timer has a precision of 10ms: interrupt is generated only when GROSSTARGET[22:0] = BASETIMECNT[26:4] and BASETIMECNT[3:0] = 0.

bits.name: finetarget
bits.comment: Fine Timer Target value on which a ble_finetgtim_irq must be generated. This timer has a precision of 625s: interrupt is generated only when FINETARGET = BASETIMECNT

bits.name: ralptr
bits.comment: Start address pointer of the RAL structure

bits.name: nbraldev
bits.comment: Number of devices in RAL Structure

bits.name: lrnd_init
bits.comment: Writing a 1 initializes of Local RPA random number generation LFSR This bit is reset once the LFSR is loaded

bits.name: lrnd_val
bits.comment: Initialization value for Local RPA random generation when LRDN_INIT is set to 1, else reports the current Local RPA random number LFSR value

bits.name: prnd_init
bits.comment: Writing a 1 initializes of Peer RPA random number generation LFSR This bit is reset once the LFSR is loaded

bits.name: prnd_val
bits.comment: Initialization value for Peer RPA random generation when PRDN_INIT is set to 1, else reports the current Peer RPA random number LFSR value

bits.name: blepriomode
bits.comment: Determine BLE Priority Scheduling Arbitration Mode 0: BLE Decision instant not used 1: BLE Decision instant used

bits.name: blemargin
bits.comment: Determine the decision instant margin for Priority Scheduling Arbitration. Decision instant is defined as per formula of section 3.6

bits.name: typ
bits.comment: Version type of bt_core. 1 for BTDM old version. 2 for BTDM new version. 3 for BLE only.

bits.name: rel
bits.comment: Major release number of bt_core

bits.name: upg
bits.comment: Upgrade number of bt_core

bits.name: rf_ext_slave
bits.comment: Set to 1 when working as a plug-in RF&modem board. Set to 0 in all other modes

bits.name: rf_ext_master
bits.comment: Set to 1 when using plug-in RF&modem board. Set to 0 in all other modes

bits.name: tport_clk_sel
bits.comment: select tport clock

bits.name: tport_trig_sel
bits.comment: select tport trigger

bits.name: tport_data1_sel
bits.comment: select tport data1

bits.name: tport_data0_sel
bits.comment: select tport data0

bits.name: pllfreq_sel_31_0
bits.comment: select pll frequency for rf/modem for channel 0~31 1 for 214.5MHz and 0 for 208MHz

bits.name: pllfreq_sel_63_32
bits.comment: select pll frequency for rf/modem for channel 32~63 1 for 214.5MHz and 0 for 208MHz

bits.name: pllfreq_sel_78_64
bits.comment: select pll frequency for rf/modem for channel 64~78 1 for 214.5MHz and 0 for 208MHz

bits.name: tx_cal_en
bits.comment: tx calibration enable

bits.name: rx_cal_en
bits.comment: rx calibration enable

bits.name: txon_force
bits.comment: force txon for rf to txon_value when txon_force is 1

bits.name: rxon_force
bits.comment: force rxon for rf to rxon_value when rxon_force is 1

bits.name: modem_txon_delay
bits.comment: delay time in us to enable modem tx after link layer txon enable

bits.name: modem_rf_txoff_delay
bits.comment: delay time in us to disable modem&rf tx after link layer txon disable

bits.name: modem_rxon_delay
bits.comment: delay time in us to enable modem rx after link layer rxon enable

bits.name: modem_rf_rxoff_delay
bits.comment: delay time in us to disable modem&rf rx after link layer rxon disable

bits.name: rccal_length
bits.comment: number of rc clock cycles when doing rc calibration

bits.name: rccal_auto
bits.comment: enable automatic rc calibration when BT wakeup

bits.name: rccal_start
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1s to rs. rc calibration start by software

bits.name: rccal_done
bits.comment: indicate rc caliration done

bits.name: rccal_result
bits.comment: number of reference clock cycles when doing rc calibration. F(rc) = F(ref) * rccal_length / rccal_result

bits.name: bt_active_mode
bits.comment: BT active indicater: 0: rf_txon 1: rf_rxon 2: rf_txon | rf_rxon 3: modem_txon | modem_rxon

bits.name: mws_mask_bt_en
bits.comment: 0: BT tx will not be masked 1: BT tx will be masked

bits.name: mws_mask_bt_mode
bits.comment: BT tx will be masked when: 0: mws_tx 1: mws_rx 2: mws_tx | mws_rx 3: mws_tx & mws_rx

bits.name: osc_en_stat
bits.comment: status of osc_en. 1 means BT is using clock derived from oscillator

bits.name: osc_en_mask
bits.comment: when set to 1, mask bt2pmu_wakeup output to 0 to avoid unnecessary wakeup

bits.name: master_soft_rst
bits.comment: Reset the complete RW-BT Core except timing generator and register blocks, when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0. In case of Dual Mode implementation, reset also common blocks.

bits.name: master_tgsoft_rst
bits.comment: Reset the timing generator, when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: reg_soft_rst
bits.comment: Reset the complete register block, when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: swint_req
bits.comment: Forces the generation of bt_sw_irq when written with a 1, and proper masking is set. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: scan_abort
bits.comment: Abort the current Inquiry / Page / Broadcast scan window when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: rftest_abort
bits.comment: Abort the current RF Testing when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0. Note that when RFTEST_ABORT is requested 1/ In case of infinite Tx, the Packet Controller FSM stops at the end of the current byte in process, and processes accordingly the packet CRC. 2/ In case of Infinite Rx, the Packet Controller FSM either stops as the end of the current Packet reception (if Access address has been detected), or simply stop the processing switching off the RF.

bits.name: pageinq_abort
bits.comment: Abort the current Inquiry Mode or Page Mode when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: sniff_abort
bits.comment: Abort the current Sniff Mode when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: flowdsb
bits.comment: 0: FLOW verification on Rx packets is activated. 1: Packets are accepted regardless of FLOW value (test mode).

bits.name: lmpflowdsb
bits.comment: 0: When FLOW = 0, LMP messages can be sent. 1: When FLOW = 0, LMP messages are not sent.

bits.name: cryptdsb
bits.comment: 0: Normal operation. Encryption enabled when required. 1: Encryption disabled. Note this works for both E0 and AES-CCM encryption mechanism

bits.name: whitdsb
bits.comment: 0: Normal operation. Whitening enabled. 1: Whitening disabled.

bits.name: arqndsb
bits.comment: 0: ARQN verification on Rx packets is activated. 1: Packets are accepted regardless of ARQN value (test mode).

bits.name: crcdsb
bits.comment: 0: Normal operation. CRC removed from incoming data stream. 1: CRC stripping disabled on Rx packets.

bits.name: hopdsb
bits.comment: 0: Normal operation. Hopping enabled. 1: Hopping disabled, the frequency is set either by CS-FREQ or by RFTESTFREQ register fields.

bits.name: seqndsb
bits.comment: 0: SEQN verification on Rx packets is activated. 1: Packets are accepted regardless of SEQN value (test mode).

bits.name: cx_txbsyena
bits.comment: This field updates the CS-TXBSY_EN field in the control structure when ends a MASTER_PAGE_RESPONSE or a SLAVE_PAGE_RESPONSE frame.

bits.name: cx_rxbsyena
bits.comment: This field updates the CS-RXBSY_EN field in the control structure when ends a MASTER_PAGE_RESPONSE or a SLAVE_PAGE_RESPONSE frame.

bits.name: cx_dnabort
bits.comment: This field updates the CS-DNABORT field in the control structure when ends a MASTER_PAGE_RESPONSE or a SLAVE_PAGE_RESPONSE frame.

bits.name: rwbten
bits.comment: 0: Disable RW-BT Core. 1: Enable RW-BT Core.

bits.name: syncerr
bits.comment: Indicate the maximum number of errors allowed to recognize the Access Code.

bits.name: typ
bits.comment: RW-BT Core Type C 0x8 means BT v4.2 (i.e. correspond LM version assigned number). Correspond to FS v8.0.11

bits.name: rel
bits.comment: Version of the RW-BT Core C Major release number. Correspond to FS v8.0.11.

bits.name: upg
bits.comment: Version of the RW-BT Core C Upgrade number. Correspond to FS v8.0.11

bits.name: build_num
bits.comment: RW-BT Core Build number

bits.name: dmmode
bits.comment: 0: RW-BT Core is used as a standalone BR/EDR device 1: RW-BT Core is used in a Dual Mode device

bits.name: mwswci2
bits.comment: 0: MWS Coexistence 2-Wire Interface not supported 1: MWS Coexistence 2-Wire Interface supported

bits.name: mwswci1
bits.comment: 0: MWS Coexistence 1-Wire Interface not supported 1: MWS Coexistence 1-Wire Interface supported

bits.name: vxportnb
bits.comment: Number of supported Audio Channel (0 to 3) 00: No Audio Channel / No PCM. 01: One Audio Channel 10: Two Audio Channels 11: Three Audio Channels.

bits.name: pcm
bits.comment: 0: PCM Not Instantiated 1: PCM Instantiated

bits.name: mwscoex
bits.comment: 0: MWS Coexistence mechanism not present 1: MWS Coexistence mechanism present

bits.name: wlancoex
bits.comment: 0: WLAN Coexistence mechanism not present 1: WLAN Coexistence mechanism present

bits.name: rfif
bits.comment: RFIF[k]= 0: Control logic supporting radio k not present RFIF[k]= 1: Control logic supporting radio k present Index k values are: 00001: RW-BT Ripple RF. 00010: External Radio Controller Support xxxx00: Reserved

bits.name: usedbg
bits.comment: 0: Diagnostics port not present 1: Diagnostics port present

bits.name: usecrypt
bits.comment: 0: AES-CCM Encryption block not present 1: AES-CCM Encryption block present

bits.name: clk_sel
bits.comment: Operating Frequency (in MHz) Default is 13 MHz

bits.name: intmode
bits.comment: 0: Interrupts are edge level generated, i.e. pulse. 1: Interrupts are trigger level generated, i.e. stays active at 1 till acknowledgement

bits.name: bus_type
bits.comment: Processor Bus Type 0: AHB Bus 1: X-Bar Bus

bits.name: data_width
bits.comment: Processor Data bus width: 0 16 bits 1: 32 bits

bits.name: addr_width
bits.comment: Value of the RW_BT_ADDRESS_WIDTH parameter converted into binary.

bits.name: sketintmsk

bits.name: frameintmsk

bits.name: swintstat

bits.name: frameapfaintstat

bits.name: frameintstat
bits.comment: End of Frame Interrupt status 0: No End of Frame Interrupt 1: End of Frame Interrupt is pending

bits.name: mwswcirxintstat
bits.comment: MWS Serial Interface Rx Interrupt status 0: No MWS WCI Interrupt 1: MWS WCI Interrupt is pending

bits.name: mwswcitxintstat
bits.comment: MWS Serial Interface Tx Interrupt status 0: No MWS WCI Interrupt 1: MWS WCI Interrupt is pending

bits.name: errorintstat
bits.comment: Error Interrupt status. 0: No Error interrupt. 1: Error interrupt is pending.

bits.name: grosstgtintstat
bits.comment: Gross Timer Interrupt status. 0: No Gross Timer interrupt. 1: Gross Timer interrupt is pending.

bits.name: finetgtintstat

bits.name: mtoffint1stat

bits.name: audioint1stat

bits.name: clknintstat

bits.name: frameapfaintrawstat

bits.name: frameintrawstat

bits.name: mwswcirxintrawstat

bits.name: mwswcitxintrawstat
bits.comment: MWS Serial Interface Tx Interrupt raw status 0: No MWS WCI Interrupt 1: MWS WCI Interrupt is pending

bits.name: errorintrawstat
bits.comment: Error Interrupt raw status. 0: No Error interrupt. 1: Error interrupt is pending.

bits.name: grosstgtintrawstat

bits.name: finetgtintrawstat

bits.name: mtoffint1rawstat

bits.name: mtoffint0rawstat

bits.name: frsyncintrawstat
bits.comment: MWS Frame Synchronization Interrupt raw status. 0: No frame_sync interrupt. 1: A frame_sync interrupt is pending.

bits.name: audioint2rawstat
bits.comment: Audio Channel 2 Interrupt raw status. 0: No eSCO SW Transport interrupt. 1: An eSCO SW Transport interrupt is pending.

bits.name: audioint1rawstat
bits.comment: Audio Channel 1 Interrupt raw status. 0: No eSCO SW Transport interrupt. 1: An eSCO SW Transport interrupt is pending.

bits.name: audioint0rawstat
bits.comment: Audio Channel 0 Interrupt raw status. 0: No eSCO SW Transport interrupt. 1: An eSCO SW Transport interrupt is pending.

bits.name: slpintrawstat
bits.comment: End of Sleep Interrupt raw Status. 0: No End of Sleep Mode interrupt. 1: An End of Sleep Mode interrupt is pending.

bits.name: rxintrawstat
bits.comment: Packet Reception Interrupt raw status. 0: No Rx interrupt. 1: An Rx interrupt is pending.

bits.name: clknintrawstat

bits.name: sketintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Skipped Exchange Table entry Interrupt acknowledgment. Software writing 1 acknowledges the Skipped Exchange Table entry interrupt. This bit resets SKETINTSTAT and SKETINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: swintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. SW triggered Interrupt acknowledgment. Software writing 1 acknowledges the SW triggered interrupt. This bit resets SWINTSTAT and SWINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: frameapfaintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. End of Frame / Anticipated Pre-Fetch Abort Interrupt acknowledgment. Software writing 1 acknowledges the End of Frame interrupt. This bit resets FRAMEAPFAINTSTAT and FRAMEAPFAINTRWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: frameintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. End of Frame Interrupt acknowledgment. Software writing 1 acknowledges the End of Frame interrupt. This bit resets FRAMEINTSTAT and FRAMEINTRWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: mwswcirxintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. MWS Serial Interface Rx Interrupt acknowledgment. Software writing 1 acknowledges the MWS Serial Interface interrupt. This bit resets MWSWCIINTSTAT and MWSWCIINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: mwswcitxintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. MWS Serial Interface Tx Interrupt acknowledgment. Software writing 1 acknowledges the MWS Serial Interface interrupt. This bit resets MWSWCIINTSTAT and MWSWCIINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: errorintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Error Interrupt acknowledgment. Software writing 1 acknowledges the Error interrupt. This bit resets ERRORINTSTAT and ERRORINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: grosstgtintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Gross Timer Interrupt acknowledgment. Software writing 1 acknowledges the Gross Timer interrupt. This bit resets GROSSTGTINTSTAT and GROSSTGTINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: finetgtintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Fine Timer Interrupt acknowledgment. Software writing 1 acknowledges the Fine Timer interrupt. This bit resets FINETGTINTSTAT and FINETGTINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: mtoffint1ack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Momentary Offset 1 Interrupt acknowledgment. Software writing 1 acknowledges the Momentary offset event interrupt. This bit resets MTOFFINT1STAT and MTOFFINT1RAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: mtoffint0ack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Momentary Offset 0 Interrupt acknowledgment. Software writing 1 acknowledges the Momentary offset event interrupt. This bit resets MTOFFINT0STAT and MTOFFINT0RAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: frsyncintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. MWS Frame Synchronization Interrupt acknowledgement. Software writing 1 acknowledges the frame_sync event interrupt. This bit resets FRSYNCINTSTAT and FRSYNCINTRAWSTAT flag. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: audioint2ack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Audio Channel 2 Interrupt acknowledgement. Software writing 1 acknowledges the Audio Channel 2 interrupt. This bit resets AUDIOINT2STAT and AUDIOINT2RAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: audioint1ack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Audio Channel 1 Interrupt acknowledgement. Software writing 1 acknowledges the Audio Channel 1 interrupt. This bit resets AUDIOINT1STAT and AUDIOINT1RAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: audioint0ack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Audio Channel 0 Interrupt acknowledgement. Software writing 1 acknowledges the Audio Channel 0 interrupt. This bit resets AUDIOINT0STAT and AUDIOINT0RAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: slpintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. End of Sleep Interrupt acknowledgement. Software writing 1 acknowledges the End of Sleep Mode interrupt. This bit resets SLPINTSTAT and SLPINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: rxintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Packet Reception Interrupt acknowledgement. Software writing 1 acknowledges the Rx interrupt. This bit resets RXINTSTAT and RXINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: clknintack
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wos to s. Slot Interrupt acknowledgement. Software writing 1 acknowledges the CLKN interrupt. This bit resets CLKINTSTAT and CLKINTRAWSTAT flags. Resets at 0 when action is performed

bits.name: samp
bits.comment: Writing a 1 samples the CLKN[27:0] value in SLOTCLK-SCLK register field. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0

bits.name: clkn_upd
bits.comment: Update the Native Bluetooth counter CLKN[27:1] (CLKN[0] is not considered), when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: sclk
bits.comment: Native Bluetooth counter CLKN sampled at the time the processor has written the SAMP bit (precsision of 312.5s). This value does not change until the next writing of SAMP bit, and can therefore be safely accessed with 8-, 16- or 32-bits accesses.

bits.name: finecnt
bits.comment: Value of the current s fine time reference counter sampled at the time the processor has written the SAMP bit. Used by the SW in order to synchronize with the HW, and obtain a more precise sleep duration

bits.name: abtpageen
bits.comment: Enable automatic A-train/B-train switch during Page procedure. 0: Page procedure A-train/B-train counter disabled 1: Page procedure A-train/B-train counter enabled

bits.name: abtpagestartvalue
bits.comment: Starting train value of Page procedure 0:Start with A-train 1:Start with B-train

bits.name: abtpageload
bits.comment: Load A-train/B-train Page procedure conter, when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: abtpagetime
bits.comment: Defines A-train/B-train duration time during Page procedure, counted by 16-slots. Loaded when ABTPAGELOAD is set. Start when Page procedure starts and ABTPAGEEN is set. Stops when ABTPAGEEN is reset. Switch of train when wrapping.

bits.name: abtinqen
bits.comment: Enable automatic A-train/B-train switch during Inquiry procedure. 0: Inquiry procedure A-train/B-train counter disabled 1: Inquiry procedure A-train/B-train counter enabled

bits.name: abtinqstartvalue
bits.comment: Starting train value of Inquiry procedure 0:Start with A-train 1:Start with B-train

bits.name: abtinqload
bits.comment: Load A-train/B-train Inquiry procedure conter, when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: abtinqtime
bits.comment: Defines A-train/B-train duration time during Inquiry procedure, counted by 16-slots. Loaded when ABTINQLOAD is set. Start when Inquiry procedure starts and ABTINQEN is set. Stops when ABTINQEN is reset. Switch of train when wrapping.

bits.name: nwinsize
bits.comment: Default value equals d26. Should not exceed 'h88. Applies when ET-SNIFF = 1 on first access code detection, in order to process the new bit offset (See section 3.5.5)

bits.name: edrbcast
bits.comment: 0: Broadcast @ 1Mbps / normal mode 1: Broadcast operation in EDR Mode (@ 2/3 Mbps) / special features The EDRCNTL-EDRBCAST bit is used in reception (slave side) as following: if RXLTADDR= 0 (i.e. broadcast packet is received) if EDRCNTL-EDRBCAST=0 , we consider the currently received packet is not an EDR-packet. The 1Mbps modulation is used. if EDRCNTL-EDRBCAST=1, then apply EDR modulation or not depending on the control structure bit " ACLEDR" set in MISCNTL field.

bits.name: rxguarddsb
bits.comment: 0: normal operation, EDR Rx guard window detection activated 1: EDR Rx guard window detection disabled.

bits.name: tx_swap
bits.comment: 0: Direct order EDR Payload data transmit 1: Reverse order EDR Payload data transmit

bits.name: rx_swap
bits.comment: 0: Direct order EDR Payload data receive 1: Reverse order EDR Payload data receive

bits.name: rxgrd_timeout
bits.comment: Time out value before EDR packet reception that allow ending the Rx transaction if an EDR packet is not correctly detected. Default value is set to 212 clock cycles @ 13MHz <-> 16.3us. Timing between Packet Header and EDR packet is defined as 5us+-0.25us + 11 synchronization symbol = 16.25us in the worst case

bits.name: etptr
bits.comment: Exchange Table pointer value

bits.name: currentrxdescptr
bits.comment: Rx Descriptor current pointer value

bits.name: extwkupdsb
bits.comment: External Wake-Up disable 0: RW-BT Core can be woken by external wake-up 1: RW-BT Core cannot be woken up by external wake-up

bits.name: ext_high_wakeup_en
bits.comment: Enable external pin high level wakeup

bits.name: ext_low_wakeup_en
bits.comment: Enable external pin low level wakeup

bits.name: ext_activity_wakeup_en
bits.comment: Enable external pin activity wakeup

bits.name: deep_sleep_stat
bits.comment: Indicator of current Deep Sleep clock mux status: 0: RW-BT Core is not yet in Deep Sleep Mode 1: RW-BT Core is in Deep Sleep Mode (only low_power_clk is running)

bits.name: soft_wakeup_req
bits.comment: Wake Up Request from RW-BT Software. Applies when system is in Deep Sleep Mode. It wakes up the RW-BT Core when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: deep_sleep_corr_en
bits.comment: CLKN integer and fractional part correction (i.e. CLKN Counter and Fine Counter). Applies when system has been woken-up from Deep Sleep Mode. It enables Fine Counter and Base Time counter when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: deep_sleep_on
bits.comment: RW-BT Core sleep mode request control 0: RW-BT Core in normal active mode 1: Request RW-BT Core to switch in deep sleep mode. This bit is reset on DEEP_SLEEP_STAT falling edge.

bits.name: radio_sleep_en
bits.comment: Controls the Radio module 0: Radio stands in normal active mode 1: Allow to disable Radio

bits.name: osc_sleep_en
bits.comment: Controls the RF High frequency crystal oscillator 0: High frequency crystal oscillator stands in normal active mode 1: Allow to disable High frequency crystal oscillator

bits.name: deepsltime
bits.comment: Determines the time in low_power_clk clock cycles to spend in Deep Sleep Mode before waking-up the device. This ensures a maximum of 37 hours and 16mn sleep mode capabilities at 32kHz. This ensures a maximum of 36 hours and 16mn sleep mode capabilities at 32.768kHz

bits.name: deepsldur
bits.comment: Actual duration of the last deep sleep phase measured in low power oscillator cycles. DEEPSLDUR is set to zero at the beginning of the deep sleep phase, and is incremented at each low power clock tick until the end of the deep sleep phase.

bits.name: twext
bits.comment: Time in low power oscillator cycles allowed for stabilization of the high frequency oscillator following an external wake-up request (signal wakeup_req) [064ms for 32kHz)

bits.name: twosc
bits.comment: Time in low power oscillator cycles allowed for stabilization of the high frequency oscillator when the deep-sleep mode has been left due to sleep-timer expiry (DEEPSLWKUP) [064ms for 32kHz)

bits.name: twrm
bits.comment: Time in low power oscillator cycles allowed for the radio module to leave low-power mode [032ms for 32kHz)

bits.name: finecntcorr
bits.comment: Phase correction value for the CLKN counter in s.

bits.name: abs_delta
bits.comment: Determines whether CLNCNTCORR is an absolute correction or a signed delta increment correction 0: Absolute correction 1: Signed delta increment correction

bits.name: clkncntcorr
bits.comment: CLKN Counter correction value / signed delta increment

bits.name: token_tx_delay
bits.comment: Token Tx delay time after Slave receive completed

bits.name: token_rx_delay
bits.comment: Token Rx delay time after Slave receive completed

bits.name: token_quick_sync
bits.comment: 0: Use normal sync pulse for token ID 1: Use quick sync pulse for token ID

bits.name: token_rxwin
bits.comment: Size of Token Rx Window

bits.name: arbiter_bypass
bits.comment: Slave arbiter receive token ID but bypass arbitration

bits.name: arbiter_en
bits.comment: Slave arbiter enable

bits.name: observer_active
bits.comment: Slave observer will respond to master

bits.name: observer_en
bits.comment: Slave observer enable

bits.name: diag3_en
bits.comment: 0: Disable diagnostic port 3 output. All outputs are set to 0. 1: Enable diagnostic port 3 output.

bits.name: diag3
bits.comment: Only relevant when DIAGEN3 = 1. Selection of the outputs that are driven to the diagnostic port 3.

bits.name: diag2_en
bits.comment: 0: Disable diagnostic port 2 output. All outputs are set to 0. 1: Enable diagnostic port 2 output.

bits.name: diag2
bits.comment: Only relevant when DIAGEN2 = 1. Selection of the outputs that are driven to the diagnostic port 2.

bits.name: diag1_en
bits.comment: 0: Disable diagnostic port 1 output. All outputs are set to 0. 1: Enable diagnostic port 1 output.

bits.name: diag1
bits.comment: Only relevant when DIAGEN1 = 1. Selection of the outputs that are driven to the diagnostic port 1.

bits.name: diag0_en
bits.comment: 0: Disable diagnostic port 0 output. All outputs are set to 0. 1: Enable diagnostic port 0 output.

bits.name: diag0
bits.comment: Only relevant when DIAGEN0 = 1. Selection of the outputs that are driven to the diagnostic port 0.

bits.name: diag3stat
bits.comment: Directly connected to bt_dbg0[7:0] output. Debug use only

bits.name: diag2stat
bits.comment: Directly connected to bt_dbg1[7:0] output. Debug use only

bits.name: diag1stat
bits.comment: Directly connected to bt_dbg2[7:0] output. Debug use only

bits.name: diag0stat
bits.comment: Directly connected to bt_dbg3[7:0] output. Debug use only

bits.name: reg_addmax
bits.comment: Upper limit for the Register zone indicated by the reg_inzone flag (see section 2.19).

bits.name: em_addmax
bits.comment: Upper limit for the Exchange Memory zone indicated by the em_inzone flag (see section 2.19).

bits.name: reg_addmin
bits.comment: Lower limit for the Register zone indicated by the reg_inzone flag (see section 2.19)

bits.name: em_addmin
bits.comment: Lower limit for the Exchange Memory zone indicated by the em_inzone flag (see section 2.19)

bits.name: rxbuf_ptr_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether the Rx eSCO (during Voice over HCI operations) or Rx LM buffer pointer value programmed is null: this is a major programming failure. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: txbuf_ptr_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether Tx eSCO (during Voice over HCI operations) or Tx LM buffer pointer value programmed is null, or if an ACL Tx packet is set with a non null length while no buffer is associated: this is a major programming failure. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: rxdesc_empty_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether Rx Descriptor pointer value programmed in register is null: this is a major programming failure / Valid for non-connected states and Broadcast Scan mode 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: txdesc_empty_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether Tx Descriptor pointer value programmed in Control Structure is null: this is a major programming failure / Valid for non-connected states and Broadcast mode 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: csattnb_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether ATT_NB field in Control Structure is null, or when during eSCO that eSCOLTCNLT<0/1/2>-RETXNB<0/1/2> register field is null: this is a major programming failure 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: csformat_error
bits.comment: Indicates whether CS-FORMAT has been programmed with an invalid value: this is a major software programming failure. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: chmap_error
bits.comment: Channel Map error, happens when actual number of bits set to one in selected CS-CHMAP is different from corresponding CS-NBCHGOOD at the beginning of Frequency Hopping process. Note this is valid only if CS-AFHENA=1 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: hopunderrun_error
bits.comment: Calculation of the hopping frequency not done before Tx/Rx EN is asserted 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: frm_cntl_timer_error
bits.comment: Indicates an Frame Controller internal timing error 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: frm_cntl_emacc_error
bits.comment: Indicate a Frame Controller Exchange Memory Access error. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: frm_cntl_apfm_error
bits.comment: Indicates Anticipated Pre-Fetch Mechanism error in Frame Controller: happens when 2 consecutive frames are programmed, and when the first frame is not completely finished while second pre-fetch instant is reached. 0: No error 1: Error occured

bits.name: frm_schdl_apfm_error
bits.comment: Indicates Anticipated Pre-Fetch Mechanism error in Frame Scheduler: happens when 2 consecutive frames are programmed, and when the first frame is not completely finished while second pre-fetch instant is reached. 0: No error 1: Error occured

bits.name: frm_schdl_entry_error
bits.comment: Indicates Frame Scheduler faced Invalid timing programing on two consecutive ET entries (e.g first one with 624s offset and second one with no offset) 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: mwswci_emacc_error
bits.comment: MWS WCI Exchange Memory access error, happens when Exchange Memory access are not served in time and Audio samples are corrupted 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: frm_schdl_emacc_error
bits.comment: Frame Scheduler Exchange Memory access error, happens when Exchange Memory access are not served in time and Audio samples are corrupted 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: pcm_emacc_error
bits.comment: PCM Exchange Memory request access error, happens when Exchange Memory access requests are not served in time and PCM samples are corrupted 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: audio_emacc_error
bits.comment: Audio EM Access Manager Exchange Memory access error, happens when Exchange Memory access are not served in time and Audio samples are corrupted 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: radiocntl_emacc_error
bits.comment: Radio Controller Exchange Memory access error, happens when Exchange Memory access are not served in time and data are corrupted. 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: pktcntl_emacc_error
bits.comment: Packet Controller Exchange Memory access error, happens when Exchange Memory access are not served in time and Tx/Rx data are corrupted 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: cryptmode_error
bits.comment: Indicates when the Encryption mode is enabled with Connectionless Slave Broadcast (Master or Slave) 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: rxcrypt_error
bits.comment: Indicates real time decryption error, happens when AES-CCM decryption is too slow compared to Packet Controller requests. A 16-bytes block has to be decrypted prior the next block is received by the Packet Controller 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: txcrypt_error
bits.comment: Indicates Real Time encryption error, happens when AES-CCM encryption is too slow compared to Packet Controller requests. A 16-bytes block has to be encrypted and prepared on Packet Controller request, and needs to be ready before the Packet Controller has to send ti 0: No error 1: Error occurred

bits.name: swprof
bits.comment: Software Profiling register: used by RW-BT Software for profiling purpose: this value is copied on Diagnostic port

bits.name: sync_pulse_mode
bits.comment: Determines whether SYNC_P output will be dragged as pulse or level maintained till end of the Packet. 0: Access Code detection indicator provided as pulse 1: Access Code detection indicator provided as level

bits.name: dpcorr_en
bits.comment: Enables the use of the delayed DC offset compensated data path in Radio Correlator block. 1: Enable 0: Disable

bits.name: forceagc_en
bits.comment: Control Ripple AGC force mode based on RADIOCNTL2-FORCEAGC_LENGTH value 1: Enable 0: Disable

bits.name: spifreq
bits.comment: Frequency of the SPI clock 00: SPI clock frequency is baseband master clock frequency divided by 2 (i.e 6.5MHz @ 13MHz) 01: SPI clock frequency is baseband master clock frequency divided by 4 (i.e 3.25MHz @ 13MHz) 10: SPI clock frequency is baseband master clock frequency divided by 8 (i.e 1.67MHz @ 13MHz) 11: Do not use

bits.name: spicomp
bits.comment: This bit is READ ONLY. 0: Indicates that the SPI transfer is in progress. 1: Indicates that the SPI transfer is complete. The RW-BT Dual Mode is ready to start another transfer.

bits.name: spigo
bits.comment: Software writing 1 triggers the SPI access. This bit is always read as 0.

bits.name: xrfsel
bits.comment: Extended radio selection field 5'h00000: No radio selected 5'h00001: RivieraWaves Ripple RF (BT4.0) 5'h00010: External Radio controller support 5'h00011-5'b11111: reserved

bits.name: spiptr
bits.comment: Pointer to the buffer containing data to be transferred to or received from the SPI port.

bits.name: tx_delay
bits.comment: Used to compensate Modem&RF Tx delay. When used, rtrip_delay should be set as Rx delay

bits.name: sync_position
bits.comment: Defines sync_p instant when provided to the Modem.

bits.name: forceagc_length
bits.comment: Defines Rx window time threshold that forces Ripple AGC to max gain

bits.name: freqtable_ptr
bits.comment: BR/EDR Frequency Table pointer

bits.name: rtrip_delay
bits.comment: Round Trip Delay. This correspond to the cumulated Tx plus Rx latency of the radio (in us)

bits.name: rxpwrupct
bits.comment: This register holds the length in us of the RX power up phase for the current radio device. Default value is 210 us (reset value). Operating range depends on supported radio.

bits.name: txpwrdnct
bits.comment: This register extends the length in us of the TX power down phase for the current radio device. Default value is 3us (reset value). Operating range depends on supported radio.

bits.name: txpwrupct
bits.comment: This register holds the length in us of the TX power up phase for the current radio device. Default value is 210 us (reset value). Operating range is depends on supported radio.

bits.name: txmicval
bits.comment: AES-CCM plain MIC value.

bits.name: rxmicval
bits.comment: AES-CCM plain MIC value.

bits.name: e0ptr
bits.comment: E0 Address pointer

bits.name: sserrren
bits.comment: Applicable in Slave eSCO reserved slot only 0: Normal mode of operation 1: Allow reply on Sync Error

bits.name: herrren
bits.comment: Applicable in Slave eSCO reserved slot only 0: Normal mode of operation 1: Allow reply on HEC Error

bits.name: infiniterx
bits.comment: Applicable for all frame format 0: Normal mode of operation 1: Infinite Rx window

bits.name: infinite_entry
bits.comment: Set to 1 to force status of exchange table entry to be ready. Used for repeated tx

bits.name: infinitetx
bits.comment: Applicable for all frame format 0: Normal mode of operation 1: Infinite Tx window

bits.name: prbstype
bits.comment: Defines the PRBS type in use 0: Tx Packet Payload are PRBS9 type 1: Tx Packet Payload are PRBS15 type

bits.name: txpldsrc
bits.comment: Applicable for all frame format 0: Tx Packet Payload source is the Control Structure 1: Tx Packet Payload are PRBS generator

bits.name: directlopbacken
bits.comment: Direct Loopback Test Mode enable control 0: Normal mode of operation 1: Direct Loopback Mode enabled (Received Packet Header, Payload Header, and Payload data directly re-transmitted in the next slot)

bits.name: testmodeen
bits.comment: Test Mode enable control, applicable if CS-FH_EN=0 0: Normal mode of operation 1: Test Mode enable, use <TX/RX>FREQ during Tx/Rx operations.

bits.name: rxfreq
bits.comment: Frequency Table index to be used during Rx operation

bits.name: txfreq
bits.comment: Frequency Table index to be used during Tx operation

bits.name: apfm_en
bits.comment: Controls the Anticipated pre-Fetch Abort mechanism 0: Disabled 1: Enabled

bits.name: prefetchabort_time
bits.comment: Defines the instant in s at which immediate abort is required after anticipated pre-fetch abort

bits.name: prefetch_time
bits.comment: Defines Exchange Table pre-fetch instant in s

bits.name: grosstarget
bits.comment: Gross Timer Target value on which an Interrupt must be generated. This timer has a precision of 10ms: interrupt is generated only when GROSSTARGET = CLKN[27:5] and CLKN[4:0] = 0.

bits.name: finetarget
bits.comment: Fine Timer Target value on which an interrupt must be generated. This timer has a precision of 625s: interrupt is generated only when FINETARGET = CLKN[27:1]

bits.name: sketclkn
bits.comment: Returns the CLKN[27:0] value on each bt_sket_irq generation.

bits.name: target_offset
bits.comment: Signed number, time offset to the current frame_sync position in s. Valid range is [-625, 625]s. When SYNC_SOURCE=1, the following formula must apply: TARGET_OFFSET = 559 C RF round trip delay C desired CS-BITOFF

bits.name: slvlbl
bits.comment: Applies only when SYNC_SOURCE equals 1. Defines which connection to align piconet clock on. The connection is labelled using CS-LINKLBL the piconet clock is aligned when CS-LINKLBL = SLVLBL field Note the RW-BT Software must ensure the labelled connection is a slave connection, else it cannot work properly

bits.name: corr_step
bits.comment: Maximum shift size during incremental phase shift. Must be programmed to 1s (0x1) Note CORR_STEP is considered as a signed value when BLINDCORR_EN is set (allows to drift forward and backward)

bits.name: blindcorr_en
bits.comment: 0: Align piconet clock on frame_sync rising edge (when CORR_INTERVAL is reached) 1: Align piconet clock when CORR_INTERVAL is reached, without frame_sync rising edge

bits.name: frsync_pol
bits.comment: Frame sync signal polarity. 0 : rising edge events sensitive 1 : falling edge events sensitive

bits.name: sync_source
bits.comment: Defines synchronization signal source 0: MWS frame synchronization 1: Scatternet network scheduling optimization (See section 2.17)

bits.name: phase_shift_en
bits.comment: Enable incremental phase shift

bits.name: corr_interval
bits.comment: Correction interval time in slot interval. Default value is 40 (i.e. 40x625s = 25ms)

bits.name: clock_shift_en
bits.comment: Performs immediate clock shift update using CLOCK_SHIFT[10:0], when written with a 1. Resets at 0 when action is performed. No action happens if it is written with 0.

bits.name: clock_shift
bits.comment: Signed value of the clock shift to apply when CLOCK_SHIFT_EN is written with a 1 in [-625, 625]s range

bits.name: shift_phase
bits.comment: Indicate the value of the phase when an immediate shift has been programmed or when a frame_sync event occurs, [-625, 625]s

bits.name: moment_offset
bits.comment: Momentary offset, signed number which indicate the time between target_offset and the nearest alignment point, in [-625, 625]s range

bits.name: tog0
bits.comment: Toggle command for Voice Channel 0. Driven by TeSCO/TSCO toggling instant. Used to perform selection of PCM pointers and Tx/Rx Descriptor Please refer to section 2.18.5 for details.

bits.name: escochanswen0
bits.comment: Enables eSCO Channel 0 SW Transport (Enable Audio data to be routed directly to EM (or through AES-CCM if encrypted link), used by Voice Transparent Modes: 0: Disabled. 1: Enabled.

bits.name: escochanen0
bits.comment: Enables eSCO Channel 0 (controls Audio Path EM Access controller voice channel 0): 0: Disabled. 1: Enabled.

bits.name: itmode0
bits.comment: 0: bt_audio0_irq is generated on TeSCO/TSCO instant 1: bt_audio0_irq is generated INTDELAY0[5:0] slots after TeSCO/TSCO instant

bits.name: intdelay0
bits.comment: Valid if ITMODE0 = 1 Determines the slot number to wait before generating bt_audio0_irq

bits.name: tesco0
bits.comment: eSCO interval (in slots). Support a [2:16] range in slots so as to support both SCO and eSCO mandatory LMP parameters range (see [1])

bits.name: mute_sink0
bits.comment: HW mute control: 0: Do not mute on bad reception of an (e)SCO packet. 1: Mute after data or bad reception, with the pattern stored in MUTEPATT0 Note: See Table 2-34 for mute pattern value to apply

bits.name: mute_source0
bits.comment: HW mute control: 0: Provides Source buffer to the Packet Controller for Tx operations 1: Forces POLL/NULL to be sent as a replacement of Audio Packets

bits.name: invl0_1
bits.comment: SW mute status for Audio buffer 1 (i.e updated when TOG0=1): Mute if not null. Please refer to Table 2-35 for details

bits.name: invl0_0
bits.comment: SW mute status for Audio buffer 0 (i.e updated when TOG0=0): Mute if not null. Please refer to Table 2-35 for details

bits.name: mutepatt0
bits.comment: Value of the null pattern used when HW muting is enabled.

bits.name: esco0ptrtx1
bits.comment: Tx (e)SCO Sample Buffer pointer 1 of Voice Channel 0. Used when eSCOCHANCNTL0-TOG0 = 1

bits.name: esco0ptrtx0
bits.comment: Tx (e)SCO Sample Buffer pointer 0 of Voice Channel 0. Used when eSCOCHANCNTL0-TOG0 = 0

bits.name: esco0ptrrx1
bits.comment: Rx (e)SCO Sample Buffer pointer 1 of Voice Channel 0. Used when eSCOCHANCNTL0-TOG0 = 1

bits.name: esco0ptrrx0
bits.comment: Rx (e)SCO Sample Buffer pointer 0 of Voice Channel 0. Used when eSCOCHANCNTL0-TOG0 = 0

bits.name: retxnb0
bits.comment: Defines the number of transmsission attemtps for SCO/eSCO operations (includes reserved slots and re-Tx slots). Default value is 1

bits.name: escoedrrx0
bits.comment: 1: eSCO EDR Mode (2/3 Mbps) in reception 0: eSCO 1Mbps in reception

bits.name: escoedrtx0
bits.comment: 1: eSCO EDR Mode (2/3 Mbps) in transmission 0: eSCO 1Mbps in transmission

bits.name: syntype0
bits.comment: Synchronous packet type: 0: SCO packet 1: eSCO packet

bits.name: synltaddr0
bits.comment: LT_ADDR of the Synchronous link (eSCO), used for TX.

bits.name: txseqn0
bits.comment: Value of the SEQN bit in eSCO TX packets. Used as follows: - Initialized by SW during eSCO link establishment - Toggled by HW on each TSCO/TeSCO, written back afterwards

bits.name: txlen0
bits.comment: Negotiated, maximum number of bytes for eSCO Tx payloads.

bits.name: txtype0
bits.comment: Negotiated Tx packet type, as defined in [1].

bits.name: rxlen0
bits.comment: Negotiated, maximum number of bytes for eSCO Rx payloads. The reception of the payload is automatically aborted if this buffer size is exceeded.

bits.name: rxtype0
bits.comment: Negotiated Rx packet type, as defined in [1].

bits.name: daycounter0
bits.comment: Day Counter for AES-CCM nonce.

bits.name: linear_format0
bits.comment: Sample Linear format for voice channel 0 00: 8-bit samples 01: 13-bit samples 10: 14-bit samples 11: 16-bit samples

bits.name: sample_type0
bits.comment: PCM / VoHCI Sample Type on Audio Path Channel 0 00: Signed 1s complement 01: Signed 2s complement 10: Signed magnitude 11: Unsigned

bits.name: aulawen0
bits.comment: a/-Law control for voice channel 0 1: Enables a/-Law transcoding 0: Disables a/-Law transcoding / bypass mode

bits.name: aulaw_code0
bits.comment: a/-Law configuration code for voice channel 0. (See Table 2-40)

bits.name: cvsden0
bits.comment: CVSD control for voice channel 0 1: Enables CVSD transcoding 0: Disables CVSD transcoding / bypass mode

bits.name: cvsd_bitorder0
bits.comment: Bit ordering at Byte interface for voice channel 0 0: LSB fist. Compatible to BT spec. 1.1 (ref. to [1]) Over the air, the bits are sent in the same order they are generated by the CVSD encoder. 1: MSB First. Compatible to BT spec. 1.0B (ref. to [1]) The bits are sent in the reverse order (maintains backward compatibility).

bits.name: linear_format1
bits.comment: Sample Linear format for voice channel 1 00: 8-bit samples 01: 13-bit samples 10: 14-bit samples 11: 16-bit samples

bits.name: sample_type1
bits.comment: PCM / VoHCI Sample Type on Audio Path Channel 1 00: Signed 1s complement 01: Signed 2s complement 10: Signed magnitude 11: Unsigned

bits.name: aulawen1
bits.comment: a/-Law control for voice channel 1 1: Enables a/-Law transcoding 0: Disables a/-Law transcoding / bypass mode

bits.name: aulaw_code1

bits.name: cvsden1

Compatible to BT spec. 1.0B (ref. to [1]) The bits are sent in the reverse order (maintains backward compatibility).

bits.name: vxchsel
bits.comment: Voice channel Selection. Select the voice channel to be routed to the PCM 00: Voice Channel 0 routed to PCM 01: Voice Channel 1 routed to PCM 10: Voice Channel 2 routed to PCM 11: Reserved

bits.name: loopback
bits.comment: Loopback Test mode control 1: Loopback Mode enabled 0: Loopback Mode disabled / Normal operations

bits.name: mono_lr_sel
bits.comment: Valid when SAMPTYPE is set to Stereo mode, else not applicable 0: Select Left channel audio samples for Mono operation 1: Select Right channel audio samples for Mono operation

bits.name: mono_stereo
bits.comment: Audio channel Mono/Stereo mode control 0: Audio channel carries Mono samples 1: Audio channel carries Stereo samples

bits.name: mstslv
bits.comment: Master/Slave mode control 0: PCM is master (i.e. PCM generates pcmclk_out and pcmfsync_out from PLL) 1: PCM is slave (i.e. PLL disabled and pcmclk_in and pcmfsync_in are used)

bits.name: byteswap
bits.comment: Byte swapping control, valid only SAMPSZ is set to 16-bits 0: Samples to be sent used as-is 1: MSB and LSB bytes are swapped within samples

bits.name: lrswap
bits.comment: Valid in Stereo mode only, defines the Left / Right channel order 0: Left channel then Right channel 1: Right channel then Left channel

bits.name: pcmen
bits.comment: PCM main control 0: PCM disabled (i.e. pcm_gclk clock not enabled) 1: PCM enabled (i.e. pcm_gclk clock enabled)

bits.name: firstactslot
bits.comment: Configures the first active slot of the frame, in [0:3] range 00: first active slot is slot 0 01: first active slot is slot 1 10: first active slot is slot 2 11: first active slot is slot 3 The maximum value this field can be configured to is determined by the SLOTNB-1 parameters.

bits.name: slotnb
bits.comment: Number of slots within a PCM frame Valid values are in [1:4] range. Other values are meaningless

bits.name: samptype
bits.comment: PCM Codec Sample type 0: PCM codec supports Mono operation 1: PCM codec supports Stereo operation

bits.name: sampsz
bits.comment: PCM codec Sample size 0: PCM Frame carries 8-bit samples 1: PCM Frame carries 16-bit samples

bits.name: lsb1st
bits.comment: Bit ordering within a PCM Frame 0: Sample are sent/received MSB first 1: Samples are sent/received LSB first

bits.name: pcm_iom
bits.comment: PCM / IOM mode selection 0: PCM mode (single clocking) 1: IOM mode (double clocking)

bits.name: lrchpol
bits.comment: Selection of the PCM Frame Synchronization polarity (Valid when SAMPTYPE is set to Stereo mode, else not applicable) 0: Right channel when = 0, Left channel when = 1 1: Right channel when = 1, Left channel when = 0

bits.name: doutcfg
bits.comment: Physical configuration of the pcmd_out pad. 00: Open-drain, hi-Z outside transmission 01: Push-pull, hi-Z outside transmission 10: Push-pull, driven to 0 outside transmission 11: Reserved

bits.name: fsyncshp
bits.comment: Physical shape of the PCM Frame Synchronization signal. 000: LF enclosing the last falling PCM Interface Clock edge in frame (Mono only) 001: FR enclosing the first rising PCM Interface Clock edge in frame (Mono only) 010: FF enclosing the first falling PCM Interface Clock edge in frame (Mono only) 011: LONG enclosing the first slot (8 bits) of the frame (Mono / Stereo 8-bits only) 100: LONG_16 enclosing first two slots (16 bits) of the frame (Mono 16 bits / Stereo 16-bits only) 101: STEREO Left/Right Frame differentiating (Stereo only, covers left or right channel only, polarity is set according to LRCHPOL)

bits.name: clkinv
bits.comment: Selection of the PCM Interface Clock polarity 0: Data is clocked out with the rising edge (standard) 1: Data is clocked out with the falling edge

bits.name: pcmclklimit
bits.comment: PCM Clock counter limit

bits.name: pcmclkval
bits.comment: PCM Clock Counter value.

bits.name: rsamppad
bits.comment: Right channel sample padding / to be used when non 16-bits PCM sample configuration is used. (LSB are used first)

bits.name: lsamppad
bits.comment: Left channel sample padding / to be used when non 16-bits PCM sample configuration is used. (LSB are used first)

bits.name: olc
bits.comment: Open Loop Correction value, see equation below.

bits.comment: PLL control word, see equation below.

bits.name: irq0_cause

bits.name: irq1_mask_set
bits.comment: bit type is changed from rs to r. When read: returns the value of the Irq1_Mask register. When written: value is used as a bit field, each bit at '1' sets the corresponding bit in the Irq1_Mask register, bits at '0' leave the corresponding bit unchanged. The Irq1_Mask masks the set/clear register to trigger interrupts on the XCPU/BCPU using line 0

bits.name: irq0_mask_set
bits.comment: bit type is changed from rs to r. When read: returns the value of the Irq0_Mask register. When written: value is used as a bit field, each bit at '1' sets the corresponding bit in the Irq0_Mask register, bits at '0' leave the corresponding bit unchanged. The Irq0_Mask masks the set/clear register to trigger interrupts on the XCPU/BCPU using line 0

bits.name: irq1_mask_clr
bits.comment: bit type is changed from rc to r. When read: returns the value of the Irq1_Mask register. When written: value is used as a bit field, each bit at '1' clears the corresponding bit in the Irq1_Mask register, bits at '0' leave the corresponding bit unchanged. The Irq1_Mask masks the set/clear register to trigger interrupts on the XCPU/BCPU using line 1

bits.name: irq0_mask_clr
bits.comment: bit type is changed from rc to r. When read: returns the value of the Irq0_Mask register. When written: value is used as a bit field, each bit at '1' clears the corresponding bit in the Irq0_Mask register, bits at '0' leave the corresponding bit unchanged. The Irq0_Mask masks the set/clear register to trigger interrupts on the XCPU/BCPU using line 0

bits.name: irq1_set
bits.comment: bit type is changed from rs to r. When read, returns the value of the set/clear register. When written, value is used as a bit field, each bit at '1' sets the corresponding bit in the set/clear register, bits at '0' leave the corresponding bit unchanged. These bits can also trigger interrupts on the XCPU/BCPU if enabled

bits.name: irq0_set
bits.comment: bit type is changed from rs to r. When read, returns the value of the set/clear register. When written, value is used as a bit field, each bit at '1' sets the corresponding bit in the set/clear register, bits at '0' leave the corresponding bit unchanged. These bits can also trigger interrupts on the XCPU/BCPU if enabled.

bits.name: irq0_clr

bits.name: ch_to_use
bits.comment: This field indicates which standard channel to use. Before using a channel, the CPU read this register to know which channel must be used. After reading this registers, the channel is to be regarded as busy. After reading this register, if the CPU doesn't want to use the specified channel, the CPU must write a disable_ in the control register of the channel to release the channel. 4'h0::use_ch0: use Channel0 4'h1::use_ch1: use Channel1 4'h2::use_ch2: use Channel2 4'h3::use_ch3: use Channel3 4'h4::use_ch4: use Channel4 4'h5::use_ch5: use Channel5 4'h6::use_ch6: use Channel6 4'h7::use_ch7: use Channel7 4'hf::all_busy: all channels are busy

bits.name: ch_busy
bits.comment: This register indicates which standard channel is busy (this field doesn't include the RF_SPI channel). A standard channel is mark as busy, when a channel is eNonebled or a previous reading of the GET_CH register, the field CH_TO_USE indicates this channel. One bit per channel

bits.name: ch_enable
bits.comment: This register indicates which channel is eNonebled. It is a copy of the enable bit of the control register of each channel. One bit per channel, for example:: 8'h00::all_ch_disabled: all channel disabled 8'h01::ch0_enabled: Ch0 enabled 8'h02::ch1_enabled: Ch1 enabled 8'h04::ch2_enabled: Ch2 enabled 8'h05::ch_0_2_enabled: Ch0 and Ch2 enabled 8'h07::ch_0_1_2_enabled: Ch0, Ch1 and Ch2 enabled 8'hff::ch_all_enabled: all channels eNonebled

bits.name: dbg_status
bits.comment: Debug Channel Status . 0:: dbg_ch_run: The debug channel is running (not idle) 1::dbg_ch_idle: The debug channel is in idle mode

bits.name: flush
bits.comment: When one, flush the interNonel FIFO channel. This bit must be used only in case of Rx transfer. Until this bit is 1, the APB request is masked. The flush doesn't release the channel. Before writting back this bit to zero the interNonel fifo must empty.

bits.name: req_src
bits.comment: Select DMA Request source 0:: SYS_ID_TX_UART 1:: SYS_ID_RX_UART 2:: SYS_ID_TX_SDMMC 3:: SYS_ID_RX_SDMMC 4:: SYS_ID_TX_SPI1 5:: SYS_ID_RX_SPI1 6:: SYS_ID_TX_DEBUG_UART 7:: SYS_ID_RX_DEBUG_UART

bits.name: size
bits.comment: Peripheral Size 0::per_size_8: 8-bit peripheral 1::per_size_32: 32-bit peripheral

bits.name: autodisable
bits.comment: Set Auto-disable_ mode 0::auto_disable_close: when TC reach zero the channel is not automatically released. 1::auto_disable_open: At the end of the transfer when TC reach zero the channel is automatically disable_d. the current channel is released.

bits.name: ch_wr_hw_exch
bits.comment: Set Auto-disable_ mode 0:: auto_dis_mode0: when TC reach zero the channel is not automatically released. 1:: auto_dis_mode1: At the end of the transfer when TC reach zero the channel is automatically disable_d. the current channel is released.

bits.comment: bit type is changed from wrc to rc. Channel Disable, write one in this bit disable_ the channel. When writing one in this bit, the current AHB transfer and current APB transfer (if one in progress) is completed and the channel is then disable_d.

bits.name: enable
bits.comment: bit type is changed from wrc to rc. Channel Enable, write one in this bit eNoneble the channel. When the channel is eNonebled, for a peripheral to memory transfer the DMA wait request from peripheral to start transfer.

bits.name: addr_out_base

bits.name: rx_break_length
bits.comment: Length of a break, in number of bits.

bits.name: rx_lock_err
bits.comment: Allow to stop the data receiving when an error is detected (framing, parity or break). The data in the fifo are kept.

bits.name: loop_back_mode
bits.comment: When set, data on the Uart_Tx line is held high, while the serial output is looped back to the serial input line, internally. In this mode all the interrupts are fully functional. This feature is used for diagnostic purposes. Also, in loop back mode, the modem control input Uart_CTS is disconnected and the modem control output Uart_RTS are looped back to the inputs, internally. In IrDA mode, Uart_Tx signal is inverted (see IrDA SIR Mode Support).

bits.name: auto_flow_control
bits.comment: Enables the auto flow control. Uart_RTS is controlled by the Rx RTS bit and the UART Auto Control Flow System. If Uart_CTS become inactive high, the Tx data flow is stopped. 1::ENABLE 0:: DISABLE

bits.name: dma_mode
bits.comment: Enables the DMA signaling for the Uart_Dma_Tx_Req_H and Uart_Dma_Rx_Req_H to the IFC. 0:: DISABLE 1::ENABLE

bits.name: irda_enable
bits.comment: When set, the UART is in IrDA mode and the baud rate divisor used is 16 (see UART Operation for details).

bits.name: divisor_mode
bits.comment: Selects the divisor value used to generate the baud rate frequency (BCLK) from the SCLK (see UART Operation for details). If IrDA is enable, this bit is ignored and the divisor used will be 16. 0 = (BCLK = SCLK / 4) 1 = (BCLK = SCLK / 16) 0:div_4 1:div_16

bits.name: parity_select
bits.comment: Controls the parity format when parity is enabled: 0::odd: an odd number of received 1 bits is checked, or transmitted (the parity bit is included). 1::even: an even number of received 1 bits is checked or transmitted (the parity bit is included). 2::space: space a space is generated and received as parity bit. 3::mark: a mark is generated and received as parity bit.

bits.name: parity_enable
bits.comment: Parity is enabled when this bit is set. 0::NO 1:: YES

bits.name: tx_stop_bits
bits.comment: Stop bits controls the number of stop bits transmitted. Can receive with one stop bit (more inaccuracy can be compensated with two stop bits when divisor mode is set to 0). 0::1_bit :one stop bit is transmitted in the serial data. 1:: 2_bits:two stop bits are generated and transmitted in the serial data out.

bits.name: data_bits
bits.comment: Number of data bits per character (least significant bit first): 0::7_bits 1::8_bits

bits.name: enable
bits.comment: Allows to turn off the UART: 0:: Disable 1::Enable

bits.name: clk_enabled
bits.comment: This bit is set when Uart Clk has been enabled and received by UART after Need Uart Clock becomes active. It serves to avoid enabling RTS too early.

bits.name: dtr
bits.comment: Current value of the DTR line.

bits.name: cts
bits.comment: current value of the Uart_CTS line. 1::Tx_allow_n:Tx not allowed. 0::Tx_alllow:Tx allowed.

bits.name: dcts
bits.comment: This bit is set when the Uart_CTS line changed since the last time this register has been written. This bit is cleared when the UART_STATUS register is written with any value.

bits.name: rx_break_int
bits.comment: This bit is set whenever the serial input is held in a logic 0 state for longer than the length of x bits, where x is the value programmed Rx Break Length. A null word will be written in the Rx Fifo. This bit is cleared when the UART_STATUS register is written with any value.

bits.name: rx_framing_err
bits.comment: This bit is set whenever there is a framing error occured. A framing error occurs when the receiver does not detect a valid STOP bit in the received data. This bit is cleared when the UART_STATUS register is written with any value.

bits.name: rx_parity_err
bits.comment: This bit is set if the parity is enabled and a parity error occurred in the received data. This bit is cleared when the UART_STATUS register is written with any value.

bits.name: tx_overflow_err
bits.comment: This bit indicates that the user tried to write a character when fifo was already full. The written data will not be kept. This bit is cleared when the UART_STATUS register is written with any value.

bits.name: rx_overflow_err
bits.comment: This bit indicates that the receiver received a new character when the fifo was already full. The new character is discarded. This bit is cleared when the UART_STATUS register is written with any value.

bits.name: rx_active
bits.comment: This bit indicates that the UART is receiving a byte.

bits.name: tx_active
bits.comment: This bit indicates that the UART is sending data. If no data is in the fifo, the UART is currently sending the last one through the serial interface.

bits.name: tx_fifo_space
bits.comment: Those bits indicate the number of space available in the Tx Fifo.

bits.name: rx_fifo_level
bits.comment: Those bits indicate the number of data available in the Rx Fifo. Those data can be read.

bits.name: data
bits.comment: The UART_TRANSMIT_HOLDING register is a write-only register that contains data to be transmitted on the serial output port. 16 characters of data may be written to the UART_TRANSMIT_HOLDING register before the FIFO is full. Any attempt to write data when the FIFO is full results in the write data being lost.

bits.name: dtr_fall
bits.comment: Falling edge detected on the UART_DTR signal.

bits.name: dtr_rise
bits.comment: Rising edge detected on the UART_DTR signal.

bits.name: rx_dma_timeout
bits.comment: In DMA mode, there is at least 1 character that has been read in or out the Rx Fifo. Then before received Rx DMA Done, No characters in or out of the Rx Fifo during the last 4 character times.

bits.name: rx_dma_done
bits.comment: Pulse detected on Uart_Dma_Rx_Done_H signal

bits.comment: Tx Overflow, Rx Overflow, Parity Error, Framing Error or Break Interrupt.

bits.name: rx_timeout
bits.comment: No characters in or out of the Rx Fifo during the last 4 character times and there is at least 1 character in it during this time.

bits.name: tx_data_needed
bits.comment: Tx Fifo at or below threshold level (current level <= Tx Fifo trigger level).

bits.name: rx_data_available
bits.comment: Rx Fifo at or upper threshold level (current level >= Rx Fifo trigger level).

bits.name: tx_modem_status
bits.comment: Clear to send signal change detected.

bits.name: dtr_fall
bits.comment: This interrupt is generated when a falling edge is detected on the UART_DTR signal. Reset control: Write one in this register.

bits.name: dtr_rise
bits.comment: This interrupt is generated when a rising edge is detected on the UART_DTR signal. Reset control: Write one in this register.

bits.name: rx_dma_timeout
bits.comment: In DMA mode, there is at least 1 character that has been read in or out the Rx Fifo. Then before received Rx DMA Done, No characters in or out of the Rx Fifo during the last 4 character times.

bits.name: rx_dma_done
bits.comment: This interrupt is generated when a pulse is detected on the Uart_Dma_Rx_Done_H signal. Reset control: Write one in this register.

bits.name: tx_dma_done
bits.comment: This interrupt is generated when a pulse is detected on the Uart_Dma_Tx_Done_H signal. Reset control: Write one in this register.

bits.name: rx_line_err
bits.comment: Tx Overflow, Rx Overflow, Parity Error, Framing Error or Break Interrupt. Reset control: This bit is cleared when the UART_STATUS register is written with any value.

bits.name: rx_timeout
bits.comment: No characters in or out of the Rx Fifo during the last 4 character times and there is at least 1 character in it during this time. Reset control: Reading from the UART_RECEIVE_BUFFER register.

bits.name: tx_data_needed
bits.comment: Tx Fifo at or below threshold level (current level <= Tx Fifo trigger level). Reset control: Writing into UART_TRANSMIT_HOLDING register above threshold level.

bits.name: rx_data_available
bits.comment: Rx Fifo at or upper threshold level (current level >= Rx Fifo trigger level). Reset control: Reading the UART_RECEIVE_BUFFER until the Fifo drops below the trigger level.

bits.name: tx_modem_status
bits.comment: Clear to send signal detected. Reset control: This bit is cleared when the UART_STATUS register is written with any value.

bits.name: afc_level
bits.comment: Controls the Rx Fifo level at which the Uart_RTS Auto Flow Control will be set inactive high (see UART Operation for more details on AFC). The Uart_RTS Auto Flow Control will be set inactive high when quantity of data in Rx Fifo > AFC Level.

bits.name: tx_trigger
bits.comment: Defines the empty threshold level at which the Data Needed Interrupt will be generated. The Data Needed Interrupt is generated when quantity of data in Tx Fifo <= Tx Trigger.

bits.name: rx_trigger
bits.comment: Defines the empty threshold level at which the Data Available Interrupt will be generated. The Data Available interrupt is generated when quantity of data in Rx Fifo > Rx Trigger.

bits.name: tx_fifo_reset
bits.comment: Writing a 1 to this bit resets and flushes the Transmit Fifo. This bit does not need to be cleared.

bits.name: rx_fifo_reset
bits.comment: Writing a 1 to this bit resets and flushes the Receive Fifo. This bit does not need to be cleared.

bits.name: rx_rts
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1s to rs. this bit is set to 1 when writing 1, cleared to 0 when corresponding filed is cleared in UART_CMD_CLR

bits.name: tx_finish_n_wait
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1s to rs. refer to bit [5]

bits.name: tx_break_control
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1s to rs. refer to bit [5]

bits.name: dsr
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1s to rs. refer to bit [5]

bits.name: dcd
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1s to rs. refer to bit [5]

bits.name: ri
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1s to rs. refer to bit [5]

bits.name: rx_cpu_rts
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1c to rc. this bit is cleared to 0 when writing 1, set to 1 when corresponding filed is set in UART_CMD_SET

bits.name: tx_finish_n_wait
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1c to rc. refer to bit [5]

bits.name: tx_break_control
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1c to rc. refer to bit [5]

bits.name: dcr
bits.comment: bit type is changed from w1c to rc. refer to bit [5]

bits.name: ri
